Asked in Jun about May, the system reports a monthly entitlement of $1,060.
Current version of the record: At application in March, no disability designation is in place.
Today the system reports $1,535.50 for May. The payment actually made that month was correct when it was issued, and is now an underpayment of $475.50.
Move either slider. The left one changes the month you ask about. The right one changes the month you ask in. The hard edge across the grid is the July decision reaching back over every earlier month. That is what a backdated decision looks like when the system keeps both axes.
Current State
Two ministries run case management: Children and Family Development, and Social Development and Poverty Reduction. The work covers assistance payments, service requests, social work, loss recovery and client support. All of it depends on a worker seeing the full picture. The work is life-critical. A wrong answer means someone might not eat this month, or a child misses a check-in.
Two systems do the work. One is an Oracle Siebel customer relationship management product, adapted for government. The other is a mainframe built in 1982. They run side by side and share the core programs between them. Every attempt to retire the mainframe has stalled or failed.
The New Design is Built on Three Pillars
Evidence, not 'facts'
The system will not store "this person is an adult." It stores this: on 14 July, AI agent ID-33422 read the uploaded image of identification, matched it to the case, and read the date of birth as 22 April 1988. Business rules then decide the person is an adult. Who or what decided, when, and on what basis all sit in the record. They do not sit in an attached PDF, or outside the system altogether.
Evidence
Apt boundaries
Two ministries with broad mandates carry a very mixed portfolio. The current system forces all of it into one rigid model. That is how a design turns brittle. Here each program family gets its own model.
Domains
A decision you can re-run
Every entitlement decision stores the rules, the engine, the facts it saw, its own reasoning and what it decided. A manager four days later, or a tribunal years later, can re-run it instead of piecing it together from memory.
Determinations
Why do backdates matter?
Much of case management is building one clear timeline as information arrives. It does not arrive in order, and what turns up later can change what earlier events meant. In the backdated designation above, the client spent four months short of what they were owed. Someone on assistance has no savings to absorb that. The same machinery runs the other way too. It lands on the same person, who then has to pay the money back.
When someone is paid too much, the money falls into one of two classes. If the client's circumstances changed and they told the ministry late, it is a recoverable overpayment. The ministry takes it back at $10 a month, out of a payment that was already only just enough. If the ministry held the information all along and did not act on it, that is administrative error, and the client should not carry it.
Telling those two apart means knowing when the ministry knew. That is a transaction-time question. A system that records only when a fact was true cannot answer it. Nor can one that stamps every moved record with the date it moved. Almost the whole overpayment backlog sits in records from before any cutover.
Mispayment is one example of many. Evidence has to back nearly every claim a client makes. That cycle of claim, evidence and proof is the core loop of the whole service.
How this is modelled
Every evidence assertion carries three time dimensions: valid_time (the period in the world for which the fact holds), recorded_at (when this system learned it), and legacy_asserted_at (when the old system asserted it, where the old record still shows that).
The third axis is nullable. It carries a confidence value of DECODED, INFERRED or UNKNOWN. On UNKNOWN, any consumer working out a knowledge-state answer must return INDETERMINATE. It must not quietly substitute the migration timestamp.
None of this can be added later. Events are immutable: you can add a field with a default, but you cannot fill it in afterwards. The axis has to exist before the first production event.
What this site covers
These pages set out the domain model, and the thinking behind the least conventional choices. Each one leads in plain English and keeps the technical statement behind a disclosure.
Read Current State first if you do not know ICM and MIS. The design makes most sense against what it replaces. Parameters lists the twenty-one rules the design has to hold to, each with the check that catches a breach.
DRAFT
A design proposal for the successor to British Columbia's integrated case management systems, covering employment assistance, disability assistance, child care subsidy, employment services and child protection.
Figures on this site are drawn from the architecture document and from 326 service-delivery procedures. Nothing here is a government commitment.

Parameters
The following parameters are the twenty-one proposed rules the design has to follow. Each one is written so a reviewer can point at something and judge whether it complies. Six of the parameters must be built in from the start; they cannot be added once the work has started.
What a parameter is
A parameter is something a system must comply with. A parameter must be check-able; it must be possible to check whether the system complies to it. To make sure that these rules are parameters, every entry below ends in a question you can put to a running system and get a wrong answer to.
The set makes three claims:
Every parameter is necessary: take one away and the design loses something nothing else supplies.
No two overlap: nothing is said twice.
And together they carry what the architecture is trying to do.
Each entry below demonstrates the first two claims. The third rests on an argument against a list of intents, and it is the weakest of the three, because another architect could reasonably draw some of these lines elsewhere.
The set

N07
The calculation uses only what it is given
While the system works out a decision, it doesn’t check the clock, look anything up in a database or call any other service. Everything it needs is handed to it at the start. The decision record is written from the result, and never feeds back into the calculation.
Why it is needed
This is what makes it possible to re-run a decision and get exactly the same answer, in practice and not just in theory. A rules service that fetches its own information ties every decision to systems that must still be running. That is the first thing a tribunal will look at.
How to check it
Give it the same rules, the same version of the engine and the same inputs. Do you get exactly the same result, down to the last character? Does it read the clock, its settings or any other service along the way?
Where it came from
Principle 8, narrowed to the calculation
Cannot be added later
The rules engine has to be sealed off before anyone writes the first rule
Words explained in the glossary
Decision (determination)
Rules engine
Replay
Decision record
Tribunal
Grouped by the part of the design each one covers. Select any parameter to see how to check it. A heavy left edge marks the six you cannot add later. Words with a special meaning are explained in the glossary, and each parameter links to the ones it uses.
Six cannot be added later
You can satisfy most of these late, at a price. Six you cannot. Each one has to be in place before a particular first event. Once that event has happened, the fix is a rebuild rather than a repair.
Before the first rule is written N07
The engine is sealed off from live data. A rule authored against a service it can call has already fixed the shape of every rule after it.
Before the first event is written N12, and the third date in N01
How records are destroyed is decided per class of fact. Events are immutable, so a date can be added with a default but never filled in afterwards.
As the first copy is made N06, N21
Where a copy came from, and what its source bars it from, are written at the moment of copying. Neither can be reconstructed later.
From the first decision N09
The point in the event sequence a decision read from goes into its record. Earlier decisions cannot be tied to a consistent view of the world.
Before the first group of clients moves N14
Moving them back is proven rather than claimed, and what the return trip loses is written down and approved.
The gates in the order delivery reaches them. This says what order the work has to happen in. It does not say which rules matter most.
Do first only what cannot be done later.
Where the twenty-one came from
Every principle in the architecture is accounted for. Seven carried across, with their wording narrowed or widened. Three split, because each held two ideas that could stand apart. One took in a clause from another, and one became more general. So twelve principles turned into fourteen parameters, and seven more joined them.
P1 split N01 · N02
P2 narrowed N08
P3 split N03 · N06
P4 absorbs P3(a) N03
P5 carried N04
P6 extended N11
P7 carried N10
P8 narrowed N07
P9 carried N05
P10 generalised N18
P11 split N12 · N13
P12 carried N14
Added N09 · N15 · N16 · N17 · N19 · N20 · N21
N09 closes a gap the architecture names in its own text. N15 and N16 close two more it had already recorded against itself. The last four came out of the policy manual, which turned out to state rules the architecture had never reached.
Those last four are the interesting ones, because nobody found them by thinking harder about the architecture. They came from reading what the ministry already tells its own staff to do. Policy sets time limits, and missing one changes what a client is owed. It names which entitlements a client can appeal, and to whom. It keeps the person who decides apart from the person who reviews. And it bars certain uses of information the ministry may lawfully hold. The twelve could not express any of that.
A rule nobody can check is not a rule
One parameter is not about the system at all. N18 ranges over the other twenty. It makes each of them name how you catch a breach, and it says that anything you could write as a lint rule or a compatibility check has to be written as one.
It stands on its own rather than folded into the others. File a rule about enforcement among the rules about behaviour, and enforcement stops being anybody's job without anyone deciding that it should.
DRAFT
A design proposal for the successor to British Columbia's integrated case management systems, covering employment assistance, disability assistance, child care subsidy, employment services and child protection.
Figures on this site are drawn from the architecture document and from 326 service-delivery procedures. Nothing here is a government commitment.

title: Business requirements — The Future of Case Management IT
description: The fourteen outcomes the new system must deliver for the ministry, with how success is measured and what delivers each one.

Business requirements
Fourteen outcomes the new system must deliver. Each says why it matters, how success is measured, and which functional and quality requirements deliver it.
Each business requirement names its drivers, the parameters that test it, and the functional and non-functional requirements that deliver it. Success criteria can be measured. Where no baseline exists yet, the criterion says who will set it.
Search requirements
[placeholder] Search by word or ID
[aria-label] Filter by priority
Priority
Must
Showing 14 of 14
Expand all
Collapse all
Business requirements 14
BR-001 Must
Entitlement is decided correctly, as policy states it
Every decision applies the statute and the policy rules in force for the period it covers, as policy states them. Show detail
Description
Every decision applies the statute and the policy rules in force for the period it covers, as policy states them. No worker should have to adjust a result by hand to reach the entitlement policy sets.
Rationale
A benefits system that calculates something other than the stated entitlement pays people wrongly, at scale. Policy states at least one entitlement the current system does not calculate. Today the gap is closed only when a worker notices it and adjusts the amount by hand OBLG-C1. A specification copied from the legacy system would carry that underpayment forward. The rules also have no single current date: the supplement rules alone carry 54 different effective dates OBLG-C3. Being correct means applying the right version of each rule to each period.
Success Criteria
Shadow comparison meets its exit criteria for every class of difference, across three monthly payment cycles in a row, on a group of clients whose cases are as complex as the real caseload. There are zero unresolved defects in the new system before any group of clients moves (FR-095).
Every rule a decision applies is named in its record by rule identifier and version, and every rule in the register carries a policy citation and effective date (FR-090, FR-091).
The entitlements that need manual adjustment today are calculated by the rules with no manual step. Test cases in the rules test suite prove it.
Drivers
DRV-01, DRV-09, DRV-10
Parameters
N01, N04, N07
Delivered by
FR-005, FR-007, FR-010, FR-033, FR-090, FR-091, FR-095
Stakeholder
Assistant Deputy Minister, Policy and Program Design
BR-002 Must
Every decision can be defended years after it is made
Any decision can be reproduced, explained and disclosed for as long as it can be reconsidered, appealed, reviewed or requested under access legislation. Show detail
Description
Any decision can be reproduced, explained and disclosed for as long as it can be reconsidered, appealed, reviewed or requested under access legislation. That means what was decided, on what facts, under which rules, and what the client was told.
Rationale
A tribunal asks what the ministry decided, on what basis, and what the client was told, and it often asks years later. A decision can only be reproduced if the calculation depends on nothing but its inputs, and if those inputs and outputs are stored in full when the decision is made TA-C3. A record that points to a running system is not evidence.
Success Criteria
For a randomly chosen adverse decision, the rule, the fact and where it came from, the reasons as issued, and the deadline to challenge that was stated can all be rebuilt from stored records alone, with no running system and no person involved (TA §C.8.5 test).
The replay horizon, and how decisions older than it will be evidenced, are set out in writing before the first live decision (FR-008).
The appeal record for any decision can be put together, and severed, on demand (FR-058, FR-078).
Drivers
DRV-02, DRV-03, DRV-11 (aim 1)
Parameters
N07, N08, N09
Delivered by
FR-001, FR-002, FR-008, FR-009, FR-058, FR-062
Stakeholder
Chief Architect, with the Reconsideration and Administrative Fairness Unit
BR-003 Must
Clients can always challenge a decision, and are told truthfully how
A client may ask for reconsideration of any communication, at any time, and the request is always recorded. Show detail
Description
A client may ask for reconsideration of any communication, at any time, and the request is always recorded. The client is told accurately whether a decision can be reconsidered or appealed, and where. Statutory deadlines are tracked by the system, and the ministry's own lateness never costs the client.
Rationale
Policy gives an unconditional right to ask for reconsideration. An independent unit decides whether reconsideration is available; the worker who sent the communication does not OBLG-C4. Whether a decision can be challenged differs by entitlement and by variant, and cannot be worked out from the parent program PRIN-C2. A missed statutory deadline changes what the client is owed PRIN-C1.
Success Criteria
No reconsideration request is refused at the point of contact on any channel, and every one is recorded with the date and channel it arrived on (FR-055).
Every entitlement and variant records its statutory basis, whether it can be reconsidered, whether it can be appealed, and to which body. The rights text in every notice is generated from those values (FR-092, FR-063).
Every breach of a statutory deadline is detected and recorded automatically, and its effect on entitlement is applied without anyone asking (FR-061).
Drivers
DRV-02, DRV-09
Parameters
N19, N20, N17
Delivered by
FR-006, FR-055, FR-056, FR-057, FR-061, FR-063, FR-092
Stakeholder
Reconsideration and Administrative Fairness Unit
BR-004 Must
Public money moves only under control, and people are paid even when the system fails
Every payment passes through one defined issuance point. Show detail
Description
Every payment passes through one defined issuance point. Separation of duties is enforced in the software. Payment runs never pay twice and can resume after a failure. Payments are reconciled daily against the corporate financial system in a three-way check. A planned, rehearsed emergency payment route exists before the first payment.
Rationale
A benefits system that calculates correctly but does not pay has failed completely. A single issuance point that is described but never specified cannot be built. If each program family builds its own link to the payment system, the controls exist once per program and are audited once per program TA-C4. Rolling back to the old system does not keep payments flowing: a client's rent is due on a date TA-C5.
Success Criteria
The five acceptance criteria for the issuance point in TA §C.6.8 pass before the first live payment (FR-042).
No payment is made outside a run, and there are no unexplained reconciliation breaks at month-end (FR-043, FR-045).
Emergency payment is exercised, at a load-tested share of a program's caseload, before M6 ends (FR-047).
Drivers
DRV-07, DRV-10, DRV-11 (aims 13, 14)
Parameters
N17, N16 [PROPOSED]
Delivered by
FR-042 to FR-048
Stakeholder
Executive Financial Officer
BR-005 Must
Debt is raised fairly, and can be reversed in bulk
An overpayment is calculated as the difference between two decision records. Show detail
Description
An overpayment is calculated as the difference between two decision records. It is classified by what changed in the evidence, and raised only after a person decides it. Automatic raising is capped per cycle. Overpayments that share one cause are reviewed together as a group. A batch of overpayments can be reversed in one step, and any money already recovered is returned automatically.
Rationale
Another jurisdiction ran a debt-raising program that was found unlawful. It raised debts automatically from averaged income data and made recipients prove they did not owe. The controls against that failure are cheap to build only before any debts exist TA-C6. Whether a debt can be recovered depends on what the ministry knew and when, and only the evidence record captures that.
Success Criteria
No overpayment is raised without a recorded human decision-maker for each component (FR-052).
Every overpayment component is classified from the type of evidence change and the party at fault that caused it (FR-051).
A raised batch can be reversed in one step, with recovery reversed and corrected notices issued. This is shown in testing before the first live decision (FR-052).
Drivers
DRV-01, DRV-02, DRV-07
Parameters
N01, N06, N17
Delivered by
FR-012, FR-048, FR-051, FR-052, FR-053, FR-060
Stakeholder
Executive Financial Officer, with the Overpayment and Recovery business owner
BR-006 Must
Information is collected, used and disclosed lawfully by design
The system collects only what it needs. Show detail
Description
The system collects only what it needs. It discloses only where a legal basis is recorded. It enforces limits on how information may be used, wherever the information goes. It severs records before release, handles correction requests across every place the information is held, and can answer "whose information was accessed, by whom, and when" with a query.
Rationale
The original design had no part responsible for how the ministry manages the information it holds. About 15% of obligations had no part of the system to own them MAP-C1, and every unowned intake obligation was about managing information NOTE3-C1. Policy bars information the ministry holds lawfully from particular uses, in five different ways PRIN-C3. Severing works phrase by phrase inside free-text notes OBLG-C5.
Success Criteria
Every disclosure record names the recipient, the legal basis and the agreement. No access decision is made from any source other than the agreement registry (FR-077, FR-085).
Every barred use is blocked by default at the point of use, and each blocked attempt is recorded as an event (FR-080).
The people affected by a privacy breach can be listed by a query (NFR-C-001).
Drivers
DRV-03, DRV-08
Parameters
N06, N13, N21
Delivered by
FR-075 to FR-083, FR-085
Stakeholder
Ministry Privacy Officer
BR-007 Must
Records can be disposed of lawfully in a store that never overwrites
Before the first live event is written, the ministry decides for each kind of fact how long it is kept and how it is disposed of. Show detail
Description
Before the first live event is written, the ministry decides for each kind of fact how long it is kept and how it is disposed of. That includes the disposal method, the published list of what survives disposal, who holds the encryption keys, and what happens when a replay reaches a disposed fact. The ministry can then meet its disposal duties without destroying its financial and control records.
Rationale
A store that only ever adds records conflicts with a legal duty to destroy them. Settling that conflict after the first event means rebuilding the store. The authority for disposal comes from the Information Management Act and the ARCS/ORCS schedules, not from the policy manual OBLG-C2.
Success Criteria
Every kind of fact has a disposal method before the first live event (DR-004).
After a test disposal, financial control totals still reconcile to the same values as before (NFR-C-003).
Drivers
DRV-04, DRV-03
Parameters
N12, N08
Delivered by
DR-004, NFR-C-003, FR-072
Stakeholder
Ministry Records Officer
BR-008 Must
Indigenous jurisdiction and custodianship are recorded accurately
The system records who is custodian of each fact for each person. Show detail
Description
The system records who is custodian of each fact for each person. It treats Indigenous governing bodies as their own class of participant outside the Crown, with their own legal bases. It supports transferring records to another sovereign government as a way of disposing of them. And it recognises designations made by another jurisdiction, while showing how current that recognition is.
Rationale
The Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act commits the Province to bringing its laws into line with the UN Declaration. A Nation's authority over its own data cannot be expressed as a retention rule or an access list. The participant class and the custodianship attribute have to be built in from the start, because they cannot be added once the registry and evidence types exist TA-C7.
Success Criteria
The system can read the custodian of every evidence type for every person, and every access decision traces to the agreement registry alone (FR-084, FR-085).
A transfer package can be produced, and the receiving body can check it without using ministry systems (FR-084).
Drivers
DRV-06
Parameters
N13
Delivered by
FR-021, FR-084, FR-085, DR-005, INT-012
Stakeholder
Ministry Indigenous relations function, with the Ministry Privacy Officer
BR-009 Must
Everyone can reach the service, whatever their ability or channel
A person gets the same result whatever their disability and whichever channel they use, with the same legal effect and the same deadlines. Show detail
Description
A person gets the same result whatever their disability and whichever channel they use, with the same legal effect and the same deadlines. No right, notice or deadline to challenge is available only online. Screens meet WCAG 2.2 AA at first release, confirmed by testing with assistive technology.
Rationale
The clients least able to use a portal make up a large share of this caseload TA-C8. A system that is correct but unreachable fails without showing up in usage figures. The duty to accommodate is set in law (OB-IN-29).
Success Criteria
For each part of the system, outcomes are measured across channels and reported at every gate (FR-086).
Evidence of accessibility, including results of manual testing with assistive technology, exists for every new screen before its gate (NFR-U-002).
Drivers
DRV-05, DRV-10
Parameters
N15
Delivered by
FR-065, FR-066, FR-083, FR-086 to FR-088, NFR-U-002
Stakeholder
Head of Service Delivery Operations, with the Chief Digital Officer
BR-010 Must
Policy changes are fast, safe and dated
Policy staff can write, test and release a rule or rate change without a software release. Show detail
Description
Policy staff can write, test and release a rule or rate change without a software release. Each change is versioned and takes effect on its own date, after review and legal sign-off. Older versions of each rule can still run, for replaying past decisions and for transition rules that run alongside current ones.
Rationale
The rules change all the time, and every decision draws on rules from several different dates RULES-C2. Taking rate changes off the software release schedule is the main financial case for the rules platform. That case rests on an untested assumption: that policy analysts can write rules on it TA-C9.
Success Criteria
Two policy analysts, without help, write, test and release one real rate change from start to finish in a test environment, with the time taken and any help needed recorded (FR-090).
Every rule carries a policy citation and effective date. No rule is released while its effective dates in policy still conflict (FR-091).
Drivers
DRV-09, DRV-10
Parameters
N01, N04, N07
Delivered by
FR-010, FR-090, FR-091, FR-094
Stakeholder
Assistant Deputy Minister, Policy and Program Design
BR-011 Must
The legacy systems are replaced step by step, reversibly, and completely
Work moves from the legacy systems to the new system one part and one group of clients at a time. Show detail
Description
Work moves from the legacy systems to the new system one part and one group of clients at a time. Only one system can change a record at any moment. A published statement says what moving back would lose. The published interface outlives the legacy system behind it. Each legacy capability is shut down as its replacement goes live.
Rationale
The vendor supports the legacy platform past 2037, so no outside deadline forces the replacement to finish TA-C10. The previous programme replaced about a third of the legacy systems and left the most important one running. Responsibility for records moves one part of the system at a time, never one field at a time TA-C11.
Success Criteria
Every part of the system that moves meets the definition of done in TA §E.10, including retiring the legacy function and closing its interfaces.
Moving back is rehearsed for every group of clients before they move, and the list of what would be lost is published and accepted (DR-015).
Removing the legacy product changes nothing in any published interface (NFR-I-001).
Drivers
DRV-11 (aims 3, 6, 7, 11)
Parameters
N05, N10, N14
Delivered by
DR-010 to DR-016, NFR-I-001, FR-095, INT-023
Stakeholder
Chief Architect
BR-012 Must
Workers can do their jobs at least as well as today, and safely
In each part of the system, the ten most common tasks take no longer, and need no more screens or switches between systems, than today. Show detail
Description
In each part of the system, the ten most common tasks take no longer, and need no more screens or switches between systems, than today. Supervisors can see caseloads across programs. Client and staff safety concerns are recorded and acted on.
Rationale
Problems for workers, not missing features, sank the child protection phases of the previous programme. A move to the new system that makes a common task slower is a defect TA-C12. Staff safety is part of the nature of the work.
Success Criteria
Baselines are captured before each part of the system is built. In acceptance testing with real workers on realistic data, task times are at or below the baseline (NFR-U-001).
Safety concerns are recorded and routed, with restricted handling applied, on every channel (FR-089).
Drivers
DRV-10
Parameters
N15, N17
Delivered by
FR-032, FR-067 to FR-070, FR-089, NFR-U-001
Stakeholder
Head of Service Delivery Operations
BR-013 Must
A system failure never harms a client
Every service has an availability target, a recovery time and a recovery point, set by what its failure would do to clients and proven in exercises. Show detail
Description
Every service has an availability target, a recovery time and a recovery point, set by what its failure would do to clients and proven in exercises. Anything that affects an entitlement or a payment must lose no data at all. Every dependency has a stated way of working when it fails.
Rationale
A lost payment instruction is a person without money TA-C13. N16, the parameter that covers this, is still [PROPOSED], because none of the 270 policy obligations calls for it PRIN-C4. Its authority lies outside the policy manual; its need is not in doubt.
Success Criteria
The C.15.1 capacity table has every cell filled, with an owner for each figure, at design freeze (NFR-P-001).
Recovery targets are proven in exercises for every tier-1 component, and disaster recovery exercises run twice a year (NFR-A-002, NFR-A-006).
Drivers
DRV-07, DRV-10, DRV-11 (aim 13)
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED]
Delivered by
NFR-A-001 to NFR-A-007, FR-047
Stakeholder
Ministry Chief Information Officer, with the Head of Service Delivery Operations
BR-014 Must
Each program family is specified from its own law and policy before it moves
For child care subsidy, employment services and child protection, the obligations are extracted from each program's own legislation and policy, by the same method used for the BCEA register, before that program's module is scoped. Show detail
Description
For child care subsidy, employment services and child protection, the obligations are extracted from each program's own legislation and policy, by the same method used for the BCEA register, before that program's module is scoped.
Rationale
The detailed requirements here rest on the BCEA policy manual. The architecture covers more than that. The first set of rules it plans to move is child care subsidy (M5), and no obligation register exists yet for that program. Specifying a program from the platform down, without its own authority, is the mistake the method was built to prevent METH-C2.
Success Criteria
Each program family has an obligation register, a rules register and a register of which decisions can be challenged, all with policy citations, before its module starts.
Every platform-level requirement in this document is re-checked against each new family's obligations, and gaps are raised as amendments.
Drivers
DRV-01, DRV-08, DRV-09
Parameters
N18
Delivered by
later versions of this document; FR-090, FR-092
Stakeholder
Chief Architect, with the program policy authority for each family
DRAFT
A design proposal for the successor to British Columbia's integrated case management systems, covering employment assistance, disability assistance, child care subsidy, employment services and child protection.

title: Data requirements — The Future of Case Management IT
description: The nineteen data requirements, the ten principal information objects, and the data quality rules for the system that replaces ICM and MIS.

Data
How the system records facts, keeps them, destroys them on schedule, and moves them from the legacy systems without losing what the ministry knew and when.
Search requirements
[placeholder] Search by word or ID
[aria-label] Filter by priority
Priority
Must
Should
Showing 19 of 19

[aria-label] Categories on this page
How facts are recorded and kept 9
Moving data from the legacy systems 7
Using data and identity 3
How facts are recorded and kept 9
DR-001 Must
Every fact carries three dates, fixed before the first event
Every fact records when it was true (valid period) and when this system learned it (transaction time). Show detail
Requirement
Every fact records when it was true (valid period) and when this system learned it (transaction time). Facts from the old systems also record legacy_asserted_at, the date the old system recorded them, with a rating of how confidently that date could be decoded. This structure is fixed before the first production event is written.
Acceptance Criteria
A sample across fact classes, including facts from the old systems, shows for each fact its valid period, its recorded time and its old-system date (or an explicit UNKNOWN), and points to its source record.
Parameters
N01
Rationale
The third date cannot be added later under the rule that new record formats must stay readable alongside all earlier ones (decision D10). Without it, corrections and supersessions made before cutover cannot be told apart PRIN-C10.
DR-002 Must
Fact states and lifecycle
The data model represents four fact states: Show detail
Requirement
The data model represents four fact states: present, asserted negative, considered but not retainable, and disposed. It also represents four lifecycle states: asserted, active, superseded and invalidated. An outside body, such as the tribunal, can invalidate a fact without a replacement determination.
Acceptance Criteria
Each state can be recorded and told apart at every point where data is captured and in every view built from it.
Parameters
N01, N08
Rationale
A rescission cancels a decision without replacing it, and only an asserted negative can support a determination (PRIN N01, N08).
DR-003 Must
Security classification and storage placement for each fact class
Every fact class carries its security classification and is stored where that classification allows. Show detail
Requirement
Every fact class carries its security classification and is stored where that classification allows. So does everything derived from it, including indexes, extracted text, thumbnails, caches and shadow comparison results (NFR-C-004).
Acceptance Criteria
An inventory of where data is stored shows no Protected C data at rest outside the permitted stores.
Parameters
N12, N13
Rationale
A search index built over Protected C content is itself Protected C (TA §C.11.6).
DR-004 Must
Retention class and disposal method for each fact class
Before the first production event, each fact class is given exactly one disposal method: Show detail
Requirement
Before the first production event, each fact class is given exactly one disposal method:
class-wide disposal on a schedule;
keeping personal details in a separate store that can be deleted (reference-based indirection);
destroying one person's encryption key (per-subject cryptographic erasure);
permanent retention and transfer to the archives.
The shred-survivor list is published as a closed, versioned list. When a replay reaches a disposed fact, it returns a typed placeholder (a tombstone), never an error or a silent gap. Each disposal produces a signed certificate.
Acceptance Criteria
Every registered fact class has a method. A disposal run in test leaves the tamper-evident record chain verifiable and the financial control totals unchanged. The survivor list covers record header fields, the existence and outcome class of each determination, financial and recovery control facts, access-decision records, disclosure records and disposal certificates.
Parameters
N12, N08
Rationale
This cannot be added after the first event. The authority for it is the ARCS/ORCS records schedules, which the ministry must obtain first (decision D13; DEP-09).
DR-005 Must
Custodianship on every evidence type
Every evidence type records its custodian, governance regime, access conditions and transfer status. Show detail
Requirement
Every evidence type records its custodian, governance regime, access conditions and transfer status. These are worked out for each person at the moment of access.
Acceptance Criteria
For any evidence type and person, the custodian is a value the system reads, and the access policy checks it.
Parameters
N13
Rationale
A fixed value that cannot vary by person is what adding this later would produce (TA §B.8.2).
DR-006 Must
Limits on use recorded on facts
Facts record barred_from and permitted_for for each use. Show detail
Requirement
Facts record barred_from and permitted_for for each use. These limits exist from the moment the fact is first captured, and they travel with every copy.
Acceptance Criteria
A fact barred for one use and allowed for another is stored once. A copy test confirms the limit is still present on the copy.
Parameters
N21
Rationale
A limit missing at capture is missing from every copy made before it was added (PRIN §V).
DR-007 Must
Every copy records its source, and every copy can be found
When one part of the system copies evidence from another, it records the source at the moment of copying. Show detail
Requirement
When one part of the system copies evidence from another, it records the source at the moment of copying. For any fact, the system can list every part holding a copy. A correction at the source requires each of them to act, and a correction that goes unprocessed raises an alarm.
Acceptance Criteria
A correction test at the source lists every copy and records what each part did. An unprocessed correction raises an alarm.
Parameters
N06
Rationale
Copying data without being able to find the copies spreads it with no record of where it went (PRIN N06). Policy says nothing about passing corrections to parties already given the information, so this requirement rests on the architecture (OBLG §6).
DR-008 Must
Policy and rate history captured when first loaded
From the first day, every rule is captured with its policy citation and the effective date shown on its own block of text. Show detail
Requirement
From the first day, every rule is captured with its policy citation and the effective date shown on its own block of text. The archived rate tables are copied in once, not relied on where they sit. Older versions of policy text held by the ministry are kept under records retention for at least the replay horizon.
Acceptance Criteria
Every register row has its citation and effective date. The copied archive is kept under the programme's own retention.
Parameters
N01, N08
Rationale
The published archive has no retention statement and has gaps. Nothing can recover what was never published NOTE2-C1.
DR-009 Must
Data quality at the point of capture
Mandatory questions cannot be left blank, and "no" answers are captured as asserted negatives. Show detail
Requirement
Mandatory questions cannot be left blank, and "no" answers are captured as asserted negatives. Every correction must say who caused the error. Values a machine reads from documents stay unverified until someone verifies them. Every migrated fact carries its confidence rating.
Acceptance Criteria
Validation rejects blank mandatory questions and corrections that do not say who caused the error.
Parameters
N01, N18
Rationale
Gaps in these fields cannot be fixed afterwards, because the information was never captured.
Moving data from the legacy systems 7
Migration Scope: History that affects entitlement, current case state, case notes and practice history, and financial history held in ICM, MIS and the stores around them. The old audit trail is included because it is the evidence for when the old system recorded each fact.
Migration Strategy: Phased, by part of the system and by group of clients, with a shadow period before each group moves. Groups move in this order: new applicants; clients in one program with no active protection involvement; clients in several programs; and last, clients with active protection concerns or court involvement. No client is moved in the middle of a determination or an appeal.
Data Transformation: A mixed approach chosen per fact class (DR-010). Migration events use the old system's terms. Business events that claim to record what someone intended are never invented.
Data Validation: Record counts, financial control totals, checks that links between records hold, sample checks by program staff, a pilot on converted data, and the date-accuracy gate (DR-012).
Rollback Plan: Per group of clients, rehearsed, with the published list of what would be lost accepted in writing by the program policy authority (DR-015).
Migration Timeline: Per capture module (M2 onwards). Profiling the old data and the trial of decoding old-system dates both happen before design freeze.
DR-010 Must
A mixed migration approach, chosen per fact class
Facts that affect entitlement (income, assets, household, dependants, shelter, designation, enrolment periods, earlier determinations, overpayment balances) are loaded with both valid time and transaction time, marked as coming from the old systems (provenance Show detail
Requirement
Facts that affect entitlement (income, assets, household, dependants, shelter, designation, enrolment periods, earlier determinations, overpayment balances) are loaded with both valid time and transaction time, marked as coming from the old systems (provenance LEGACY). The case shell and current operational state migrate as current state only. Case notes and practice history are archived and made available through an adapter that marks them as coming from the old systems. Everything else is loaded through named migration events such as LegacyClientWasImported.
Acceptance Criteria
Every fact class appears in the migration register with its approach. No invented business events exist.
Parameters
N01, N06
Rationale
Each fact class has its own right answer, and using one approach for everything is an error (decision D10).
DR-011 Must
Migration records its source, can be re-run, and can be reversed per group
Every migrated fact records its source system, source record identifier, migration batch identifier, migration time and a confidence rating. Show detail
Requirement
Every migrated fact records its source system, source record identifier, migration batch identifier, migration time and a confidence rating. Migration can be re-run without creating duplicates, keyed on the source record identifier, and can be reversed for each group of clients TA-C43.
Acceptance Criteria
Running a migration batch twice creates no duplicates. In test, a group of clients can be un-migrated and migrated again.
Parameters
N01, N14
Rationale
Migration is a product with its own quality gates, not a one-off task.
DR-012 Must
Migration quality gates, including date accuracy
Migration gates check record counts, control totals, links between records, samples checked by people, and a pilot on converted data. Show detail
Requirement
Migration gates check record counts, control totals, links between records, samples checked by people, and a pilot on converted data. They also set two date-accuracy minimums for each fact class: the percentage of facts with a known valid period, and the percentage with a recoverable old-system date. Both minimums are agreed before migration begins.
Acceptance Criteria
No group of clients passes a gate whose minimums were set after the data was measured.
Parameters
N01, N18
Rationale
The standard gates cannot detect that the "when did we learn it" dates have all collapsed to the import date. The comparator ran no pilot on converted data and produced about 114,000 errors in converted client data (TA §C.2.8).
DR-013 Must
Unknown old-system dates are visible, and default in the client's favour
When a replay reaches a fact whose old-system date is UNKNOWN, it treats the fact as recorded at migration and marks the determination TEMPORALLY_UNVERIFIED. Show detail
Requirement
When a replay reaches a fact whose old-system date is UNKNOWN, it treats the fact as recorded at migration and marks the determination TEMPORALLY_UNVERIFIED. This marker is carried onto notices and appeal packages. An overpayment component that depends on such a fact defaults to administrative error and is not recovered, unless a person reclassifies it on recorded evidence. Before design freeze, the old audit trail is profiled across the most important fact classes, with at least 10,000 records for each.
Acceptance Criteria
Profiling results are published for each class. A TEMPORALLY_UNVERIFIED determination cannot, on its own, show what the ministry knew at a past date.
Parameters
N01, N08
Rationale
If the ministry cannot show when it knew something, it cannot meet the burden of proof a tribunal places on it TA-C19.
DR-014 Must
Running old and new systems side by side, and writing back to the old system
Responsibility for a record moves from the old system to the new one per part of the system and per group of clients, never one field at a time. Show detail
Requirement
Responsibility for a record moves from the old system to the new one per part of the system and per group of clients, never one field at a time. When the new system writes changes back to the old one for groups it has taken over, the write-back:
uses only insert and update operations. It never uses a synchronize operation on an object with child records, unless a check before writing confirms the data is complete;
is kept out of the new system's outgoing event queue, so it cannot loop back;
is removed from both sides of every reconciliation and shadow comparison;
keeps the old system's validation, or records a decision for each case where validation is bypassed;
runs one way only for records the new system has taken over;
follows a published mapping, per fact class, that lists every field with nowhere to go in the old system.
Acceptance Criteria
A deliberately incomplete write is refused. A loop test shows no echoed events. The list of what would be lost is published before the new system takes over writing for a group (state S2).
Parameters
N05, N14
Rationale
Writing back to the old system is the most dangerous write path in the old and new systems combined (TA §C.2.6).
DR-015 Must
Rollback rehearsed, with its losses published
Every group of clients moved to the new system can be moved back to the old one without a separate data project. Show detail
Requirement
Every group of clients moved to the new system can be moved back to the old one without a separate data project. The published list of losses names every fact class that would not survive the move back, and the difference between a correction and a supersession is always on it. Rollback is rehearsed before any group moves.
Acceptance Criteria
The rollback rehearsal record and the accepted list of losses are present at the capture gate.
Parameters
N14
Rationale
A rollback plan that does not say what is lost has not been tested (PRIN N14).
DR-016 Must
Retiring the old systems and disposing of their data
Each old system is retired as its replacement goes live. Show detail
Requirement
Each old system is retired as its replacement goes live. Each record class receives one of five outcomes: moved, archived for a period, transferred to the archives, permanently and ethically deleted, or transferred to another government (an Indigenous governing body or other sovereign). The oldest core systems and the old audit trail are kept in a complete archive with controlled access. People who use a core old system, staff and oversight bodies get at least twelve months' notice before it is shut down. Disposal decisions are in place before the new system takes over writing for each part (state S2).
Acceptance Criteria
Old interfaces are closed, with evidence, and counted against the full list of interfaces from Module 0.
Parameters
N12, N13, N14
Rationale
Systems cannot be retired by deleting them, and retention duties run for decades beyond the programme (TA §C.2.9).
Using data and identity 3
DR-017 Should
Analysis without making copies
People and systems analysing data get what they are entitled to, at the level of detail they are entitled to, from one governed store, without a new copy being made. Show detail
Requirement
People and systems analysing data get what they are entitled to, at the level of detail they are entitled to, from one governed store, without a new copy being made. Only de-identified, aggregated, synthetic or differentially private versions leave the trusted environment.
Acceptance Criteria
The list of data consumers shows no new extracts. Every dataset in public cloud is a registered de-identified or aggregated version.
Parameters
N02, N12
Rationale
Endless copying of production data is the defining data failure of the current systems (commitment 4; decision D6). A data warehouse that already exists, built on shared reporting dimensions, means this is a migration from what exists (APP §9).
DR-018 Should
Mapping the old work categories to the new ones
Migrated work items and historical reporting are mapped from the old service request types and sub-types (about 30 types and 128 sub-types) to the new work item types through a published mapping. Show detail
Requirement
Migrated work items and historical reporting are mapped from the old service request types and sub-types (about 30 types and 128 sub-types) to the new work item types through a published mapping. The new types come from the ministry's service catalogue and obligations, not from the old categories.
Acceptance Criteria
Every old type and sub-type maps to a new type or to a recorded retirement.
Parameters
N10
Rationale
Reports need to stay comparable across the cutover (GAPS P-02). Carrying the old categories forward as the design would tie the new model to the old system's vocabulary (N10).
DR-019 Must
Identity data is read when needed, not stored
The system reads identity details from provincial identity services when it needs them and does not keep them longer than they stay valid. Show detail
Requirement
The system reads identity details from provincial identity services when it needs them and does not keep them longer than they stay valid. The client index holds only identifiers and the personal details needed to match people, and does not become a second directory.
Acceptance Criteria
An inventory of stored data shows no login credential or identity-service detail kept beyond its validity.
Parameters
N03, N11
Rationale
Participant Identity holds only identifiers and matching details (TA §B.6.1).
The main information objects
Each object belongs to one part of the system. They are not a shared model that every part must use; each part keeps its own view of what it needs.
1 Evidence assertion
Description: A dated claim about the world, with a record of where it came from. Every decision is worked out from these claims. Owned by Evidence and Verification.

Data Volume: Not measured. The only indicators are the Release 26.7 volumes (NFR-P-001) and the record counts expected at cutover (NFR-S-003).

Data Classification: Protected B by default, and Protected C for classes that are classified that way. Data from the old systems is treated as Protected C until it is reclassified.
Data Retention: Set per fact class under the approved records schedules (DR-004). The ministry has not yet obtained these schedules.

7 Consent instrument
Description: A consent, with its scope, period, legal authority and lifecycle. Owned by Consent and Disclosure.
Attributes: instrument type; subject; the person giving consent and anyone acting for them; scope (sources, purposes, parties); valid period; lifecycle state (granted, expired, revoked); how it can be revoked; evidence of signature or the verbal record.
Data Classification: Protected B.
8 Data-sharing agreement
Description: A machine-readable agreement that is the only source of authority for every data exchange and access right. Held in the agreement registry.
Attributes: agreement identifier; participants by class (provincial, federal, Indigenous governing body, contracted provider); permitted services; authorities relied on; purpose; retention and onward-disclosure terms; expiry and review dates; accountable executives; lifecycle state; unchangeable change history.
Data Classification: Protected A.
9 Work item
Description: A unit of work that points to the record it concerns in the part of the system that owns it. Owned by Work Management.
Attributes: work item type (registered); subject reference; owning part of the system; state; priority; due date and where it comes from (a legal clock or a service standard); assignment history with reasons; supervisors watching after escalation.
Constraints: Program-specific fields are not allowed.
Data Classification: Protected B.
10 Issued notice
Description: What the client was actually sent. Owned by Notices and Correspondence.
Attributes: notice identifier; determination reference; template version fingerprint; language; format; the rendered document; delivery events (issued, delivered, deemed received, proven served); notification date.
Data Classification: Same as the determination it explains.
Data Retention: Same as the decision it explains. The rendered document is kept for every notice that conveys a decision.
Data quality
Data Accuracy: Shadow comparison proves correctness separately for each type of difference (FR-095). A single overall match rate does not count. Two wrong amounts that cancel each other out to a zero total count as a defect.
Data Completeness: Mandatory questions are answered or recorded as asserted negatives (DR-009). Determination records carry every required field (FR-001). Migrated facts that affect entitlement meet minimum rates, agreed in advance, for having a known valid period and a recoverable old-system date (DR-012).
Data Consistency: Only one system can change each record for each group of clients (N05). Reference data has one master copy, published as events (FR-094). Money is reconciled three ways every day (FR-045). Read-only views are compared with the old system every day, with rows written back by the new system removed from both sides first (DR-014).
Data Timeliness: The system refuses a determination when its facts are older than the consistency limit allows (FR-009). Delays in processing published events have limits and raise alarms (NFR-P-005).
Data Lineage: Every fact records where it came from, including the extraction tool version and confidence where a machine read it. Every copy records its source (DR-007). Every migrated fact records its source system, source record, migration batch, migration time and confidence (DR-011).
DRAFT
A design proposal for the successor to British Columbia's integrated case management systems, covering employment assistance, disability assistance, child care subsidy, employment services and child protection.
Figures on this site are drawn from the architecture document and from 326 service-delivery procedures. Nothing here is a government commitment.

Functional requirements
What the system must do, in sixteen groups that follow a client's matter through the ministry. Each requirement lists the policy obligations it meets and the checks that prove it.
Functional requirements are grouped by capability, in the order a client's matter moves through the ministry. Each one lists the policy obligations it meets (Obligations) and the architecture parameters that test it (Parameters). Where a requirement has no obligation, its authority is the architecture section named in its rationale. Appendix E and the companion file ARC-001-REQ-v1.0-traceability.csv map all 270 obligations to requirements.
Module names the delivery module in which the requirement must first be met (target architecture §A.8). Requirements assigned to M0 are foundations. Several of them cannot be added later, once the first event, copy, rule or cohort exists (PRIN §V) PRIN-C5.
