A Decisions and the decision record 10
FR-001 Must M0 High
Decision types and what the decision record holds
The system records every decision as one of three types: Show detail
First needed in: M0 (schema), M5 (first rule surface)
Description
The system records every decision as one of three types: grant; deny; or reduce or discontinue. Each is a determination in its own right. Its record states the criteria met and not met, the statutory provisions applied, the assumptions made, the evidence lacking, any decision-support report used, and every item of information considered.
Relates To
BR-002, UC-1, UC-2
Obligations
OB-D01, OB-D03, OB-D04, OB-D05, OB-D06, OB-D07, OB-D09, OB-D11
Parameters
N01, N07, N08, N20
Acceptance Criteria
Given any issued determination, when its record is read, then it holds its type, criteria met, criteria not met, provisions applied, assumptions made and evidence lacking as separate fields, none of which can only be recovered by re-running the rules.
Given a determination informed by a decision-support report, when the record is read, then a full copy of the report is stored with it.
Given a request to disclose the information considered, when the record is queried, then every item considered can be listed from the record alone.
Data
Inputs: evidence snapshot, rules artefact, decision-maker input; Outputs: determination record; Validations: the assumptions and evidence-lacking fields cannot be empty (an explicit "none" counts as an answer).
Dependencies
FR-008, FR-011
Rationale
Policy sets out what the record must contain. That includes negative facts, the assumptions made and the evidence lacking, which cannot be rebuilt after the decision (PRIN N08 amendment (a)).
FR-002 Must M5 Medium
Reasons that name the rule applied and the fact behind it
Every decision carries real reasons, generated from the decision trace: Show detail
First needed in: M5
Description
Every decision carries real reasons, generated from the decision trace: the specific rule, the specific fact, its source and the period it covers. Each rule has its own reasons text, written with the rule and released with it.
Relates To
BR-002, BR-003, UC-1
Obligations
OB-D02
Parameters
N07, N08, N18
Acceptance Criteria
Given an adverse determination chosen at random, when its notice is inspected, then each adverse element names the rule identifier, the fact relied on, where that fact came from, and its period.
Given a rules artefact release, when any rule that produces an adverse outcome lacks approved reasons text, then the release fails.
Edge case: a category code or a generic "you do not meet the criteria" paragraph is not accepted as reasons.
Data
Inputs: decision trace; reasons text keyed by rule identifier; Outputs: reasons text bound into the notice; Validations: every adverse rule that fired has reasons text.
Dependencies
FR-062, FR-090
Rationale
A person cannot challenge reasons they cannot trace to a rule and a fact. Untraceable reasons were a defining feature of the automated-debt failure the architecture designs against (TA §C.8.7).
FR-003 Must M0 Medium
Decision classes and the human decision-maker
Every output of a rules artefact carries a decision class. Show detail
First needed in: M0 (schema), M5
Description
Every output of a rules artefact carries a decision class. The policy author declares it, the program policy authority approves it on legal advice, and the system enforces it when running. There are three classes:
an administrative decision, which needs reasons and a route to challenge it;
a decision that needs a human decision-maker before it issues, held until that person records it;
a computational intermediate, which is never presented as a decision.
Relates To
BR-002, BR-005, UC-1, UC-7
Parameters
N07, N08, N17
Acceptance Criteria
Given a rules artefact with an unclassified output, when release is attempted, then release is refused.
Given a determination whose adverse outcome rests on any inferred, estimated, averaged or apportioned input, when it is computed, then it is held for a human decision-maker, whatever class the artefact declares TA-C14.
Given a held determination, when no human decision is recorded, then nothing issues and no timeout issues it automatically.
Given a computational intermediate, when any client-facing screen or notice would present it as a decision, then the output is blocked and a governance defect is raised.
Data
Inputs: class on the artefact; where each input came from; Outputs: class recorded on the determination; DiscretionaryDetermination evidence for human decisions; Validations: a human decision records identity, authority and rationale.
Dependencies
FR-093
Rationale
The duty to give reasons attaches to the decision, not to the software, and operating procedures break down at volume (TA §B.4.4, §D.5). Open item: the architecture names the classes three ways, with different ordering: (i)/(ii)/(iii) at §B.4.4, Class 1/2/3 at §C.8.5 and Class A/B/C at §D.5. This document uses the §D.5 A/B/C names. The Chief Architect is asked to adopt one set throughout.
FR-004 Must M4 Medium
Who may decide, value bands, and reasoning that cannot be handed off
The system routes each decision to the person or body with authority for it, by entitlement and, where policy sets one, by value band. Show detail
First needed in: M4 (routing), M5
Description
The system routes each decision to the person or body with authority for it, by entitlement and, where policy sets one, by value band. It records the person who reasoned the decision as the decision-maker of record. It keeps anything the system or another person proposed separate from what the decision-maker concluded.
Relates To
BR-002, BR-003, UC-1, UC-3
Obligations
OB-D10, OB-EL-23, OB-EL-74, OB-SU-02, OB-SU-32, OB-SU-62, OB-SU-63
Parameters
N17
Acceptance Criteria
Given a decision whose value or type needs a higher authority, when a worker without that authority tries to finalise it, then the system routes it to the required authority and refuses to finalise it.
Given any decision where a recommendation or pre-filled outcome was shown, when the record is read, then the proposal and the decision-maker's conclusion are recorded separately PRIN-C6.
Given a request to close or re-open a type of case that needs a named approver, when no approval is recorded, then the action is refused.
Data
Inputs: the schedule of delegated authority (reference data with effective dates); Outputs: decision-maker identity and authority on the record; Validations: the authority was in force on the decision date.
Dependencies
FR-094
Rationale
Policy says a decision-maker "must not delegate the actual decision or allow advice to take the place of their own reasoning". It also sets decision-makers by dollar band, up to Executive Director and ADM (PRIN N17).
FR-005 Must M5 High
Effective dates worked out by rule, for each part of the benefit
A versioned rule works out the effective date of every determination, including one that replaces an earlier determination, a reconsideration outcome, and a re-determination after the tribunal rescinds a decision. Show detail
First needed in: M5
Description
A versioned rule works out the effective date of every determination, including one that replaces an earlier determination, a reconsideration outcome, and a re-determination after the tribunal rescinds a decision. The date is worked out separately for each benefit component and recorded as derived. The ministry's own timeliness is one of the inputs.
Relates To
BR-001, BR-003, UC-2, UC-4
Obligations
OB-R11, OB-A08, OB-SU-79
Parameters
N01, N19
Acceptance Criteria
Given a determination granting several components, when it is recorded, then each component carries its own effective date and the version of the rule that worked it out.
Given a decision issued after its legal time limit expired, when the effective date is worked out, then the earlier date the clock rule sets is applied automatically, without anyone asking.
Given two components policy does not allow in the same month, when both would otherwise be granted, then the determination grants only what the rule allows and records why.
Data
Inputs: benefit type, component, clock state; Outputs: effective dates per component, marked as derived; Validations: no effective date entered by hand without a recorded override authority.
Dependencies
FR-061, FR-090
Rationale
A determination that replaces an earlier one does not take effect on the day it is made. Policy sets the date by benefit type. Where the ministry decided late, policy sets it as the date the decision was due (PRIN N01 amendment v3.1).
FR-006 Must M5 Medium
A pre-decision letter, kept separate from a decision
The system supports a pre-decision communication as its own kind of record, separate from a determination and available to any part of the system that makes decisions. Show detail
First needed in: M5
Description
The system supports a pre-decision communication as its own kind of record, separate from a determination and available to any part of the system that makes decisions. It carries reasons, a response deadline, what happens if the client responds or does not, and a plain statement that no decision has been made yet.
Relates To
BR-003, BR-005, UC-1, UC-5
Obligations
OB-EL-27
Parameters
N01, N08, N19
Acceptance Criteria
Given a pre-decision communication, when its notice is generated, then it states the issues, the response due date and how to respond, and no reconsideration or appeal rights are drawn from it.
Given a client's response within the window, when it arrives, then it is recorded as evidence for the determination that follows.
Given a client asks for reconsideration of a pre-decision communication, when the request is made, then it is recorded (FR-055). The communication's status never causes the request to be refused.
Data
Inputs: draft calculation or list of issues, response clock definition; Outputs: pre-decision communication record; Validations: it cannot carry an adjudicability attribute.
Dependencies
FR-055, FR-061
Rationale
If this were only a status flag on a determination, one rule change could make the system read it as a decision and attach appeal rights to it. The ministry's own intake practice already runs this pattern correctly (NOTE-001 v2.0).
FR-007 Must M5 Medium
Checks that must be recorded before an adverse decision
Before a sanction, reduction, ineligibility or non-compliance decision, the system requires the checks policy sets out to be recorded as evidence: Show detail
First needed in: M5, M8
Description
Before a sanction, reduction, ineligibility or non-compliance decision, the system requires the checks policy sets out to be recorded as evidence:
whether the request made of the client was reasonable;
the client's ability to meet the obligation;
any exemption that applies;
that the requirement was clearly explained and the client had a fair chance to meet it;
the individual assessment of homelessness risk.
It prevents a decision based on anticipation or unconfirmed suspicion.
Relates To
BR-001, BR-003, UC-2
Obligations
OB-EL-01, OB-EL-12, OB-EL-24, OB-EL-76, OB-EL-78, OB-IN-49
Parameters
N07, N08, N20
Acceptance Criteria
Given an adverse decision of a type with registered checks, when any check is unrecorded, then the decision cannot be finalised.
Given a family unit recorded as homeless or at imminent risk, when a failure to provide information would otherwise make it ineligible, then the rule for that group is applied and the reason recorded.
Given an ineligibility based on absence, when the qualifying condition has not yet happened, then no ineligibility decision can be recorded.
Data
Inputs: registered list of checks per decision type; Outputs: check evidence stored with the determination; Validations: every check answered, including answers recorded as a definite "no".
Dependencies
FR-011
Rationale
These are policy rules, and each can be checked. Administrative fairness is the principle behind them, not a criterion in its own right METH-C3.
FR-008 Must M0 High
Replay from stored records, and a declared replay horizon
Any determination can be replayed from what was stored with it (the rules artefact, the engine version and its archived copy, a full copy of the input snapshot, the decision trace and the notice template) without depending on any running system. Show detail
First needed in: M0 (declaration), M5
Description
Any determination can be replayed from what was stored with it (the rules artefact, the engine version and its archived copy, a full copy of the input snapshot, the decision trace and the notice template) without depending on any running system. Before the first live determination, the ministry declares in writing how long replay is guaranteed and what serves as evidence after that.
Relates To
BR-002, UC-4
Parameters
N07, N08
Acceptance Criteria
Given a determination issued in a previous year, when it is replayed in an isolated environment from storage alone, then it produces a decision trace identical to the original, byte for byte.
Given the archived engine copies inside the declared window, when the scheduled test runs, then every archived copy runs or an alarm is raised.
Given a determination whose inputs were disposed of, or whose governing policy text was never published, when it is replayed, then the result is marked with the declared limit and points the reader to the trace, the notice and the shred-survivor set.
Data
Inputs: the five stored artefacts; Outputs: replay result with limit markers; Validations: each artefact's digest checks out against the hash chain.
Dependencies
FR-010, NFR-SEC-009
Rationale
A pointer to a running system is not evidence (PRIN N08). The architecture chooses a layered horizon. It keeps a runnable archive for seven years, a written specification with a regression corpus up to twenty years, and the trace after that TA-C15. Superseded policy text that was never published shortens that horizon unless it is captured when the rules are loaded NOTE2-C1.
FR-009 Must M0 High
Recording the point in time a decision's facts were read
Every determination records the watermark: Show detail
First needed in: M0
Description
Every determination records the watermark: the point in the system's history up to which its evidence snapshot was read. The system refuses to issue a determination when the gap between now and the watermark is larger than the limit set for its class.
Relates To
BR-002, UC-1, UC-6
Parameters
N09
Acceptance Criteria
Given any determination, when its record is read, then the watermark is present.
Given an interactive determination whose gap is over its limit, when issuance is attempted, then it is refused, the worker sees the reason, and a work item is raised TA-C16.
Given a batch issuance run, when any contributing data stream is over the batch limit at the start of the run, then the run stops and no partial run issues.
Data
Inputs: how far each data stream has been applied; limit per determination class; Outputs: watermark on the record; Validations: limits set from measured lag before the first live determination.
Dependencies
NFR-P-004
Rationale
Two determinations made moments apart can each legitimately see a different set of facts, and without the watermark nothing detects it. This is a required addition to the architecture's parameter set, and in practice it cannot be added later (PRIN N09).
FR-010 Must M5 High
Several generations of rules running side by side
The system assesses each period against the generation of rules in force for it and keeps every superseded generation runnable. Show detail
First needed in: M5
Description
The system assesses each period against the generation of rules in force for it and keeps every superseded generation runnable. Where a transition regulation freezes a set of rules, the system runs that frozen set alongside the live one for as long as the regulation requires.
Relates To
BR-001, BR-010, UC-7
Parameters
N01, N07
Acceptance Criteria
Given a retroactive recalculation that spans a rule change, when it runs, then each period is assessed against the generation in force for that period and the record names each generation.
Given a case governed by a frozen transition ruleset, when a determination is made, then the frozen generation is applied and the live generation is not.
Data
Inputs: rules register with effective-from and effective-to dates; Outputs: generation identifier per period; Validations: no period assessed against a generation not in force for it.
Dependencies
FR-090, FR-091
Rationale
There is no date on which the whole rule set is current RULES-C2. Child in the Home of a Relative needs a frozen ruleset running alongside the live one indefinitely OBLG-C6.
B Evidence and verification 14
FR-011 Must M0 High
The four states of a fact
The fact model tells apart four cases: Show detail
First needed in: M0
Description
The fact model tells apart four cases: a value never asked for; a question asked and answered "no"; evidence that was considered but that policy forbids keeping; and evidence that was disposed of. It enforces the bans on printing, scanning, copying or recording that make some evidence impossible to keep.
Relates To
BR-002, BR-006, UC-1
Obligations
OB-EL-07, OB-EL-28, OB-EL-29, OB-EL-40, OB-EL-71, OB-EL-72
Parameters
N01, N08, N12
Acceptance Criteria
Given a capture form, when a question is answered "no", then a recorded "no" (an asserted negative) is stored and can be told apart from a blank.
Given evidence of a type policy forbids keeping or printing, when a worker tries to print it, scan it to the case or attach it, then the action is refused and the fact is recorded as considered but not kept.
Given a determination that rests on evidence that could not be kept, when it is recorded, then the record says its replay chain is incomplete, and why.
Data
Inputs: rules on what can be kept, per evidence type; Outputs: fact state on every assertion; Validations: mandatory questions cannot be left blank.
Dependencies
DR-001, DR-002
Rationale
Only a recorded "no" can support a determination, and the model must represent "considered and may not be held" as a distinct state PRIN-C7.
FR-012 Must M0 High
Corrections, updates, and who made the error
Every change to evidence is recorded as either a supersession (the world changed) or a correction (the record was wrong). Show detail
First needed in: M0 (schema)
Description
Every change to evidence is recorded as either a supersession (the world changed) or a correction (the record was wrong). Every correction must say whose error it was: the client's, the ministry's, a third party's, or undetermined. Completed declarations are never struck out or overwritten, and both parties sign off on any change to them.
Relates To
BR-005, UC-2, UC-5
Obligations
OB-IN-12
Parameters
N01, N06
Acceptance Criteria
Given a correction submitted without saying whose error it was, when it is submitted, then it is refused.
Given a change to a completed application, when it is recorded, then the original stays readable and the change carries the attestation of both the client and the worker.
Given a supersession and a correction affecting the same period, when the overpayment is calculated, then each produces its own separately classified component.
Data
Inputs: type of change and whose error; Outputs: correction or supersession event; Validations: whose error is required on every correction.
Dependencies
FR-051
Rationale
The two kinds of change differ only in how they treat the period a fact was true, and that difference decides whether money can be recovered. The error field must be in the schema before the first event is written (TA §C.7.2).
FR-013 Must M3 Medium
Asking for information, and verifying it
When the ministry needs information, the system sends a request that states what is needed, why, the due date, and how to get help or more time. Show detail
First needed in: M3, M8
Description
When the ministry needs information, the system sends a request that states what is needed, why, the due date, and how to get help or more time. It records contact attempts before any payment is held or changed. It applies the verification rules policy sets for shelter costs, confirmed jobs and other entitlement evidence.
Relates To
BR-001, BR-003, UC-1, UC-2
Obligations
OB-EL-02, OB-EL-26, OB-IN-27, OB-IN-30, OB-IN-43, OB-SU-38, OB-SU-77, OB-SU-78, OB-SU-87
Parameters
N01, N02, N19
Acceptance Criteria
Given an information request, when it is issued, then it lists each item required, a due date worked out from its registered clock, and how to get help or an extension.
Given missing information, when a payment hold or change is proposed, then the system first requires the registered number of recorded contact attempts on the registered channels.
Given shelter-cost evidence supplied by someone other than the landlord, when it is assessed, then it is not rejected for that reason alone.
Data
Inputs: request templates, clock definitions; Outputs: request record, evidence of contact attempts; Validations: due date worked out, never typed.
Dependencies
FR-061, FR-062
Rationale
The client must provide information. The ministry must ask clearly and make reasonable attempts before acting on its absence (OB-EL-02, OB-IN-27, OB-IN-30).
FR-014 Must M8 Medium
Monthly reports and reporting changes
Recipients report the listed types of change and required earnings each reporting period, on any channel. Show detail
First needed in: M8
Description
Recipients report the listed types of change and required earnings each reporting period, on any channel. Each report identifies its reporting period and has its supporting documents attached. Staff may explain the report but cannot fill it in or change it for the client. An incomplete report starts recorded contact attempts.
Relates To
BR-001, BR-009, UC-2
Obligations
OB-EL-15, OB-EL-16, OB-EL-17, OB-EL-18, OB-EL-19, OB-EL-20, OB-IN-51, OB-SU-22
Parameters
N01, N09, N15, N19
Acceptance Criteria
Given a monthly report, when it is submitted, then each reported change becomes evidence with the period it covers, and each required signature is captured.
Given a worker session, when the worker tries to enter or change a client's declaration, then the system refuses and offers the assisted-completion route, with the client's attestation, instead.
Given a report with missing information, when it is processed, then a work item for the registered contact attempts is raised.
Data
Inputs: report, documents; Outputs: evidence assertions; Validations: every report identifies its reporting period.
Dependencies
FR-071, FR-083
Rationale
The monthly report is the main source of evidence for ongoing entitlement, and policy makes it the client's job (OB-EL-15 to OB-EL-20).
FR-015 Must M8 Medium
Third-party checks only with valid consent
The system runs third-party checks only where a valid consent of the right scope and period is on the case. Show detail
First needed in: M8
Description
The system runs third-party checks only where a valid consent of the right scope and period is on the case. It runs the mandatory checks at application, eligibility review and compliance review unless a registered deferral applies. It verifies only what the client provided, asking the client first. It attaches every result received, including "no record found" results.
Relates To
BR-006, UC-1
Obligations
OB-EL-03, OB-EL-04, OB-EL-06, OB-EL-08, OB-EL-09, OB-EL-11, OB-EL-42, OB-IN-53
Parameters
N02, N13, N17, N21
Acceptance Criteria
Given a check request, when no valid consent covers its source and period, then the check is refused before any outside call is made.
Given a verbal consent taken by telephone, when its registered validity runs out without a signature, then checks relying on it are refused.
Given a mandatory check at a review, when no registered deferral applies, then the review cannot be completed without it.
Given a check result, when it comes back, then it is recorded as evidence with its source, including "no record found" results.
Data
Inputs: consent instruments; Outputs: check evidence; Validations: consent scope and period checked at the time of the call.
Dependencies
FR-075, INT-006, INT-015
Rationale
A third-party check without valid consent is unlawful collection. Verbal consent is not enough for taxpayer information (OB-EL-06).

The system treats a warrant as outstanding only when the Ministry of Public Safety and Solicitor General confirms it. It refuses warrant enquiries about dependent children or anyone under the registered age. It keeps the warrant alert up to date as warrants are resolved, issues the prescribed letter on confirmation, and applies the shelter entitlement policy sets for the family unit with no manual adjustment.

Parameters

Given a person under the registered age or a dependent child, when a warrant check is attempted, then it is refused.
Given a family unit with a confirmed warrant and shelter costs in any band, when shelter is determined, then the amount equals the entitlement policy sets, taken from the rules register, with no manual adjustment step.
Given a resolved warrant, when it is recorded, then the alert updates and the clocks of any dependent supplements respond.

FR-017 Must M8 High
Assets, trusts, registered disability savings plans and structured settlements

Description
The system records:
assets and their verified values;
the client's evidence where an asset cannot be turned into cash;
the source of funds for exempt purchases;
trust and RDSP activity and elections;
structured-settlement documents.
Before deciding a case that meets one of the registered trust triggers, the system requires a legal opinion through the ministry's litigation branch. It holds legal opinions as privileged, and it records that eligible clients were told about trust and RDSP exemptions.
Relates To

Obligations

FR-023 Must M8 Medium
Child in the Home of a Relative
The system supports the rules of the Child in the Home of a Relative program, which is closed to new cases: Show detail
First needed in: M8
Description
The system supports the rules of the Child in the Home of a Relative program, which is closed to new cases:
screening consent from every adult in the home, as a condition of eligibility;
identity checks on the person submitting the form;
recording the submitter's ID numbers and the case numbers, without the child's name;
not keeping the screening consent form itself;
checking screening results daily;
approval before a case is closed or re-opened;
immediate referral of any child protection concern.
Relates To
BR-001, BR-006, UC-2

Parameters
N01, N12, N13, N17
Acceptance Criteria
Given a screening consent form, when it is processed, then its content is recorded as policy allows and the form itself is not kept.
Given a child protection concern on a case, when it is recorded, then a referral to the child protection authority is raised immediately and its routing is recorded.
Given a case, when someone tries to close or re-open it without the required approval, then the action is refused.
Data
Inputs: screening consents and results; Outputs: eligibility evidence; Validations: the child's name is never stored on the consent record.
Dependencies
FR-010, FR-070
Rationale
The program runs on a frozen transition ruleset and has stricter privacy and child-safety rules than the general case (OBLG §6).
FR-024 Must M4 Medium

Relates To

OB-EL-25, OB-EL-35, OB-SU-23, OB-SU-26, OB-SU-35, OB-SU-47, OB-SU-48, OB-SU-49, OB-SU-81, OB-IN-57
Parameters
N19, N20, N05
Acceptance Criteria
Given each registered review type, when its clock reaches its trigger, then a review work item is created with its due date and calendar basis.
Given confirmed non-attendance at a mandatory review, when it is recorded, then the notice, the payment actions and the reconsideration clock follow as one recorded sequence.
Given an active investigation review on a case, when a scheduled review would start, then it is suspended as FR-054 requires, without telling the client.
Data
Inputs: review schedule rules; Outputs: review work items and outcomes; Validations: each review type states its calendar basis.
Dependencies
FR-061, FR-067
Rationale
Completing an eligibility review is mandatory, and not completing it ends eligibility (OB-EL-25). Review clocks run on seven different calendar bases (PRIN N19).

Data

FR-040 Must M8 Medium

FR-041 Must M6 Medium
Money paid out now that may have to be repaid
Some money is paid out against a signed promise to repay: Show detail
First needed in: M6, M7
Description
Some money is paid out against a signed promise to repay: reconsideration and appeal supplements, security and pet deposits, co-op share purchases, warrant-related supplements, and hardship promises to pay. The system records each as a repayable issuance. It holds the signed promise, the decision it is waiting on and the outcome. It becomes a debt only on the outcome policy sets.
Relates To
BR-004, BR-005, UC-4, UC-5
Obligations
OB-R18, OB-A11, OB-EL-38, OB-SU-04, OB-SU-06, OB-SU-07, OB-SU-08, OB-SU-67
Parameters
N01, N05, N19
Acceptance Criteria
Given a repayable issuance, when the promise to repay is not signed, then no payment instruction issues.
Given the decision it is waiting on, when that decision issues, then the repayable issuance settles automatically as closed, partly repayable or fully repayable, with no manual reconciliation.
Given deposit rules that depend on earlier deposits still owing, when a new deposit is requested, then the rule is applied using the recorded repayable issuances.
Data
Inputs: signed promise, reference to the awaited decision; Outputs: settlement events; Validations: settled only by the linked decision.
Dependencies
FR-042, FR-053
Rationale
Money paid now, whose repayment depends on a later decision, fits neither the payment model nor the overpayment model NOTE5-C1. Whether an appeal supplement must be repaid when the appeal is dismissed has been referred to the ministry, and the model must support either answer.
E Payments and financial control 9
FR-042 Must M0 High
Every payment goes through one issuance service
Every payment of public money starts as a payment instruction created from a determination. Show detail
First needed in: M0 (specification and criteria 1–3), M6
Description
Every payment of public money starts as a payment instruction created from a determination. Once accepted, an instruction cannot be changed. It carries an identifier the system can recalculate, the determinations it pays, the payee and the capacity they are paid in, the gross amount with each deduction listed, the value date, the benefit period, the channel, a purpose code, a funding code, and the requester and approver. Every instruction passes through one Issuance Service. No other component holds a credential for a payment rail, a cheque print stream or the corporate financial system's posting interface.
Relates To
BR-004, UC-6
Parameters
N17, N05, N18
Acceptance Criteria
Given the credential inventory and the build, when any module outside the Issuance Service declares a dependency on a payment rail, print or posting client, then the build fails (an automated architecture test).
Given an instruction identifier that already exists, when it is submitted again, then no second payment is created, whether or not the details match; if the details differ, the submission is rejected with a reason.
Given an instruction with no determination reference, when it is submitted, then it is flagged as an exception and needs the exception approval.
Given an accepted instruction, when a change is needed, then it is cancelled and replaced, or stopped and reissued. It is never edited.
Data
Inputs: DeterminationIssued events. Outputs: payment instructions. Validations: the identifier is derived from the determination reference, benefit period, payee reference and instruction sequence.
Dependencies
FR-043, FR-046, INT-001
Rationale
A chokepoint that is stated but never specified cannot be built. Adding one after three contexts already hold their own payment-rail credentials means accrediting the payment path all over again TA-C4.
FR-043 Must M6 High
Issuance runs
Payments are issued in runs. Show detail
First needed in: M6
Description
Payments are issued in runs. A run is scheduled, can be resumed, can be audited, and follows a published calendar. Its stages are: cycle open, cutoff, assembly and pre-flight checks, control totals set before approval, approval, release, settlement and returns, reconciliation, and close. A run can be released more than once without paying twice. Supplementary and off-cycle payments are a run of one, with the same controls.
Relates To
BR-004, UC-6
Parameters
N17, N09
Acceptance Criteria
Given a release interrupted part-way, when it resumes, then it finishes instruction by instruction without paying anything twice, and the control totals match those set before approval TA-C17.
Given pre-flight exceptions above the published threshold, when assembly finishes, then the run does not proceed.
Given a closed run, when an adjustment is needed, then it is made with new instructions, and the run cannot be reopened.
Data
Inputs: the set of instructions selected by query, and the cycle definition version. Outputs: a run record with frozen totals. Validations: thresholds are policy settings, not values written into code.
Dependencies
FR-042, FR-045, FR-009
Rationale
The dangerous failure is a run that stops halfway. An operator under pressure then runs it again and pays a live caseload twice (TA §C.6.2).
FR-044 Must M0 High
Payment channels, stop, recall, reissue and returns
The system pays by direct deposit, by cheque and through the province's approved payment service. Show detail
First needed in: M0 (returns handling), M6
Description
The system pays by direct deposit, by cheque and through the province's approved payment service. Stop payment, recall, reissue and return are four separate operations, each with its own states. The system refuses to reissue a payment unless the original is stopped, returned or rejected. When a payment is returned, the system marks the entitlement as unpaid and queues a work item. It starts electronic traces, and it applies a client's choice of payment channel by the cut-off policy sets.
Relates To
BR-004, UC-6
Obligations
OB-SU-29, OB-SU-30, OB-SU-31, OB-SU-34
Parameters
N05, N06, N19
Acceptance Criteria
Given a stop request, when the channel reports failure, then the state is "stop failed" and no reissue is permitted.
Given a failed recall, when it is recorded, then the move to an overpayment is recorded as an event, not re-keyed by hand.
Given a returned payment, when it arrives, then the entitlement is marked unpaid and a work item with its service level is created.
Given a lost or stolen cheque, when a replacement is requested, then the policy conditions (including any service provider signature) are met before it is reissued.
Data
Inputs: channel acknowledgements and return files. Outputs: channel states and links from each reissue to its original. Validations: a reissue never creates a second entitlement.
Dependencies
FR-042, INT-002, INT-003
Rationale
If a system can pay but cannot find and resend failed payments, some clients go unpaid and nobody notices (TA §C.6.3).
FR-045 Must M6 High
Benefit ledger and three-way reconciliation
The system keeps its own double-entry ledger of benefit obligations, recorded when they are owed. Show detail
First needed in: M6
Description
The system keeps its own double-entry ledger of benefit obligations, recorded when they are owed. It records each obligation raised, each payment released and settled, each reversal, each debt raised, each recovery and each write-off. Every entry carries the coding block, the determination reference and the run identifier. Each day the system reconciles the ledger against the channels' settlement records and against the corporate financial system. Each cycle it checks that every financial determination has an obligation and every obligation has a determination.
Relates To
BR-004, UC-6
Parameters
N18, N04
Acceptance Criteria
Given any unmatched item, when reconciliation runs, then a break record is created with an owner, an age and an escalation threshold.
Given a financial determination with no obligation, or an obligation with no determination, when the cycle's reconciliation runs, then it raises an alarm at once.
Given a full monthly cycle at production volume on synthetic data, when it is reconciled, then there are no unexplained breaks.
Data
Inputs: ledger entries, settlement files, corporate postings. Outputs: reconciliation and break feeds. Validations: control totals do not change after assembly.
Dependencies
FR-042, INT-001, INT-002
Rationale
The corporate financial system stays the book of record. The third check, determinations against obligations, is the one that catches the architecture's central claim failing (TA §C.6.4).
FR-046 Must M0 Medium
Separation of duties enforced in code
No person or program can both start and approve a payment. Show detail
First needed in: M0 (specification), M6
Description
No person or program can both start and approve a payment. The system refuses a run's approval if the approver requested any instruction in it, or if the approver's delegated authority is below the run's net value. Changes to a payee's bank details made within the registered window before a run are held for a second approval. Only a separate role can change channel settings.
Relates To
BR-004, UC-6
Parameters
N17
Acceptance Criteria
Given a realistic run in a test environment, when someone who created an instruction in it tries to approve it, then the service refuses, logs the attempt, and the refusal appears in the audit stream with no person stepping in TA-C18.
Given a payee account change inside the hold window, when the next run is assembled, then the affected instruction is held until a second person approves it.
Data
Inputs: the delegated authority schedule. Outputs: refusal events. Validations: authority limits are effective-dated.
Dependencies
FR-094
Rationale
A control left to process only holds until it is tested by pressure (PRIN N17).
FR-047 Must M0 High
Emergency payments and interim provider payments
The system has a designed emergency payment path. Show detail
First needed in: M0 (design and rehearsal), M6 (exercise)
Description
The system has a designed emergency payment path. Clients receive emergency issuance; providers receive interim payments. The path skips only the automated determination. A worker with stated authority pays an amount against a named statutory head, and the system records this as a discretionary determination. The payment still goes through the same chokepoint, ledger, control totals and separation of duties. Each emergency payment creates an obligation to reconcile it later against the real determination. The path has ceilings per cycle and per client, measurable triggers, and a time limit on each use.
Relates To
BR-004, BR-013, UC-6
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED], N17
Acceptance Criteria
Given a registered trigger, when the authorised role invokes emergency issuance, then the invocation ends at the end of the cycle unless someone invokes it again with a written reason.
Given any emergency or interim instruction, when the determination is later made, then the system calculates and classifies the difference automatically and raises a reconciliation work item with its service level.
Given the path's stated capacity, when it is load-tested, then it carries the stated share of a program's caseload for the stated number of days. This is exercised before M6 ends.
Data
Inputs: authority, statutory head, reason. Outputs: emergency instructions with purpose codes. Validations: ceilings are reference data.
Dependencies
FR-042, FR-043, FR-051
Rationale
A rollback restores the system of record over days, but a client's rent is due on a set date. An emergency path invented under pressure cannot be reconciled afterwards TA-C5.
FR-048 Must M6 Medium
Deductions, set-off and the minimum amount a client must keep
Recovery reduces the net amount of a payment instruction. Show detail
First needed in: M6
Description
Recovery reduces the net amount of a payment instruction. It appears as a listed deduction and never as a lower gross amount. The system checks the statutory minimum a client must keep when it issues each payment, and the chokepoint refuses any deduction that would go below it. Set-off across programs happens only through Overpayment and Recovery and the chokepoint.
Relates To
BR-004, BR-005, UC-5, UC-6
Obligations
OB-SU-09
Parameters
N03, N17
Acceptance Criteria
Given an agreed recovery rate, when a client's entitlement falls so the rate would go below the minimum, then the deduction is reduced to the minimum when the payment is issued, and the reason is recorded.
Given any deduction, when the notice is issued, then the deduction appears as its own line.
Given a case context, when it tries to set off directly against another context's entitlement, then the operation is not available.
Data
Inputs: repayment agreements and the minimum-amount rule. Outputs: deduction lines. Validations: the minimum comes from the rules register.
Dependencies
FR-042, FR-053
Rationale
If a deduction engine can be set below the minimum, someone will eventually do it in a hurry for a whole group of clients (TA §C.7.3).
FR-049 Must M6 Low
Tax information slips
The system issues the tax information slip policy requires to every recipient above the registered threshold for the tax year. Show detail
First needed in: M6
Description
The system issues the tax information slip policy requires to every recipient above the registered threshold for the tax year. It takes the figures from the ledger's payment records.
Relates To
BR-004
Obligations
OB-IN-32
Parameters
N06, N09
Acceptance Criteria
Given a tax year's settled payments, when slips are generated, then each slip matches the ledger for that recipient and year.
Data

Dependencies
FR-045
Rationale
This is a statutory reporting duty, met from the book of record (OB-IN-32).
FR-050 Should M6 Medium
Managing and paying providers
The system records recognised providers and the principles used to recognise a type of provider. Show detail
First needed in: M6
Description
The system records recognised providers and the principles used to recognise a type of provider. It proposes contracted providers first where policy says so. It records provider confirmations and client acknowledgements at delivery, and enforces provider obligations such as trial periods and supplies that must come with an item. It pays providers through the chokepoint.
Relates To

Given delivery of equipment that needs the client's signed acknowledgement, when the acknowledgement is missing, then the provider's invoice cannot be paid.
Data

Dependencies

Rationale
Provider and Outcome Management has its own obligations, and a current system the architecture never specified (APP §5).
F Overpayment, compliance and investigation 4
FR-051 Must M6 High
Overpayments calculated and classified from the evidence that changed
An overpayment is the difference between two determination records for the same period. Show detail
First needed in: M6
Description
An overpayment is the difference between two determination records for the same period. The system splits it into one component for each change in evidence. It classifies each component by the operation and fault recorded on that change:
a supersession, or a correction where the client was at fault, is recoverable;
a correction where the ministry was at fault is administrative error;
where a third party was at fault, a person decides, and the default is administrative error;
where fault cannot be determined, it is administrative error unless a person reclassifies it.
Relates To
BR-005, UC-5
Parameters
N01, N06, N08
Acceptance Criteria
Given a recalculation with components in more than one class, when the overpayment is raised, then each component has its own classification and recovery terms, and the notice states each one separately.
Given a migrated fact where nobody knows when the ministry learned it, when a component depends on it, then the component defaults to administrative error and is not recovered unless a person reclassifies it on recorded evidence TA-C19.
Data
Inputs: two determination records and the evidence events. Outputs: classified components. Validations: classification is required; an unclassified component cannot be acted on.
Dependencies
FR-012, DR-013
Rationale
The same arithmetic can be a recoverable debt in one case and an administrative error in another. What decides it is what changed in the evidence (TA §C.7.2). Legal counsel owns the question of how each class is treated under the statute.
FR-052 Must M0 High
A person decides every debt; raising is capped, grouped by cause and reversible
No overpayment is raised and no recovery starts unless a person decides each component. Show detail
First needed in: M0 (reversal mechanism), M6
Description
No overpayment is raised and no recovery starts unless a person decides each component. Automated raising has a cap per cycle on count and on value. When a single cause produces overpayments for more clients than the published threshold, the whole group is held for review before any notice goes out. A batch of debts can be reversed in one operation. The reversal also undoes recovery already taken and issues corrected notices.
Relates To
BR-005, UC-5
Parameters
N17, N18, N14
Acceptance Criteria
Given a calculated component, when no person has recorded a decision, then no debt, notice or recovery exists TA-C6.
Given automated raising that exceeds its cap in a cycle, when the cap is reached, then raising stops and escalates rather than queuing.
Given a batch identifier, when reversal is invoked, then every debt, deduction, set-off and collections referral from that batch is reversed, and corrected notices are issued.
Data
Inputs: components and the group-review thresholds. Outputs: debts and reversal events. Validations: thresholds are set before the first live determination.
Dependencies
FR-051, FR-060
Rationale
A defect that produces a hundred thousand wrong records shows up as one pattern repeated. A process that looks only at one case at a time will never see it (TA §C.7.6).
FR-053 Must M6 Medium
Repayment, write-off, collections and disputes
Repayment agreements keep a version history. Show detail
First needed in: M6
Description
Repayment agreements keep a version history. Where policy requires it, repayment continues after a recipient leaves assistance. A write-off needs one person to request it and a different person, with authority at the threshold, to approve it. A write-off never deletes the overpayment record. A debt referred to collections can be recalled in one operation. A client may dispute whether the debt exists, the amount, the classification or the terms. Each kind of dispute follows the route the architecture sets. Recovery pauses by default while the determination or the classification is disputed.
Relates To
BR-005, UC-5
Obligations
OB-SU-05
Parameters
N17, N01
Acceptance Criteria
Given a dispute of the underlying determination, when it is recorded, then recovery pauses by default, and only a named authority can change that default.
Given a referred debt that is reduced on appeal, when the outcome is recorded, then the referral is recalled in one operation.
Data
Inputs: agreements, disputes, write-off requests. Outputs: ledger events. Validations: write-off thresholds are reference data.
Dependencies
FR-045, INT-019
Rationale
The most common collections complaint in this area is a debt that was disputed or reduced after referral and never withdrawn (TA §C.7.4).
FR-054 Must M6 Medium
Allegations, investigations and referral to investigators
Staff can refer suspected fraud, duplicate identification or long-term ineligibility to the investigation unit, including on closed cases. Show detail
First needed in: M6, M8
Description
Staff can refer suspected fraud, duplicate identification or long-term ineligibility to the investigation unit, including on closed cases. Current eligibility must be assessed first. While an investigation is open, it blocks other work as policy requires, and the system hides it from the client and from staff who do not need to know. The system prevents direct confrontation or contact where policy forbids it, and records the outcome of each investigation.
Relates To
BR-005, BR-006, UC-2
Obligations
OB-EL-13, OB-EL-14, OB-EL-31, OB-EL-33, OB-IN-44, OB-IN-45, OB-IN-46, OB-IN-59, OB-IN-60
Parameters
N05, N17, N21
Acceptance Criteria
Given an open investigation on a case, when a worker opens the case, then the system blocks disclosing the investigation to the client and routes the client's questions about it to the investigation office.
Given a suspicion of personation or duplicate identification, when it is recorded, then a referral is created at once and contact with the client about it is blocked.
Given a referral, when current eligibility has not been assessed, then the referral cannot be submitted.
Data
Inputs: allegations and data matches. Outputs: referrals and investigation status. Validations: referral content follows policy.
Dependencies
FR-080, FR-070
Rationale
An open investigation holds up work in other contexts and continues after a case closes. The mapping found that no context owned it (NOTE-003: Investigation and Loss Management).
G Reconsideration and appeal 6
FR-055 Must M7 Medium
Every reconsideration request is accepted and recorded
A client may ask for reconsideration of any communication, on any channel, including when the ministry thinks no decision has been made. Show detail
First needed in: M7 (M2 for the screens that take requests)
Description
A client may ask for reconsideration of any communication, on any channel, including when the ministry thinks no decision has been made. The system records every request with the date and channel it arrived by. No path in the system lets staff turn a request away when it is made.
Relates To
BR-003, UC-4
Obligations
OB-R14, OB-R15
Parameters
N15, N17, N19
Acceptance Criteria
Given any client-facing channel and any communication, when a client asks for reconsideration, then the request is recorded with the date received and the channel NOTE1-C1.
Given a worker or contact centre screen, when a request comes in, then there is no control to refuse it, only to record and route it.
Given a request made on paper or in person, when it is recorded later, then its received date is the day it physically arrived.
Data
Inputs: the request, and a reference to what it is about (which may be something the ministry does not consider a decision). Outputs: a request record that starts the decision on whether reconsideration is available. Validations: received date and channel are required.
Dependencies
FR-056, FR-071
Rationale
Policy gives an unconditional right to ask. Telling a client "there is nothing to reconsider" is a defect in practice (Conflict C-1) OBLG-C4.
FR-056 Must M7 Medium
The independent unit decides whether reconsideration is available
Whether reconsideration is available is an adjudication. Show detail
First needed in: M7
Description
Whether reconsideration is available is an adjudication. The Reconsideration and Administrative Fairness Unit makes it, modelled as an adjudicating authority that holds that power. The officer who issued the communication never makes it.
Relates To
BR-003, UC-4
Obligations
OB-R16
Parameters
N17, N05, N20
Acceptance Criteria
Given a request, when availability is decided, then the person deciding belongs to the independent unit and took no part in the original communication.
Given a finding that reconsideration is not available, when the client is told, then the notice states the finding and the reasons.
Data
Inputs: the request and the adjudicability attributes. Outputs: the availability decision. Validations: the person deciding took no part in the original.
Dependencies
FR-036, FR-092
Rationale
If the context that runs reconsiderations also decided availability, it would rule on its own jurisdiction (NOTE-001 v2.0).
FR-057 Must M7 Medium
Reconsideration is a new decision by an independent officer
A reconsideration is a new decision on the whole matter. Show detail
First needed in: M7
Description
A reconsideration is a new decision on the whole matter. An officer who took no part in the original decision makes it, using the evidence held when the decision is made. The system supports both kinds of extension, each with its own authorisation. A ministry-side extension without its required authorisation is invalid.
Relates To
BR-003, UC-4
Obligations
OB-R01, OB-R02, OB-R06, OB-R07, OB-R08
Parameters
N01, N05, N09, N17, N19
Acceptance Criteria
Given an officer who took part in the original decision, when someone tries to assign them, then the assignment is refused.
Given evidence that arrives after the reconsideration decision, when it is recorded, then it is left out of that decision's snapshot.
Given a ministry-requested extension without the required authorisation, when it is recorded, then the original time limit stands.
Data
Inputs: the package from FR-058. Outputs: the reconsideration determination. Validations: evidence is cut off at the moment of decision.
Dependencies
FR-061, FR-058
Rationale
Policy requires both an independent reviewer and an evidence cut-off (OB-R02, OB-R08).
FR-058 Must M7 High
The appeal record is assembled from the decision record
The system builds the reconsideration package and the appeal record from the decision record, not by hand. Show detail
First needed in: M7
Description
The system builds the reconsideration package and the appeal record from the decision record, not by hand. They contain the determination, the rules version, the evidence snapshot with where each fact came from, the trace, the notice exactly as issued and the client's submissions. The system severs them under FOIPPA and supplies them to the tribunal and the client within the period the tribunal sets.
Relates To
BR-002, BR-003, UC-4
Obligations
OB-R09, OB-R10, OB-A03, OB-A04
Parameters
N02, N08, N13
Acceptance Criteria
Given any determination, when the appeal record is requested, then it is built entirely from stored records, including the notice exactly as issued, byte for byte.
Given the assembled record, when it is released, then severing has been applied with a reason for each severed passage.
Given a first decision made by another body (for example Pacific Blue Cross), when the ministry must reconsider it, then the administrator's record can be obtained under the terms of its contract.
Data
Inputs: the decision record store. Outputs: the package and the severed appeal record. Validations: a completeness check against the record's inventory.
Dependencies
FR-078, FR-008, INT-009
Rationale
Replay lets the ministry reconstruct a decision for itself. Disclosure hands the record to the client so they can challenge it. A design that only supports replay fails the client (PRIN N08 amendment (b)).
FR-059 Must M7 Medium
The tribunal is an outside party
The tribunal is an outside party listed in the integration inventory. Show detail
First needed in: M7
Description
The tribunal is an outside party listed in the integration inventory. For each appeal the system records how the appeal ended (decided, withdrawn or abandoned) separately from the panel's decision (confirmed or rescinded). It takes in the panel's decision as a decision made by an outside body. It records evidence that entered at the hearing with the hearing as its source. It carries out a rescission by cancelling the original decision and making a new one, never by editing it. It keeps the ministry's representative separate from the original decision-maker and the reconsideration officer.
Relates To
BR-002, BR-003, UC-4
Obligations
OB-A05, OB-A06, OB-A07, OB-A09, OB-A14
Parameters
N01, N02, N08, N17
Acceptance Criteria
Given an appeal outcome, when it is recorded, then only the panel decisions the statute allows are available, and a withdrawn or abandoned appeal has no panel decision NOTE6-C1.
Given a rescission, when it is recorded, then the original determination is cancelled without being replaced, and a work item to make a new determination is created.
Given the choice of the ministry's representative at a hearing, when the candidate made or reconsidered the decision, then the assignment is refused.
Data
Inputs: tribunal decisions (INT-011). Outputs: appeal outcomes and outside decisions. Validations: only the statutory terms are allowed.
Dependencies
INT-011, FR-060
Rationale
The panel can only confirm or rescind, and it may consider evidence that is not in the record. If the list of outcomes is wider than the statute allows, people will use the extra options (NOTE-006).
FR-060 Must M7 High
Putting a decision right, and undoing recovery
When a client wins, the system makes a new retroactive determination and calculates the difference from the old one. Show detail
First needed in: M7
Description
When a client wins, the system makes a new retroactive determination and calculates the difference from the old one. It then pays the underpayment or reverses the overpayment. Where an overpayment is reversed, the system automatically undoes any recovery already taken (deductions, set-offs, collections referrals) and issues a corrected notice.
Relates To
BR-003, BR-005, UC-4
Obligations
OB-A10
Parameters
N06, N08
Acceptance Criteria
Given an allowed appeal that reverses an overpayment, when the new determination is issued, then recovery already taken is reversed and a corrected notice goes out with no manual step TA-C20.
Given an underpayment to be put right, when it is calculated, then it is paid through the chokepoint with its purpose code.
Data
Inputs: the outcome and the old and new determinations. Outputs: payments to put things right, and reversals. Validations: the amount is calculated, never typed in.
Dependencies
FR-052, FR-042
Rationale
A client who wins an appeal and still has money taken from their next payment is the most damaging fairness failure in this area (TA §C.8.4).
H Statutory time 1
FR-061 Must M0 High
One register of legal time limits
Every statutory and policy time limit is registered once as a clock with a unique identifier. Show detail
First needed in: M0 (register), M7
Description
Every statutory and policy time limit is registered once as a clock with a unique identifier. Each clock records:
its owner (the ministry, the client, the tribunal or an outside adjudicator);
its class (entitlement or service standard);
the event that starts it, how long it runs, and its calendar base and day type;
the extensions allowed and who must authorise each.
The system detects and records a breach automatically. Where policy attaches a consequence, the system applies it without anyone asking. Business-day counting is one shared, tested capability.
Relates To
BR-003, UC-2, UC-4
Obligations
OB-R03, OB-R04, OB-R05, OB-R12, OB-A01, OB-A02, OB-A13
Parameters
N19, N01
Acceptance Criteria
Given the clock register, when it is loaded, then every clock states its owner, class, base and day type, with no defaults assumed. The obligation registers number clocks within each partition, and 18 of those numbers repeat across partitions; each clock gets a unique identifier instead.
Given a ministry-owned entitlement clock, when it is breached, then the breach is recorded and its effect on the effective date passes to FR-005 automatically.
Given a clock the ministry does not own, when it is breached, then the ministry bears no consequence for a breach it could not avoid.
Given day counting, when it is tested across holidays, year ends and February's shorter night counts, then every registered base counts correctly.
Data
Inputs: the provincial holiday calendar (reference data) and the start events. Outputs: running clocks and breach events. Validations: each clock is versioned and effective-dated like a rules artefact.
Dependencies
FR-090, FR-094
Rationale
Legal time limits are modelled once and used by every program TA-C21. A missed deadline changes what the client is owed PRIN-C1. Policy contains 138 clocks.
I Notices and correspondence 5
FR-062 Must M2 High
Notices are built from the decision record
Every notice that conveys a decision is produced from the determination record and a template version. Show detail
First needed in: M2
Description
Every notice that conveys a decision is produced from the determination record and a template version. The template version is fingerprinted and stored in that record as the fifth bound artefact, so the same inputs always produce the same notice. Content designers write templates against a registered list of variables. Templates are reviewed for plain language, for legal content where they convey a decision or a right, and for accessibility. They are then approved and released through the rules pipeline. Old templates are superseded, never deleted.
Relates To
BR-002, UC-1, UC-4
Parameters
N08, N10
Acceptance Criteria
Given a determination and its bound template version, when the notice is produced again years later, then it is identical, byte for byte, to the notice issued TA-C22.
Given a template that uses an undeclared variable, when it is validated, then validation fails.
Given a notice that conveys a decision, when it is issued, then the finished document itself is kept.
Data
Inputs: the determination record and the template version. Outputs: the finished notice and its delivery details. Validations: variables come from the record, never from live data.
Dependencies
FR-008, FR-090
Rationale
A tribunal asks what the client was told as often as what was decided (TA §C.8.6).
FR-063 Must M2 Medium
Rights wording and what every notice must say
Every notice of a decision, change or overpayment states what changed, why, when it takes effect, the legislation applied and the information used. Show detail
First needed in: M2, M7
Description
Every notice of a decision, change or overpayment states what changed, why, when it takes effect, the legislation applied and the information used. The system writes the rights section (whether and how to ask for reconsideration or appeal, and to whom) from the entitlement's adjudicability attributes. The prescribed brochure and request form go with every adverse decision. The request form is included even where reconsideration is not available.
Relates To
BR-003, UC-1, UC-2, UC-4
Obligations
OB-D12, OB-R17, OB-EL-10, OB-EL-30, OB-EL-43, OB-EL-77, OB-IN-28, OB-IN-42, OB-SU-60
Parameters
N20, N08, N19
Acceptance Criteria
Given an entitlement that can be reconsidered but not appealed, when its adverse notice is produced, then it offers reconsideration and does not offer appeal.
Given an entitlement whose appeals go to an outside body, when its notice is produced, then it names that body.
Given any adverse notice, when it is issued, then the brochure and request form are in the package delivered.
Data
Inputs: adjudicability attributes and the determination. Outputs: the rights section. Validations: nobody types rights wording by hand.
Dependencies
FR-062, FR-092
Rationale
Getting adjudicability wrong hurts the client either way: offering a route that does not exist, or hiding one that does (PRIN N20).
FR-064 Must M2 Medium
Delivery, proof of service and deemed receipt
The system tells apart a notice that was issued, delivered, deemed received and proven served. Show detail
First needed in: M2
Description
The system tells apart a notice that was issued, delivered, deemed received and proven served. It calculates deemed receipt from the clock artefact. It records the date the client was told on the decision record, separately from the date of the decision. It uses deemed receipt to state, on the notice, how long the client has to respond.
Relates To

Acceptance Criteria

Given a notice, when an operator tries to set the deemed-receipt date by hand, then there is no field to do it.

Dependencies
FR-061, INT-003, INT-004
Rationale
The date the client is told starts their clock, and it differs from the date of the decision (OB-D08).
FR-065 Must M2 Medium
Languages, plain language and accessible formats
Templates and reasons wording exist in every language the ministry must use for correspondence, and the system records the language each notice went out in. Show detail

Templates and reasons wording exist in every language the ministry must use for correspondence, and the system records the language each notice went out in. FR-066 Must M3 Low

The system helps staff arrange interpretation and translation through the contracted provider for applicants who need it. Show detail
First needed in: M3

The system helps staff arrange interpretation and translation through the contracted provider for applicants who need it. It refuses documents needed to decide eligibility if they were translated by a source that cannot be checked, including search-engine or artificial-intelligence translation.

J Work management 4
FR-067 Must M4 High
Work items, queues, and due dates from legal time limits
Work Management owns the task, and the case context owns the work. Show detail
First needed in: M4
Description
Work Management owns the task, and the case context owns the work. Work items have registered types and a typed link into the context that owns them. Assignment and reassignment are recorded as events with reasons. Queues use a pull or push discipline. Due dates come from legal time limits where one applies, and from service standards otherwise. Due dates set by a legal time limit are marked, and operations staff cannot change them.
Relates To
BR-012, UC-1, UC-4
Obligations
OB-EL-73, OB-IN-23
Parameters
N19, N17, N03
Acceptance Criteria

Given a due date set by a legal time limit, when an operator tries to change it, then the change is refused TA-C24.
Given a task record, when someone proposes adding a program-specific field to it, then design review rejects it because it rebuilds a shared model.
Data
Inputs: work item types and clocks. Outputs: work items and their history. Validations: a typed link to the subject.
Dependencies
FR-061
Rationale
Named once, work management avoids five separate task models. Defined too broadly, it becomes the shared case model the architecture exists to prevent (TA §C.9.1).
FR-068 Must M4 Medium
Supervision, escalation and overdue work
Overdue items show first on the worker's own view. Show detail
First needed in: M4
Description
Overdue items show first on the worker's own view. Escalation adds a supervisor as a watcher once an item reaches a set age or state; it does not quietly reassign the item. A supervisor's view covers every team they own, across contexts.
Relates To

Parameters
N19, N17
Acceptance Criteria

Given a supervisor, when they open their view, then items from every context their teams work in appear together.
Data
Inputs: escalation rules. Outputs: supervisor views. Validations: escalation never reassigns.
Dependencies
FR-067
Rationale
Quiet reassignment destroys the record of who was accountable (TA §C.9.3).
FR-069 Should M4 Medium
Balancing caseloads, with a supervisor deciding

First needed in: M4
Description
The system shows where caseloads are uneven and suggests how to redistribute them. A supervisor decides, and the record shows the suggestion was advice only.
Relates To

Parameters
N17

FR-070 Must M4 Low

K Documents, capture and signature 4
FR-071 Must M3 Medium
Documents captured from every channel, with arrival date and context
Documents come in by office scanning, client upload, photos from a phone, worker upload, mail and fax, and partner submission. Show detail
First needed in: M3
Description
Documents come in by office scanning, client upload, photos from a phone, worker upload, mail and fax, and partner submission. Every route records the capture date, the arrival date where different, who captured it, the channel, and the request or case it answers. When a client uploads a document, the system tells them straight away if something is wrong with it.
Relates To
BR-009, UC-1, UC-2
Parameters
N01, N15
Acceptance Criteria
Given a document from any route, when it is stored, then its arrival date, channel, capturer and request reference are present. A document with no request context becomes an orphan work item.
Given a paper document scanned later, when it is stored, then its arrival date is the day it physically arrived, and any clock runs from that date.
Data
Inputs: documents. Outputs: document records. Validations: size, type, page count and format are checked at capture.
Dependencies
FR-072
Rationale
Documents with no link to a request cause most "we never received it" disputes, and a clock runs from the arrival date (TA §C.11.1).
FR-072 Must M3 High
Classification, inherited retention and malware scanning
A document attaches to evidence, to a case or to both, through a typed link. Show detail
First needed in: M3
Description
A document attaches to evidence, to a case or to both, through a typed link. It takes the stricter of its own classification and that of what it is attached to, and it keeps the retention of what it supports. Every incoming file is scanned for malware before anyone can reach it, and scanned again when the malware signatures are updated. Anything derived from a document (extracted text, search indexes, thumbnails) carries the document's classification and is disposed of with it.
Relates To
BR-006, BR-007
Parameters
N12, N13
Acceptance Criteria
Given a document disposed of with its subject, when disposition runs, then extracted text, index entries, thumbnails and in-between copies are disposed of too, as the published list for documents requires.
Given a file caught by a later signature update, when the rescan runs, then it is quarantined and a work item is raised.
Data
Inputs: classification at capture. Outputs: the scan result, kept as part of the document's state. Validations: each document is stored where its classification allows.
Dependencies
DR-003, DR-004
Rationale
Document processing makes copies in more places than any other part of the platform (TA §C.11.2).
FR-073 Must M3 Medium
Values read by machine are unverified evidence
Values produced by text recognition, classification or extraction come in as evidence. Show detail
First needed in: M3
Description
Values produced by text recognition, classification or extraction come in as evidence. They record that a machine extracted them, the extractor's version, a confidence for each field and the part of the page they came from. They start as unverified. Extraction never marks a value verified, and an adverse determination cannot rest on an unverified extracted value.
Relates To
BR-002, BR-005
Parameters
N01, N07, N17
Acceptance Criteria
Given an extracted value, when it is stored, then its status is unverified and it points to the document, page and area TA-C25.
Given an adverse outcome with any unverified extracted input, when it is calculated, then it is held for a person to decide (FR-003).
Data
Inputs: extractor output. Outputs: evidence assertions. Validations: only a person, or a check against an authoritative source, can verify a value.
Dependencies
FR-003
Rationale
The comparator jurisdiction failed to separate "the system read the document" from "the fact is true" (TA §C.11.4).
FR-074 Must M3 Medium
Signatures and attestations
The system supports three kinds of signature: Show detail
First needed in: M3
Description
The system supports three kinds of signature: attestation, a captured signature and a digital signature. Legal advice decides which kind each instrument needs. For every kind the system keeps the signed document and a binding record of the exact text shown, who signed, how they were identified, when, and from which session.
Relates To
BR-002, BR-009, UC-1
Parameters
N08, N01
Acceptance Criteria
Given any signed instrument, when it is retrieved, then the exact text shown at signing can be retrieved, with how the signer was identified and when.
Given a transaction completed with help, when the client attests, then both the helper's identity and the client's attestation are recorded.
Data
Inputs: the instrument and the kind of signature assigned to it. Outputs: the signed document and binding record. Validations: the kind of signature per instrument comes from reference data.
Dependencies
FR-027
Rationale
A signature record without the text that was shown proves nothing about what the person agreed to (TA §C.11.5). Legal counsel still has to decide which instruments need which kind.
L Information governance 11
FR-075 Must M1 Medium
Consents with scope, time limit and withdrawal

Description
Every consent is recorded as an instrument with a status (granted, scoped, expired, withdrawn), a stated scope and period, and the legal authority it relies on. This covers verbal and written consents, consent to taxpayer information, screening consents and consents to disclose. Staff share information only when a consent, power of attorney or other authorising document is on record.

Data

Dependencies

Rationale
The analysis found thirteen consent instruments, and twelve state no way to withdraw consent. That is a missing step in the design, not missing data (NOTE-003).
FR-076 Must M0 Low
Collect only what is needed
The system collects only the information needed to decide eligibility or deliver the service. Show detail
First needed in: M0

The system collects only the information needed to decide eligibility or deliver the service. Each evidence type is registered against its purpose, and the system rejects fields that have not been declared.

FR-077 Must M1 Medium
Disclosure only with a recorded legal basis
Every disclosure is authorised against a legal basis and, where one exists, an agreement in the registry. Show detail
First needed in: M1
Description
Every disclosure is authorised against a legal basis and, where one exists, an agreement in the registry. The system first establishes who is asking and who the information is about. It records each disclosure with the recipient, legal basis, agreement, date and what was released. Where information is disclosed without consent because of compelling circumstances, the system triggers the notice to the client that policy requires. Disclosures required by statute (for child protection, maintenance enforcement, coroners and elected members' enquiries) are set up with their conditions.
Relates To
BR-006, UC-8
Obligations
OB-EL-05, OB-EL-56, OB-IN-19, OB-IN-20, OB-IN-33, OB-IN-34, OB-IN-37, OB-IN-38, OB-IN-40, OB-IN-41
Parameters
N13, N21, N06
Acceptance Criteria
Given a disclosure request with no recorded legal basis, when it is assessed, then it is refused.
Given a statutory disclosure request that policy says must be in writing and cite its authority, when either is missing, then it is refused and recorded.
Given any disclosure, when it is complete, then its record is kept in the shred-survivor set.
Data
Inputs: requests and agreements. Outputs: disclosure records. Validations: the requester's identity is established first.
Dependencies
FR-085, FR-080
Rationale
Most information exchange happens because a statute permits it, not because the client consented. The model therefore starts from legal basis and treats consent as one case of it (TA §C.3.3).
FR-078 Must M3 High
Severing within sentences
Whenever a record is released, the system can sever anything that would identify another person, including an informant, down to individual phrases inside free text. Show detail
First needed in: M3, M7

Whenever a record is released, the system can sever anything that would identify another person, including an informant, down to individual phrases inside free text. It records a reason for each severed passage. This works across every context's records.

FR-079 Must M1 Medium
Correction requests and annotations
A request to correct personal information is received once and acted on across every context that holds the information. Show detail
First needed in: M1
Description
A request to correct personal information is received once and acted on across every context that holds the information. Where the ministry decides not to correct it, an annotation saying a correction was requested but not made is attached, and it travels with the record and every copy.
Relates To
BR-006, UC-8
Obligations
OB-IN-36
Parameters
N06, N01

Given an accepted correction, when it is recorded at the source, then every context holding a copy is listed and must act.
Data

Dependencies
DR-007
Rationale
A refused correction is itself a recorded fact that must travel with the record. Policy states the right to correction but gives no way to carry a correction to parties who already received the information (OBLG §6).
FR-080 Must M0 High
Limits on use travel with the information
Sometimes the ministry may lawfully hold information but is barred from using it a certain way. Show detail
First needed in: M0
Description
Sometimes the ministry may lawfully hold information but is barred from using it a certain way. The bar can cover a detail used in assessing eligibility, a type of content sent to a particular recipient, contact with a particular person, disclosure of a subject, or an act of communication. The system records the bar on the information itself, and the bar travels with every copy. The system enforces it at the point of use: a request must state its purpose, the system refuses by default, and each blocked use creates an event.
Relates To
BR-006, UC-8
Obligations
OB-IN-24
Parameters
N21, N06, N07
Acceptance Criteria
Given a bar on a fact, when the fact is copied into another context, then the copy carries the bar (verified by test).
Given a read that does not state its purpose, when it is made, then it is refused.
Given a barred use, when someone attempts it, then it is refused and an event is recorded PRIN-C3.
Given a detail a client volunteered that is barred from use in assessing eligibility, when a determination is calculated, then that detail is left out of the calculation but still available for its permitted routing use.
Data
Inputs: barred_from and permitted_for on facts. Outputs: enforcement events. Validations: each fact is held once, with a bar per use; facts are never duplicated to express a bar.
Dependencies
DR-006
Rationale
No other rule catches lawfully held information reaching a use it was barred from. A bar missing when information is captured is missing from every copy made before it was added (PRIN N21, §V).

FR-084 Must M0 High
Custodianship and Indigenous data governance

Description
Every evidence type records its custodian, governance regime, access conditions and transfer status. Transferring records to another sovereign is one way a record can leave the system. Relates To

Parameters

Dependencies

Rationale
