FR-085 Must M0 High
The agreement registry is the only source of access rights
Data-sharing agreements are stored as machine-readable records in a registry. Show detail
First needed in: M0/M1
Description
Data-sharing agreements are stored as machine-readable records in a registry. Each records the parties, the services allowed, the authority relied on, the purpose, retention and onward-sharing terms, expiry and review dates, the accountable executives, its status and its history. All gateway and access settings are generated from the registry, and no access decision comes from anywhere else. The registry treats provincial public bodies, federal institutions, Indigenous governing bodies and contracted providers as separate kinds of party, each with its own vocabulary of legal basis.
Relates To
BR-006, BR-008, UC-8
Parameters
N13, N21, N18
Acceptance Criteria
Given the gateway's administration interface, when any credential other than the generator's tries to create a route or consumer, then it is refused.
Given an Indigenous governing body, when an agreement is recorded, then it uses the non-Crown party type and its own legal-basis vocabulary, not a provincial statutory head.
Given an agreement that reaches its review date, when the date passes, then an event is raised automatically.
Data
Inputs: agreements. Outputs: generated settings. Validations: every access right traces back to an agreement.
Dependencies
INT-022, NFR-SEC-003
Rationale
Once anyone grants access outside the registry, the link between legal authority and system access is broken and cannot be rebuilt (TA §C.3.4; decision D8).
M Channels, reach and safety 4

N Rules, adjudicability and automated decisions 5
FR-090 Must M0 High
Policy staff write rules as versioned, effective-dated artefacts
Eligibility rules, rates, clocks and reasons wording are versioned artefacts. Show detail
First needed in: M0 (minimum viable), M5
Description
Eligibility rules, rates, clocks and reasons wording are versioned artefacts. Each carries its policy citation and effective date. An embeddable engine runs them inside the determination service. Policy analysts write and simulate them. They are released through a pipeline with review, sign-off by two people and legal sign-off, and tested against a regression corpus that does not depend on any one engine. A change that reduces the corpus's coverage fails the pipeline.
Relates To
BR-001, BR-010, UC-7
Parameters
N04, N07, N01, N18
Acceptance Criteria
Given two named policy analysts working without help, when they write, simulate and release one real rate change end to end in a test environment, then it succeeds, and the time taken and help needed are recorded TA-C9.
Given a released artefact, when it is inspected, then it is fingerprinted and tagged, carries its policy citation and effective date, and has a regression result.
Given a rule whose only authority is a spreadsheet, when someone tries to release it, then release is blocked until a policy citation exists or the rule is recorded as unauthorised for the ministry to decide.
Data
Inputs: policy text and rate tables. Outputs: rules artefacts. Validations: a citation and effective date are required.
Dependencies
D3 decision; FR-091
Rationale
Running the engine inside the service against a snapshot passed to it is what makes pure evaluation achievable (commitment 2). The business case for the rules platform is that rate changes no longer wait for a software release. That case assumes analysts can write rules in the tool, and nobody has tested that yet.
FR-091 Must M0 Medium
A rules register whose date conflicts block release
Every rule is held in a register with its wording, policy citation, effective marker, start and end dates, authority status (confirmed, several dates, conflicting dates, no marker, unauthorised) and where it lives today. Show detail
First needed in: M0
Description
Every rule is held in a register with its wording, policy citation, effective marker, start and end dates, authority status (confirmed, several dates, conflicting dates, no marker, unauthorised) and where it lives today. Historic rates are captured once when policy is ingested, not fetched again later. Effective dates are taken from the marker on each block of text, never from the page's footer.
Relates To
BR-001, BR-010, UC-7
Parameters
N01, N04
Acceptance Criteria
Given a rule with conflicting effective dates, when someone tries to release it, then release is blocked until a ministry ruling is recorded RULES-C3.
Given a policy page being ingested, when effective dates are captured, then they come from the block's marker and never from the page's "last updated" footer.
Given a practice rule with no policy authority, when it is found, then it is recorded as unauthorised and not released.
Data
Inputs: policy pages, archived rate tables, and the spreadsheets that decide entitlement once they are obtained. Outputs: register rows. Validations: a citation is required.
Dependencies
FR-090
Rationale
Nine rules carry conflicting effective dates in policy, three of them on a single page. A determination made between the two dates cannot be replayed with a certain result (RULES §3).
FR-092 Must M0 Medium
A register of what can be challenged, for each entitlement and variant
For every entitlement and every variant, the system records the statutory basis, whether decisions can be reconsidered, whether they can be appealed, and to which body. Show detail
First needed in: M0 (register), M7
Description
For every entitlement and every variant, the system records the statutory basis, whether decisions can be reconsidered, whether they can be appealed, and to which body. The values are effective-dated and never inherited from a parent entitlement. A client can always ask, whatever the values say.
Relates To
BR-003, UC-3, UC-4
Obligations
OB-R13
Parameters
N20
Acceptance Criteria
Given the register, when it is loaded, then every entitlement and variant has all four values, or is marked unresolved and cannot be used to produce notices.
Given a variant whose parent can be appealed, when the variant's own policy says otherwise or says nothing, then the variant has its own value or is marked unresolved. It never takes the parent's.
Data
Inputs: the 95-row adjudicability register (ARC-001-ADJ-v0.1). Outputs: attributes used by notices and routing. Validations: an unresolved value blocks notices.
Dependencies
FR-090
Rationale
The four values vary independently. One supplement can be reconsidered but not appealed; one variant loses reconsideration while its parent keeps it. None can be worked out from the others PRIN-C2. Fifteen register rows are still unresolved on at least one of the four values.
FR-093 Must M5 Medium
A register of automated decisions, suspended automatically when challenged
The system keeps a published register of the classes of decision it makes automatically. Show detail
First needed in: M5
Description
The system keeps a published register of the classes of decision it makes automatically. Each entry records the program, the rules and version range, the classification and who approved it, whether human review is needed and which statutory decision-maker delegated it, the reasons template, the volume, and how often decisions are challenged and overturned. When a class hits its registered trigger, the system automatically sends every decision in it to a person for review.
Relates To
BR-002, BR-005
Parameters
N17, N18
Acceptance Criteria
Given a class without an approved reasons template, when a decision in it would be issued, then it cannot be issued.
Given a class whose rate of decisions overturned against the ministry exceeds its registered threshold in a cycle, when the cycle closes, then the class moves to human review, and decisions keep being issued with a person approving each one.
Given a class allowed to issue without human review, when its entry is read, then it cites the delegation from the statutory decision-maker TA-C2.
Data
Inputs: challenge and outcome data. Outputs: the register and suspension events. Validations: only the governance decision can reinstate a class.
Dependencies
FR-003
Rationale
The comparator was missing a rule about which outputs count as decisions; more testing would not have caught it (TA §D.5).
FR-094 Must M0 Medium
Reference data with one owner and effective dates
Reference data that drives decisions and controls has one master, effective dates, publication as events, and change control. Show detail
First needed in: M0
Description
Reference data that drives decisions and controls has one master, effective dates, publication as events, and change control. It includes the provincial holiday calendar, the delegated authority schedule, value bands, approval and write-off thresholds, pre-flight thresholds, emergency ceilings and deemed-receipt rules.
Relates To
BR-004, BR-010
Parameters
N04, N05, N01
Acceptance Criteria
Given a threshold a control uses, when it is changed, then the change is versioned with an effective date and an approver, and no deployment is needed.
Given any system that needs reference data, when it uses it, then it reads the published master and keeps no copy of its own.
Data
Inputs: approved changes. Outputs: reference data events. Validations: the schema compatibility policy applies.
Dependencies
NFR-I-003
Rationale
Each financial control threshold is a setting under change control, not a value fixed in a deployment (TA §C.6.5).
O Transition assurance and analytics 2
FR-095 Must M5 High
Shadow comparison against recorded inputs
While old and new systems run side by side, each legacy determination records a snapshot of exactly what the legacy calculation read, from every legacy system that runs program logic. Show detail
First needed in: M5
Description
While old and new systems run side by side, each legacy determination records a snapshot of exactly what the legacy calculation read, from every legacy system that runs program logic. The new determination service is then run against that snapshot. The comparison checks the structure of each result: the outcome, each rule, each input fact, the effective period and each component. Each difference is classified as a new-system defect, a legacy defect, a difference in policy interpretation, a data difference or rounding. Each class has its own exit criteria, which must hold for three monthly cycles in a row.
Relates To
BR-001, BR-011
Parameters
N07, N05, N18
Acceptance Criteria
Given a comparison where two wrong components cancel out to the same total, when it runs, then it is reported as a difference TA-C26.
Given a timing difference, when one is seen, then it is raised as a defect in the snapshot mechanism, not sent for adjudication.
Given a difference in policy interpretation, when it is found, then it goes to the standing panel's queue, and the panel's ruling is built into the rules artefact.
Given the legacy side of the comparison, when it is set up, then it includes every legacy place the calculation happens (including MIS benefit calculation).
Data
Inputs: snapshots of legacy inputs and legacy decision records. Outputs: classified differences. Validations: difference records are classified and disposed of like any other client data.
Dependencies
FR-008, INT-023, DR-014
Rationale
Comparing live against a lagging copy makes timing the main source of differences. Replaying against recorded inputs removes timing by design (TA §C.2.7). The legacy output is the benchmark to compare against, not the specification.
FR-096 Should M1 High
Reports and analytics from the governed analytics platform
Operational, management and statutory reports come from the governed analytics platform without new copies of production data. Show detail
First needed in: M1 onwards
Description
Operational, management and statutory reports come from the governed analytics platform without new copies of production data. So do the automated-decision register's rates, reconciliation and drift measures, and the decommission burn-down. Direct reporting from transactional databases is retired, or kept as a dated exception with a named owner.
Relates To
BR-006, BR-011
Parameters
N02, N03, N12
Acceptance Criteria
Given a reporting user, when they get data, then it comes from the governed store at the level of detail they are entitled to, with no new extract.
Given a direct database read found on a transactional store, when it is found, then it is recorded in the channel register with a disposition and an owner.
Data
Inputs: published events. Outputs: governed datasets. Validations: interactive queries must filter on a partition.
Dependencies
DR-017, D5
Rationale
Downstream use must not need a copy (commitment 4). A conformed-dimension warehouse is already in production, so this is a migration, not a fresh start (APP §9).
P Explicitly excluded 3
FR-097 Won't Low
Card payment processing inside the ministry
The system does not process cardholder data. Show detail
First needed in: n/a
Description
The system does not process cardholder data. Card payments go through the province's approved payment service, as one channel of the Issuance Service.
Relates To
BR-004
Parameters
N11
Acceptance Criteria
Given any store, event or log, when it is scanned, then it contains no cardholder data TA-C27.
Data
Outputs: tokens and settlement references only.
Dependencies
INT-025
Rationale
The private cloud platform was never built to meet PCI-DSS. Processing cards in-house would be a programme in its own right (TA §C.6.7).
FR-098 Won't Low
Automatic resolution of conflicting changes to client data
The system does not resolve conflicting changes to client data automatically. Show detail
First needed in: n/a
Description
The system does not resolve conflicting changes to client data automatically. When the legacy system changes a record the new system now owns, the change is rejected at source or sent to a person to reconcile within a service level. The latest change never simply wins.
Relates To
BR-011
Parameters
N05
Acceptance Criteria
Given a legacy change to a record the new system owns for that group of clients, when it arrives, then it is rejected or queued for a person, never merged.
Data
Outputs: items in the reconciliation queue.
Dependencies
DR-014
Rationale
If software settles conflicts in data that decides what someone receives, a merge rule makes a choice that belongs to policy or to a person (PRIN N05).
FR-099 Won't Low
Tribunal outcomes the statute does not allow
The system does not record "allowed in part" or "referred back" as panel outcomes. Show detail
First needed in: n/a
Description
The system does not record "allowed in part" or "referred back" as panel outcomes. The panel confirms or rescinds. Withdrawn and abandoned describe how an appeal ended, not what the panel decided.
Relates To
BR-003
Parameters
N20, N08
Acceptance Criteria
Given the list of appeal outcomes, when it is inspected, then confirm and rescind are the only panel decisions.
Data
Outputs: statutory terms only.
Dependencies
FR-059
Rationale
If the list of outcomes is wider than the statute allows, people will use the extra options. Two of the six values in the architecture's list have no statutory basis (NOTE-006). This exclusion amends target architecture §C.8.2.
DRAFT
A design proposal for the successor to British Columbia's integrated case management systems, covering employment assistance, disability assistance, child care subsidy, employment services and child protection.
Figures on this site are drawn from the architecture document and from 326 service-delivery procedures. Nothing here is a government commitment.

=== page: requirements/index.html
title: Requirements — The Future of Case Management IT
description: The 213 requirements for the system that replaces ICM and MIS: what it must do, how well, what it connects to, and where the trade-offs are.
Skip to content

Requirements
These are the requirements for the system that replaces ICM and MIS. Each one says what the system must do, how to check it, and which law, policy or design parameter it comes from.
[aria-label] The requirements in numbers
213 requirements across five categories
270/270 policy obligations traced to a requirement
21/21 design parameters carried by at least one requirement
8 trade-offs set out, 2 still waiting on a ministry ruling
Where the requirements come from
Sources are ranked, and the ranking settles any conflict between them. Where a procedure says one thing and policy says another, the requirement follows policy and the procedure is recorded as a defect for the ministry to fix.
Legislation The Employment and Assistance Acts and their regulations, privacy, records and human rights law. Overrides everything else.
Policy The BCEA Policy and Procedure Manual: 126 pages, 270 obligations, 297 rules, 138 time limits. Overrides every procedure, job aid and spreadsheet.
Practice Procedures, job aids and spreadsheets that show how the work is done today. Evidence of current practice. Never the authority for a requirement.
What they cover
Each category has its own page. Every requirement opens to show its description, the checks that prove it is met, and the reasons it exists.
14 Business What the ministry needs the new system to achieve, and how success is measured. 14 must
99 Functional What the system must do, from a first application to an appeal, grouped by capability. 91 must · 5 should · 3 won't
56 Quality How well it must do it: availability, recovery, security, privacy, accessibility and more. 53 must · 3 should
25 Integrations Every outside system it must exchange information with, and on what terms. 19 must · 6 should
19 Data How facts are recorded, kept, destroyed and moved from the legacy systems. 17 must · 2 should
When they are needed
The architecture delivers the system in ten modules, each in use before the next is funded. This chart counts the functional requirements by the module in which each is first needed. The foundations module carries the most, because some things cannot be added once the first record, rule or payment exists.
20 M0 Foundations
10 M1 Read access and client index
4 M2 Notices and correspondence
9 M3 Documents and capture
8 M4 Work management
9 M5 Decisions and rules
11 M6 Payments and recovery
6 M7 Reconsideration and appeal
18 M8 Employment and disability assistance
0 M9 Child protection
Functional requirements by the module in which each is first needed. A requirement needed across several modules is counted in the first.
How each requirement is written
It can be checked. Every requirement carries acceptance criteria written as "given, when, then", so a tester can say whether it passes.
It says where it comes from. Each one lists the policy obligations it meets and the design parameters that test it, and links to them.
It holds no dollar amounts or day counts. Those change, so they live once in the rules register with their policy source and effective date. A requirement names the rule; the register holds the value.
It does not copy today's system. Where the current system calculates something other than what policy states, the requirement follows policy.
What is still open
Some requirements depend on decisions nobody has made yet: rulings on conflicts inside policy, the records schedules, and several architecture decisions. The trade-offs page sets out each conflict, how it was resolved or who must resolve it, and the dependencies and risks that go with them.
Source: requirements specification, version 1.1, a draft. Words with a special meaning link to the glossary.
DRAFT
A design proposal for the successor to British Columbia's integrated case management systems, covering employment assistance, disability assistance, child care subsidy, employment services and child protection.
Figures on this site are drawn from the architecture document and from 326 service-delivery procedures. Nothing here is a government commitment.

Integrations
Every outside system the new system must exchange information with: what flows each way, how it is protected, and what happens when it fails.
Three rules apply to every integration below. They are not repeated in each entry.
1. An integration that is not in the Module 0 integration inventory is not authorised to exist TA-C42. Each entry here becomes one or more named rows in that inventory, using the columns in TA §C.13.2: system, counterparty and accountable role, direction, pattern, classification, legal basis, criticality and disposition. The Programme Chief Architect owns the inventory, and it is due by month 4 of Module 0. 2. Every integration has a legal basis recorded in the agreement registry (FR-085). An integration without one is unauthorised, whatever it does today. 3. No interactive path depends synchronously on more than one external participant (NFR-A-004). Where an entry says "asynchronous", this rule is why. Where no source states a service level, the entry says "not stated". The design then assumes the exchange is not on a path a worker waits on, until the counterparty commits to a figure in writing.
Details marked [U] are unverified in the architecture's own register. They are settled in the inventory, not here.

INT-001 Must
Corporate Accounting System
Post payments, reversals, amounts owed to the ministry, recoveries and write-offs to the book of record, and reconcile daily and at month-end. Show detail
Purpose
Post payments, reversals, amounts owed to the ministry, recoveries and write-offs to the book of record, and reconcile daily and at month-end.
Integration Type
Batch posting and reconciliation query
Data Exchanged
From this system to CAS: postings with coding block, determination reference and run identifier; supplier records for provider payments.
From CAS to this system: the posted position, rejections, the month-end calendar and blackout periods.
Integration Pattern
Only through the Issuance Service (FR-042). No other component holds a posting credential.
Authentication
A service credential held only by the Issuance Service, over mutual TLS.
Error Handling
CAS rejects some batches as a whole when supplier key fields are missing (APP-R8). Supplier keys are therefore checked before submission. A rejection becomes a reconciliation break with an owner and an age. It is never retried silently.
SLA
Daily reconciliation. Postings are queued during blackouts (NFR-A-005). Today CAS offers only file-availability windows. The cutoff calendar is still to be confirmed by the Executive Financial Officer.
Owner
Provincial corporate financial function; ministry Executive Financial Officer.
Classification
Protected B
Rationale
The corporate financial system remains the book of record (TA §C.6.4). CAS is outside the replacement scope, so the new system must connect to it (APP §1.1).
INT-002 Must
Bank and electronic funds transfer
Pay by direct deposit; Show detail
Purpose
Pay by direct deposit; receive settlement, return and reject files; run payment traces; receive client debt repayments.
Integration Type
Batch file transfer
Data Exchanged
Outbound: payment files in the format the bank requires; trace requests.
Inbound: settlement confirmations, returns, rejects, trace results and repayment files.
Integration Pattern
Through the Issuance Service only. A missing inbound file raises an alarm.
Authentication
Mutual TLS and file signing, as the bank requires.
Error Handling
A returned payment reopens the entitlement and queues a work item (FR-044). A missing file raises an alarm.
SLA
Settlement within the bank's stated window. The maximum reconciliation lag is stated for each payment channel.
Owner
The settlement institution; ministry payment operations lead.
Classification
Protected B
Rationale
Payment is the most critical integration (TA §C.13.3).
INT-003 Must
Provincial print-and-mail and cheque printing
Print and mail notices, letters and booklets; Show detail
Purpose
Print and mail notices, letters and booklets; print cheques; receive returned mail and delivery confirmations.
Integration Type
Batch file transfer (assumed, because no public API specification has been found [U])
Data Exchanged
Outbound: rendered documents with delivery details; cheque print files drawn from a controlled range of cheque numbers.
Inbound: confirmations that mail was lodged; returned mail.
Integration Pattern
Notices go through Notices and Correspondence. Cheques go through the Issuance Service.
Authentication
SFTP with service credentials, to be confirmed with the service.
Error Handling
Returned mail updates the delivery record and raises a work item. Deemed receipt is calculated by rule (FR-064), never typed in.
SLA
The file delivery windows the service sets.
Owner
Provincial print-and-mail service; ministry correspondence business owner.
Classification
Protected B/C
Rationale
Notices and cheques go through this service today, over 10 named interfaces (APP §4.2).
INT-004 Must
Provincial notification service
Send notices and messages electronically, and receive delivery confirmations. Show detail
Purpose
Send notices and messages electronically, and receive delivery confirmations.
Integration Type
API
Data Exchanged
Outbound: messages and notice references.
Inbound: delivery events.
Integration Pattern
Asynchronous. The service is used as it is. If it is not ready in time for correspondence capture, a named and funded fallback takes over: the federal notification platform or the provincial common hosted email service.
Authentication
OAuth 2.0 client credentials, as the service requires.
Error Handling
If electronic delivery fails, the notice goes by the client's next preferred channel.
SLA
Not stated. To be confirmed against the correspondence capture date.
Owner
Provincial notification platform; Chief Digital Officer.
Classification
Protected A/B
Rationale
The system reuses the provincial service, but the service is still being built, so it is treated as a dependency (TA §C.18).
INT-005 Must
Provincial identity services
Sign in workers, citizens, businesses and partners. Show detail
Purpose
Sign in workers, citizens, businesses and partners. Exchange tokens across organisational boundaries so that the legal basis for an exchange travels with the request.
Integration Type
Real-time OIDC
Data Exchanged
From the identity provider: signed-in identities and their assurance levels (the corporate directory with multi-factor authentication, the BC Services Card at assurance level 3, and BCeID).
Token exchange (RFC 8693) and rich authorization requests (RFC 9396), which carry the agreement identifier and the legal authority relied on.
Integration Pattern
A back end for front end for each experience. Tokens are delegated, never impersonated.
Authentication
OIDC confidential clients.
Error Handling
Every channel depends on this service, so its availability counts in the combined availability arithmetic (NFR-A-001).
SLA
Highly available across sites [V as at January 2026]. It is unconfirmed whether the deployed version supports token exchange and rich authorization requests [U]. The ministry CTO checks this within 60 days of programme start.
Owner
Provincial identity service; ministry CTO.
Classification
Not applicable
Rationale
Rich authorization requests are what carry the legal basis, and they still have to be built (TA §C.3.3).
INT-006 Must
Canada Revenue Agency
Check income and tax information for eligibility and overpayments, with valid consent. Show detail
Purpose
Check income and tax information for eligibility and overpayments, with valid consent.
Integration Type
Batch file transfer, consent-based query, or both [U]
Data Exchanged
Inbound: taxpayer information, as consented. It is not printed or kept as a document (FR-011).
Outbound: requests that carry a consent reference.
Integration Pattern
Asynchronous. Consent is checked before every request (FR-015).
Authentication
As the agreement specifies [U].
Error Handling
If no response arrives, the check is deferred. The determination then follows the policy on deferral. The system never fills in a value.
SLA
Twice-daily batch today. Not stated for the new system.
Owner
Federal revenue agency; the ministry business owner named in the inventory.
Classification
Protected B/C
Rationale
This information drives eligibility and overpayment decisions (TA §C.13.3).
INT-007 Must
Employment and Social Development Canada and Service Canada
Exchange CPP, OAS/GIS and EI information; Show detail
Purpose
Exchange CPP, OAS/GIS and EI information; verify social insurance numbers; support assignments and consents to deduction.
Integration Type
Batch and query [U]
Data Exchanged
Inbound: federal benefit status and amounts; SIN verification.
Outbound: requests, assignments and deduction consents.
Integration Pattern
Asynchronous. Volumes include a CPP request file of about 250,000 records (APP §10).
Authentication
As the agreement specifies [U].
Error Handling
A failed file raises an alarm. No deduction is applied without a confirmed consent.
SLA
Not stated.
Owner
Federal benefits administrator; the ministry business owner named in the inventory.
Classification
Protected B/C
Rationale
Entitlement and set-off both depend on federal income benefits (FR-018).
INT-008 Should
Provincial health insurance and health data
Enrol recipients in health coverage, confirm coverage status, and exchange health identity and pharmacare information. Show detail
Purpose
Enrol recipients in health coverage, confirm coverage status, and exchange health identity and pharmacare information.
Integration Type
A mix of file, event and query [U]
Data Exchanged
Outbound: coverage applications; reported changes to name, sex or birth date.
Inbound: coverage status; identity matches; death notifications.
Integration Pattern
Asynchronous. Health data is Protected C, and cross-ministry traffic goes through the exchange.
Authentication
As the agreement specifies [U].
Error Handling
Pending coverage appears as a work item (FR-029).
SLA
Not stated.
Owner
Ministry of Health and Health Insurance BC; the ministry business owner named in the inventory.
Classification
Protected C
Rationale
Health coverage depends on assistance status (TA §C.13.3).
INT-009 Must
Pacific Blue Cross (delegated decision-maker)
Exchange requests and decisions for the health supplement lines Pacific Blue Cross decides, and receive the outcomes that use up ministry replacement intervals. Show detail
Purpose
Exchange requests and decisions for the health supplement lines Pacific Blue Cross decides, and receive the outcomes that use up ministry replacement intervals.
Integration Type
Batch, API or both [U]
Data Exchanged
Inbound: first decisions, recorded as evidence with their source; outcomes that use up ministry replacement intervals.
Outbound: eligibility confirmations; the ministry's rules and intervals as the administrator applies them.
Integration Pattern
Asynchronous. External decisions are taken in under FR-036.
Authentication
As the contract specifies.
Error Handling
A missing return is detected by checking the record of used intervals.
SLA
The contract obliges the administrator to send outcomes back, and to make its records disclosable and severable. Both are needed because Reconsideration must review decisions it did not make.
Owner
Pacific Blue Cross; the ministry's health supplement business owner.
Classification
Protected C
Rationale
Policy never requires these outcomes to be sent back, so the ministry's clocks run where only the administrator can see them MAP-C2.
INT-010 Must
Community Living British Columbia
Receive CLBC's decisions and appeal outcomes for the entitlement it decides and reviews, and issue payment on them. Show detail
Purpose
Receive CLBC's decisions and appeal outcomes for the entitlement it decides and reviews, and issue payment on them.
Integration Type
Batch, portal or both [U]
Data Exchanged
Inbound: eligibility decisions, appeal outcomes and prescribed-class verifications.
Outbound: payment status.
Integration Pattern
Asynchronous. The record shows that the ministry keeps only the power to issue payment (FR-036).
Authentication
As the agreement specifies [U].
Error Handling
No payment is made without a recognised decision.
SLA
Not stated. The CLBC appeal runs on no clock the ministry can see.
Owner
CLBC; the ministry business owner named in the inventory.
Classification
Protected C
Rationale
The ministry pays on a decision it neither made nor can review (PRIN N17 v3.5).
INT-011 Must
Employment and Assistance Appeal Tribunal
Send appeal records; Show detail
Purpose
Send appeal records; receive notices of appeal, hearing details, the outcome of each appeal and the panel's decision.
Integration Type
Records go out and decisions come back. The exchange mechanism is unconfirmed [U].
Data Exchanged
Outbound: the severed appeal record, sent to the tribunal and, through it, to the appellant.
Inbound: notice of appeal (EAAT001), hearing schedule, how the appeal ended, and whether the panel confirmed or rescinded.
Integration Pattern
Asynchronous. The tribunal is an external party, not a user of the system.
Authentication
As agreed. Legal counsel is still to confirm the legal basis for disclosure.
Error Handling
The record-supply clock and the hearing clock are registered (FR-061), so a missed deadline is detected.
SLA
The record is supplied within the period the tribunal sets. The hearing is held within the tribunal's clock.
Owner
The tribunal; Reconsideration and Administrative Fairness Unit.
Classification
Protected C
Rationale
Statutory clocks depend on this exchange (TA §C.8.2). Policy now confirms which tribunal it is (NOTE-006).
INT-012 Must
BCANDS, Indigenous Services Canada and First Nations that run assistance
Each side recognises the other's disability designations. Show detail
Purpose
Each side recognises the other's disability designations. The ministry verifies on-reserve designations. For people living on reserve or on Modern Treaty land, the system records where they are sent and the evidence for any exception.
Integration Type
Request and response through Band Social Development Workers and the deciding body [U]
Data Exchanged
Outbound: verification of ministry designations, within the registered clock.
Inbound: designations made in the other jurisdiction, recorded with how current they are; First Nation confirmations.
Integration Pattern
Asynchronous. Where a body acts under its own jurisdiction, it is recorded in the non-Crown branch of the registry (FR-085).
Authentication
As the agreement specifies.
Error Handling
Today neither side tells the other when a designation changes. The record therefore says "recognised as at [date], not confirmed since".
SLA
The ministry's verification clock, as registered.
Owner
BCANDS, ISC and First Nations; the ministry's Indigenous relations function.
Classification
Protected B/C
Rationale
Mutual recognition took effect on 2026-07-13 and is new (OBLG §4.4); DRV-06.
INT-013 Must
Ministry of Children and Family Development and delegated agencies
Report child protection concerns, respond to disclosure requests under section 96 of the CFCSA, run screening for the Child in the Home of a Relative program, and work with delegated agencies. Show detail
Purpose
Report child protection concerns, respond to disclosure requests under section 96 of the CFCSA, run screening for the Child in the Home of a Relative program, and work with delegated agencies. The close ties between the two ministries continue until child protection is captured (M9).
Integration Type
A mix of referral, request and response, and partner access [U]
Data Exchanged
Outbound: reports and referrals; information disclosed in writing under section 96.
Inbound: screening results; requests; submissions from delegated agencies.
Integration Pattern
Cross-ministry traffic goes through the Secure Data Exchange (INT-022). Delegated-agency access is listed first, because external users with direct access to the legacy system are the riskiest group not yet listed (TA §C.12.1).
Authentication
Through the exchange and the agreement registry.
Error Handling
If a referral cannot be sent electronically, it goes by a recorded manual route. It is never dropped.
SLA
The duty to report is immediate. The screening mailbox is checked daily today.
Owner
MCFD and the delegated agencies; the ministry business owner named in the inventory.
Classification
Protected C
Rationale
Child safety depends on this exchange, which makes it the most critical (TA §C.13.3); DRV-08.
INT-014 Must
Ministry of Public Safety and Solicitor General
Confirm outstanding arrest warrants for applicants and recipients who have consented. Show detail
Purpose
Confirm outstanding arrest warrants for applicants and recipients who have consented.
Integration Type
Request and response [U]
Data Exchanged
Outbound: confirmation requests with the consent reference.
Inbound: confirmation results.
Integration Pattern
Asynchronous, through the exchange.
Authentication
Through the exchange.
Error Handling
An unconfirmed warrant flag cannot drive a determination (FR-016).
SLA
Not stated.
Owner
PSSG; the ministry business owner named in the inventory.
Classification
Protected B/C
Rationale
Policy recognises only a confirmed warrant (OB-EL-36).
INT-015 Must
Third-party verification sources
Run the mandatory and discretionary third-party checks where valid consent exists. Show detail
Purpose
Run the mandatory and discretionary third-party checks where valid consent exists. These cover consumer credit, vehicle and driver records, land title and personal property registries, property assessment, student financial assistance, and financial institution queries.
Integration Type
Query, automated where the source allows [U]
Data Exchanged
Outbound: queries covered by consent.
Inbound: results, including "no record found", recorded as evidence with the source named.
Integration Pattern
Asynchronous, with work items. The new system does not use screen-scraping robots, except as a dated, recorded exception.
Authentication
As each source requires.
Error Handling
A failed check is retried or deferred as policy says. The system never assumes a result.
SLA
Not stated.
Owner
Each source organisation; the ministry business owner named in the inventory.
Classification
Protected B
Rationale
These checks are mandatory at application, eligibility review and compliance review (OB-EL-04).
INT-016 Should
Vital statistics
Receive births, deaths and name changes as events. Show detail
Purpose
Receive births, deaths and name changes as events.
Integration Type
Event or batch [U]
Data Exchanged
Inbound: births, deaths and name changes.
Integration Pattern
Asynchronous. A death stops future payments and starts the related work.
Authentication
As the agreement specifies [U].
Error Handling
Matching runs through the client index (FR-028). A person decides any uncertain match.
SLA
Not stated.
Owner
Provincial vital statistics service; the ministry business owner named in the inventory.
Classification
Protected B
Rationale
Death notices prevent overpayment, and births change entitlement (TA §C.13.3).

INT-019 Must
Collections

INT-020 Should
Provider contract management and provider portal
Exchange provider records, contracts, orders, invoices and payment status with the ministry's provider contract system and provider portal. Show detail
Purpose
Exchange provider records, contracts, orders, invoices and payment status with the ministry's provider contract system and provider portal.
Integration Type
REST API with OAuth token exchange
Data Exchanged
Both directions: provider recognition, orders, invoices and payment status.
Integration Pattern
The current provider contract system (PCMS) is recent. It is to be assessed for keeping rather than replacing (APP §2). The integration goes through the published contract.
Authentication

Error Handling
An invoice that does not match becomes a work item.
SLA
Not stated.
Owner
The provider contract management service owner.
Classification
Protected B
Rationale
Provider and Outcome Management already has a system in place (APP §12).
INT-021 Should
Employment services (WorkBC)
Exchange employment-service referrals, plans and messages about client issues. Show detail
Purpose
Exchange employment-service referrals, plans and messages about client issues.
Integration Type
API and exchange of work items [U]
Data Exchanged
Both directions: referrals, plan status and requests to communicate.
Integration Pattern
Asynchronous.
Authentication
As agreed.
Error Handling
A failed message becomes a work item.
SLA
Not stated.
Owner
The employment services program; the ministry business owner named in the inventory.
Classification
Protected B
Rationale
Employment services are in the architecture's scope. How deep these requirements go follows BR-014.
INT-022 Must
Secure Data Exchange
Carry all exchange with other ministries. Show detail
Purpose
Carry all exchange with other ministries. The exchange provides secure transport and access control. This system adds the evidence of what was exchanged.
Integration Type
API gateway
Data Exchanged
Both directions: every cross-ministry request and response, each carrying a token limited to its purpose and an agreement identifier.
Integration Pattern
Gateway configuration is generated only from the agreement registry (FR-085). Evidence tier E1 is in place before the first production exchange (NFR-SEC-010).
Authentication
Mutual TLS and delegated tokens.
Error Handling
When the exchange is down, determinations proceed on the evidence held, where policy permits, and are flagged for later verification (NFR-A-008).
SLA
No availability target has been committed. It must be obtained in writing (DEP-06).
Owner
The provincial exchange programme; ministry CIO.
Classification
Up to Protected C in transit
Rationale
This is commitment 1 (TA §A.3).
INT-023 Must
Legacy platforms while old and new run side by side
Serve the published contract from the legacy platforms while capture proceeds; Show detail
Purpose
Serve the published contract from the legacy platforms while capture proceeds; write data back to legacy for captured cohorts; feed the shadow comparison.
Integration Type
Anti-corruption layer (facade, adapter and translator), runtime events, transactional outbox, change-data capture
Data Exchanged
From the legacy platforms: events and read models for cohorts not yet captured; the inputs each legacy decision used (FR-095).
To the legacy platforms: write-back for captured cohorts, using insert and update operations only (DR-014).
Integration Pattern
The layer holds no business rules and is set up to be retired. MIS is not a passive store: it holds payment issuance, debt and time limits, and it is the master copy when income data conflicts (APP §2). Both the coexistence design and the legacy side of the shadow comparison must therefore include MIS and every other legacy system that runs program logic (APP §7.1).
Authentication
Dedicated integration identities. Write-back uses its own identity, so the system can recognise its own writes and stop them looping back.
Error Handling
A late legacy change to a captured record goes to a queue for a person to reconcile (FR-098).
SLA
Sized from the measured point at which the legacy platform saturates (NFR-P-001).
Owner
The coexistence lead; the legacy platform's configuration authority, whose capacity is itself an open dependency (DEP-03).
Classification
Protected C
Rationale
Replacing the legacy platforms step by step is impossible without this (commitment 3). A comparison against only part of the legacy calculation is not a real check (TA §C.2.7).
INT-024 Must
Recipients entitled to disclosure by law
Disclose information on request to recipients entitled to it by statute or policy. Show detail
Purpose
Disclose information on request to recipients entitled to it by statute or policy. These are the maintenance enforcement program, coroners, police where authorised, and elected members acting for constituents with a certificate of authority.
Integration Type
Request and response, mostly manual [U]
Data Exchanged
Outbound: only the permitted information, with severing and use limits applied. Personal correspondence may not go to the maintenance program without consent (FR-080).
Integration Pattern
Each disclosure is recorded under FR-077.
Authentication
The requester's identity and authority are confirmed first.
Error Handling
A request without the required authority is refused and recorded.
SLA
Not stated.
Owner
The access and privacy office.
Classification
Protected B/C
Rationale
These disclosure duties come from obligations OB-IN-38, OB-IN-40 and OB-IN-41.
INT-025 Must
Sanctioned provincial payment service
Send card payments and some electronic payments through the province's approved payment service, which posts to the corporate financial system. Show detail
Purpose
Send card payments and some electronic payments through the province's approved payment service, which posts to the corporate financial system.
Integration Type
API and batch
Data Exchanged
Outbound: payment instructions.
Inbound: tokens and settlement references. No cardholder data enters ministry systems.
Integration Pattern
One of the Issuance Service's payment channels. It does not bypass the Issuance Service.
Authentication
As the service requires.
Error Handling
Differences in posting times are reconciled.
SLA
The service's stated levels.
Owner
The provincial payment service; the Executive Financial Officer.
Classification
Tokenised
Rationale
This keeps the platform out of PCI-DSS scope (TA §C.6.7).
DRAFT
A design proposal for the successor to British Columbia's integrated case management systems, covering employment assistance, disability assistance, child care subsidy, employment services and child protection.
Figures on this site are drawn from the architecture document and from 326 service-delivery procedures. Nothing here is a government commitment.

Quality requirements
How well the system must work: how fast, how available, how secure, how accessible and how easy to support. Targets come from the architecture or are measured from the running legacy systems.
The figures in this section come from two places: the architecture's own positions, and measurements in the Release 26.7 technical design documents. For the services that make decisions and pay benefits, the architecture does not set response-time, concurrency or availability figures. It requires them to be measured from the running legacy system and given an owner TA-C28, and this document does the same. No volume figure in the sources covers concurrency, response time or storage APP-C2, and the service-delivery procedures give none either BPCM-C3.
