[aria-label] Categories on this page
Performance 6
Availability and Resilience 8
Scalability 3
Security 12
Compliance and Regulatory 8
Usability 5
Maintainability and Supportability 7
Portability and Interoperability 7
Performance 6
NFR-P-001 Must
The capacity and response table is complete, measured and owned
Before design freeze, every cell of the architecture's capacity table is filled in and has a named owner. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Before design freeze, every cell of the architecture's capacity table is filled in and has a named owner. The table covers peak and average transactions per second, concurrent workers, annual determination volume, p95 and p99 response times, availability, recovery time and recovery point. It covers the Open Host Service, the anti-corruption layer, the determination service, the event backbone, each domain store, work management and payments.
Figures come from the legacy system's own telemetry over a full monthly issuance cycle, not from workshop estimates.
Concurrent worker numbers come from directory and session data. Determination volumes come from legacy counts per program family.
Response targets start from observed legacy behaviour, plus the improvement the service standard commits to.
Measurement Method
The table is reviewed at the design-freeze gate. Every figure must trace to a telemetry extract.
Load Conditions
The only volumes recorded today are per-interface and batch figures from the technical design documents APP-C1. For example, the employment-assistance monthly rollover covers about 158,414 benefit plans, 414,225 benefit lines and 73,920 orders. MIS feedback runs to about 400,000 header and 400,000 detail records a month. A CPP request file holds about 250,000 records. The predecessor's audit counted about 9,400 user accounts (TA §C.16.4). That is the number of users, not the number working at once.
Rationale
Nobody can responsibly approve the combined caseworker read while the legacy platform's saturation point is unmeasured. The anti-corruption layer's rate limits, circuit breakers and bulkheads are sized from these numbers (TA §C.15.2).
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED], N18
NFR-P-002 Must
Payment runs finish within the financial calendar
A full monthly issuance cycle at production volume completes within the window the corporate financial calendar allows. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
A full monthly issuance cycle at production volume completes within the window the corporate financial calendar allows. The cycle includes assembly, pre-flight checks, approval, release, settlement intake and three-way reconciliation. If release is interrupted, it resumes and still finishes within the same window.
Measurement Method
A full-scale synthetic run in a production-shaped environment, including a test that interrupts release part-way (TA §C.6.8 criterion 3).
Load Conditions
Monthly rollover volumes as in NFR-P-001. The peak follows the issuance run, not the working day.
Rationale
Load on the payments service peaks with the issuance run, not over the course of the day (TA §C.15.1).
Parameters
N17
NFR-P-003 Must
Determination capacity at measured volume and peak
The determination service handles the measured annual determination volume for each program family and the measured peak rate. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
The determination service handles the measured annual determination volume for each program family and the measured peak rate. This includes recalculating every affected case in batch after a rate change. The capacity model records the headroom factor, set by its owner, the ministry CTO.
Measurement Method
A load test that replays a recorded month of determinations, and a rate-change simulation across the full affected population.
Rationale
The architecture calls annual determination volume "the single most important number" in its capacity table (TA §C.15.1).
Parameters
N07
NFR-P-004 Must
A limit on how stale the facts behind a decision can be
Before the first production determination, the system sets a limit on how far the evidence snapshot may lag behind the latest recorded facts. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Before the first production determination, the system sets a limit on how far the evidence snapshot may lag behind the latest recorded facts. There is one limit per determination class (interactive, batch issuance and retroactive recalculation), set from measured projection lag. The system monitors the lag against the limit.
Measurement Method
Projection-lag telemetry for each contributing stream, with an alarm as lag approaches the limit.
Rationale
The architecture's example limits (seconds for interactive decisions, about a minute for batch) are unverified. The real numbers must come from measurement (TA §B.4.3).
Parameters
N09
NFR-P-005 Must
Event backbone consumer lag
Each consumer publishes the most lag it can tolerate. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Each consumer publishes the most lag it can tolerate. The system raises an alarm at half that figure. Past the maximum, captured cohorts move to manual verification before any payment issues.
Measurement Method
Lag metrics for each consumer against its own threshold.
Rationale
When the backbone degrades, messages pile up, and a pile-up is only safe if it has a limit (TA §E.8.3).
Parameters
N06, N18
NFR-P-006 Should
Analytics query profile
Interactive analytics queries must filter on a partition. Show detail
Priority: SHOULD_HAVE ---
Requirement
Interactive analytics queries must filter on a partition. Service tiers are committed per data class, as decided under D5. Caching for the most sensitive class happens in memory only.
Measurement Method
The Module 0 object-store benchmark, and query-plan checks that reject interactive queries without a partition filter.
Rationale
The object store's documented profile is response times over 100 ms and 1,000 active connections per node. Partition pruning is the first lever, and local disk caching is forbidden for Protected C (TA §A.5, §C.14).
Parameters
N12
Availability and Resilience 8
NFR-A-001 Must
Availability targets and combined availability
Each component on the caseworker's interactive path is available 99.9% of the time. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Each component on the caseworker's interactive path is available 99.9% of the time. The combined caseworker read has a design target of 99.5%. That read runs through the experience back end, the Open Host Service, three contexts and the determination service. Availability is stated per service, and the combined figure is recalculated whenever the chain of calls changes.
A 99.5% combined figure allows about 2¼ minutes of unplanned downtime per 7.5-hour working day [D].
Maintenance windows for payment services come from the financial calendar (NFR-M-007).
Measurement Method
Availability is measured at the contract boundary, as the consumer experiences it (NFR-M-002).
Rationale
Availability multiplies along a chain of dependencies, and nobody has yet done that arithmetic for this system's own chain of calls (TA §C.3.8).
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED]
NFR-A-002 Must
Recovery point and recovery time
- RPO: Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
RPO: zero for anything that affects an entitlement or a payment, meaning determinations, payment instructions and evidence assertions TA-C29. Other data may have a stated RPO.
RTO: stated for each service against the harm its failure causes. Shared infrastructure takes the strictest target of anything that depends on it.
Recovery objectives are proven by exercise for each release train, not just stated.
Measurement Method
Recovery exercise results for each tier-1 component. A figure nobody has measured is not a target.
Rationale
A lost payment instruction is a person without money TA-C13.
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED]
NFR-A-003 Must
Every dependency declares its timeout, circuit breaker and fallback
Every synchronous dependency has a declared timeout, a circuit breaker and a declared fallback behaviour. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Every synchronous dependency has a declared timeout, a circuit breaker and a declared fallback behaviour. Every screen that depends on the exchange states what the worker sees, what they can still do, and what is queued.
Circuit breaker for external dependencies
Timeout on all network calls
Retry with backoff only for idempotent operations
Bulkhead isolation, including per external provider
Degraded behaviour documented per screen
Measurement Method
An architecture fitness function that checks every outbound client has a timeout and a breaker, plus tests of each fallback mode.
Rationale
A dependency without a stated fallback takes the caseworker desktop down with it (TA §C.15.3).
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED], N18
NFR-A-004 Must
Dependencies on other organisations in interactive work
No interactive path depends synchronously on more than one external participant . Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
No interactive path depends synchronously on more than one external participant TA-C30. Any exchange on a caseworker path that blocks the worker needs 99.9% availability, run active-active across multiple sites, with bulkheads for each provider. Where two or more participants are involved, the design is asynchronous and uses a work item.
Measurement Method
Call-graph analysis for each interactive journey. The exchange's availability commitment is obtained in writing (dependency DEP-06).
Rationale
Four participants at 99.5% each combine to 98.0%, which is too low for work a caseworker waits on (TA §C.3.8).
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED]
NFR-A-005 Must
Payments continue during a corporate posting blackout
Payments keep issuing while the corporate financial system is closed for month-end or year-end posting. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Payments keep issuing while the corporate financial system is closed for month-end or year-end posting. Postings wait in a queue that has an owner and an age alarm, and they are released when posting reopens.
Measurement Method
A blackout simulation in the M6 test cycle, plus an age alarm on queued postings.
Rationale
A benefit payment must not depend on a finance system's maintenance window (TA §C.6.6).
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED], N17
NFR-A-006 Must
Disaster recovery and business continuity are exercised
Disaster recovery exercises run twice a year, and at least one each year is unannounced to the operations team . Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Disaster recovery exercises run twice a year, and at least one each year is unannounced to the operations team TA-C31. They cover catalogue restore, event backbone recovery, read-model rebuild and determination replay from the decision record store.
The business owns a business continuity plan that is separate from rollback. It covers how an office serves a client with no system for a day and for a week, how staff record actions for later entry, and who authorises payment. It is exercised each year with the regional offices before the first capture.
Measurement Method
Exercise reports with measured recovery times, checked against NFR-A-002.
Rationale
A restore nobody has run is a hypothesis (TA §E.8.5).
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED], N14
NFR-A-007 Must
The child protection reporting line has its own availability target
The 24/7 statutory child protection reporting line has the highest availability target in the platform, set by its business owner with the CIO. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE (M9) ---
Requirement
The 24/7 statutory child protection reporting line has the highest availability target in the platform, set by its business owner with the CIO. Its intake path depends on no service whose combined availability falls below that target. A rehearsed fallback path receives and safely records a report when downstream services are down. The line has its own change window.
Measurement Method
The combined-availability arithmetic is run against this chain of calls specifically, and the fallback path is rehearsed.
Rationale
If the reporting line is down for two hours on a Sunday, a child protection report goes unreceived (TA §C.12.2).
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED], N15
NFR-A-008 Must
Platform fallback modes are specified, rehearsed and owned
Each failure below has a fallback mode that is rehearsed and has a named decision-maker: Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Each failure below has a fallback mode that is rehearsed and has a named decision-maker:
The anti-corruption layer is unavailable. Read models keep serving and show a visible staleness indicator.
The event backbone is unavailable. The outbox accumulates messages.
The determination service is unavailable. Determinations queue, and a captured cohort never falls back to legacy.
The exchange is unavailable. Where policy permits, determinations proceed on the evidence held and are flagged for verification after issue TA-C32.
The legacy platform is unavailable. Cohorts not yet captured become read-only.
Measurement Method
Rehearsal records for each fallback mode.
Rationale
A fallback mode first discovered during an incident is an outage (TA §E.8.3).
Parameters
N05, N16 [PROPOSED]
Scalability 3
NFR-S-001 Must
Scale to caseload and payment-run peaks
Services scale horizontally, without code changes, to the measured peaks in NFR-P-001 to NFR-P-003. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Services scale horizontally, without code changes, to the measured peaks in NFR-P-001 to NFR-P-003. The capacity model records growth projections for caseload and determination volume, set by its owner.
Growth Projections
None of the sources give any. The capacity model's owner (the ministry CTO, with the operations directorate) records them before design freeze.
Measurement Method
A scale test to the recorded headroom factor.
Rationale
Scale depends on the number of people served, not on the legacy system, so today's volumes are a minimum.
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED]
NFR-S-002 Must
Data volume across decades of retention
Stores can be partitioned by retention class from the first event, and are sized to keep records for decades. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Stores can be partitioned by retention class from the first event, and are sized to keep records for decades. The current system keeps child services records for up to 90 years after closure and investigation records for 15 years (APP §6). Records are disposed of by class when their schedule expires.
Data Archival Strategy
Set per fact class under DR-004. The default is disposal of a whole class on schedule. Large, loosely structured content uses reference-based indirection. Per-subject cryptographic erasure applies only to named classes. Archival transfer applies where required.
Rationale
Partitioning by retention class must be in place from the first event (TA §B.7.1).
Parameters
N12
NFR-S-003 Must
Migration and backfill at cutover volumes
Migration, identity matching and backfill run, re-run and reconcile at cutover volumes within agreed windows. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Migration, identity matching and backfill run, re-run and reconcile at cutover volumes within agreed windows. The design documents record matching-key volumes of about 15 million contact aliases, 35 million service-provider keys in the corporate accounting system, 1 million service-provider keys and 8 million contact-matching keys.
Measurement Method
A full-volume migration rehearsal that passes the quality gates in DR-012.
Rationale
Migration is a product with its own quality gates, not a project task (TA §C.2.8).
Parameters
N01, N14
Security 12
NFR-SEC-001 Must
Authentication
All users sign in through the provincial single sign-on service using OIDC. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
All users sign in through the provincial single sign-on service using OIDC.
Staff: the corporate directory, with its multi-factor authentication.
Citizens: the BC Services Card authentication service, at identity assurance level 3.
Businesses and providers: BCeID Basic and Business.
Browser security: each experience has a back end for front end that holds the confidential client. No access token, refresh token or identity assertion reaches storage the browser can read TA-C33.
Session and re-authentication rules follow the provincial service's policy and are recorded for each experience.
Measurement Method
A security architecture review at each module gate, plus an automated check that no token reaches the browser.
Rationale
Identity is a commodity and is reused as it is (TA §B.6.1; commitment 8).
Parameters
N11
NFR-SEC-002 Must
Access rules written as tested code
Program confidentiality rules and API access rules are versioned, tested policy artefacts. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Program confidentiality rules and API access rules are versioned, tested policy artefacts. A policy engine evaluates them, and they are released through the same pipeline as eligibility rules. Access is checked at every resolver and endpoint, on both the links and the records of the graph. A restricted client record is a separate type, not an empty field on a normal record. Every access decision is logged with who, what, the purpose and the legal basis.
Measurement Method
A policy test corpus in CI, where a policy change that reduces coverage fails the build. Graph tests confirm that a restricted record's existence cannot be inferred from empty fields.
Rationale
In child protection, the fact that a record exists is often the sensitive fact (TA §B.6.2).
Parameters
N21, N13, N18
NFR-SEC-003 Must
Access rights are generated, never granted by hand
Access rights come from role definitions and program assignments held in a system of record, and automation applies them. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Access rights come from role definitions and program assignments held in a system of record, and automation applies them. Manual grant is not a supported operation TA-C34. Every role definition has a named owner and an expiry date. The system publishes a count of accounts holding rights that the access model does not explain, with a target of zero. Access reviews run every quarter for standard roles and every month for elevated and restricted-record access.
Measurement Method
Accounts reconciled against the access model and published every cycle.
Rationale
The predecessor's audit found that more than a third of about 9,400 users had access outside the defined model, and that nobody was checking (TA §C.16.4).
Parameters
N17, N18
NFR-SEC-004 Must
Active access monitoring and restricted-record controls
The system watches access patterns for anomalies, such as records outside the assigned caseload, out-of-hours restricted access and unusual volumes. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
The system watches access patterns for anomalies, such as records outside the assigned caseload, out-of-hours restricted access and unusual volumes. Alerts go to a monitored queue with an SLA. Staff must record a business reason before opening a restricted or active-protection record. Break-glass access exists, is logged, and is reviewed within one business day. Restricted-record access is logged separately and can raise its own alerts.
Measurement Method
SLA metrics for the monitoring queue, plus sampled reviews of break-glass events.
Rationale
In a social-services breach, the people most at risk are those under active protection (TA §C.16.2).
Parameters
N17, N18
NFR-SEC-005 Must
Encryption and key management
- Data in transit: Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Data in transit: TLS everywhere, with mutual TLS between exchange participants.
Data at rest: encrypted in every store, backup and document store. Per-subject payload encryption applies only to fact classes assigned cryptographic erasure.
One key inventory records, for each key, the custodian role, how it is held, how it is rotated, how it is destroyed, and what becomes unreadable if it is lost.
Per-subject data keys are wrapped by a master key in a hardware security module or the platform key service. They are never exported in plaintext and never held in escrow. The wrapping key rotates once a year.
Measurement Method
The key inventory is reviewed at each gate. Destruction is verified by showing that a known ciphertext can no longer be decrypted.
Rationale
A key whose loss makes twenty years of determinations unverifiable needs different handling from one whose loss only means reissuing a certificate (TA §C.16.3, §B.7.3).
Parameters
N12, N08
NFR-SEC-006 Must
Secrets management
No secret appears in code, configuration, design documents or logs. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
No secret appears in code, configuration, design documents or logs. Secrets are kept in the platform secrets service. No connection uses clear-text authentication.
Measurement Method
Secret scanning in CI and across document repositories, plus a credential inventory.
Rationale
The platform already provides secrets management, and the system reuses it (TA §C.18).
Parameters
N11, N18
NFR-SEC-007 Must
Vulnerability management and penetration testing
- SBOM generation, licence scanning and vulnerability scanning block builds in CI, across the whole platform. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
SBOM generation, licence scanning and vulnerability scanning block builds in CI, across the whole platform.
An independent tester runs a penetration test at each module gate. It covers what changed, plus a standing set of identity, access and exchange-edge tests.
Remediation: critical findings are fixed, or formally risk-accepted by a named executive, before the gate closes. High findings are fixed within 30 days with a tracked plan. Medium findings are fixed within 90 days. Low findings go into the backlog with an expiry date TA-C35. Risk acceptances expire after 90 days.
Measurement Method
Gate evidence. An open critical finding means the gate fails.
Rationale
A finding without a fix date is an open finding (TA §C.16.1).
Parameters
N18
NFR-SEC-008 Must
Threat models and incident response
Each bounded context has a threat model before its first production release. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Each bounded context has a threat model before its first production release. The model is revised whenever trust boundaries, external interfaces or data classification change. An incident response runbook and severity model exist before the first production release, and are exercised at least once a year.
Measurement Method
Both are required artefacts at the release gate.
Rationale
No threat model, no production release (TA §C.16.1).
Parameters
N18
NFR-SEC-009 Must
Records that show if they have been tampered with
The decision record store, the event backbone and the access-decision stream are hash-chained. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
The decision record store, the event backbone and the access-decision stream are hash-chained. Chain heads are signed and kept separately from the store, under different administrative control. An offline verifier can check integrity without the live systems.
Measurement Method
A job that verifies the chain, plus a tampering simulation in test.
Rationale
Records examined years later need integrity designed in, not assumed (TA §C.4.4, §B.5.5).
Parameters
N08, N13
NFR-SEC-010 Must
Evidence of exchanges with other organisations
The system reaches four evidence tiers for cross-organisation exchange: Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE (E1, E2) · SHOULD_HAVE (E3) · COULD_HAVE (E4) ---
Requirement
The system reaches four evidence tiers for cross-organisation exchange:
E1, in place before the first production exchange: every request and response is logged with participant, agreement, legal basis, purpose, correlation identifier, timestamp and hashes of the message bodies.
E2, at launch: the log is hash-chained, and signed chain heads are kept independently.
E3, within the first year: chain heads get trusted timestamps.
E4: each message is signed, for a named class of disclosures agreed with legal counsel.
Measurement Method
Exchange log records checked against the schema, plus chain verification.
Rationale
A message exchanged before E1 is in place leaves no evidence, ever TA-C36.
Parameters
N18, N21
NFR-SEC-011 Must
Every entry path is checked the same way
Aggregates enforce their own rules, and no integration, batch load, migration script or write-back path gets around them. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Aggregates enforce their own rules, and no integration, batch load, migration script or write-back path gets around them. Any write path that skips validation needs a written decision that names each skipped check and what makes up for it.
Measurement Method
Tests that send invalid commands through every entry path, plus an inventory of written bypass decisions.
Rationale
A rule the aggregate enforces cannot be skipped by an integration, a batch load or a migration script (PRIN N04).
Parameters
N04
NFR-SEC-012 Must
Personal information outside production
Development, test and training environments use synthetic or de-identified data. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Development, test and training environments use synthetic or de-identified data. The shadow-comparison pipeline processes real personal information, so it is classified, retained and disposed of under the same rules as the main store.
Measurement Method
Classification scans of non-production stores.
Rationale
Comparison records must not become an uncontrolled second store of client data (TA §C.2.7, §E.7.2).
Parameters
N12
Compliance and Regulatory 8
NFR-C-001 Must
Privacy compliance and breach readiness
Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act; Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Applicable Regulations
Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act; the ministry's FOIPPA policy.
Compliance Requirements
Collection limited to what is necessary (FR-076); disclosure starts from the legal basis (FR-077)
Access and correction rights supported (FR-079, FR-081)
Privacy impact assessment complete for each context before its gate, alongside the security assessment (NFR-C-006)
"Whose personal information was accessed, by whom, and when" answerable with a query, not an investigation
Correlation identifiers carried across every boundary, so a breach that spans legacy, the layer and a new context can be traced
Data Residency
Canadian data centres, per provincial cloud policy. Protected C storage per NFR-C-004.
Rationale
The duty to notify runs on a "without unreasonable delay" standard, so the time from detection to assessment is the control that matters (TA §C.16.2).
Parameters
N13, N21, N06
NFR-C-002 Must
What the audit log records, and how long it keeps it
Each audit event records who (user or service), what, when (UTC), where (component), why (purpose, legal basis, correlation identifier) and the result. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Each audit event records who (user or service), what, when (UTC), where (component), why (purpose, legal basis, correlation identifier) and the result. Retention follows the records classification and the appeal window, not the platform defaults of two months for system logs and thirteen months for audit logs TA-C37. Retention is set before the first production audit log is written. Log content is treated as personal information.
Log Integrity
Hash-chained, per NFR-SEC-009.
Rationale
Retention that was never applied cannot be applied after the fact (TA §C.17.2).
Parameters
N12, N18
NFR-C-003 Must
Records retention and disposition
Before the first production event, the system decides disposition for each fact class (DR-004). Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Before the first production event, the system decides disposition for each fact class (DR-004). That covers the mechanism, the published shred-survivor set, key custody, how destruction is verified, and what replay does with disposed data. Replay substitutes a typed tombstone. It never fails and never skips. Each disposition is certified, and afterwards the financial control totals still reconcile to the same values TA-C38.
Rationale
The authority for N12 is the Information Management Act and the ARCS/ORCS schedules, and neither has been acquired yet OBLG-C2.
Parameters
N12, N08
NFR-C-004 Must
Classification and where data is kept
Protected C data is stored only on-premise. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Protected C data is stored only on-premise. It may be processed on the general compute tiers, within the D12 decision on what counts as storage TA-C39. No Protected C data is processed or stored in public cloud. Public cloud workloads, in Canadian regions only, use only de-identified, aggregated, synthetic or differentially-private derivatives (D6). Access by support staff and vendor telemetry from outside Canada count as disclosure.
Measurement Method
An inventory of where each store and derived artefact is placed. Node settings in the sensitive pool, with swap and core dumps turned off, are verified.
Rationale
Legacy data counts as Protected C by inheritance until it is reclassified (commitment 5).
Parameters
N12, N13
NFR-C-005 Must
Automated administrative decisions
Every class of automated determination is classified, registered and authorised under FR-003 and FR-093. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Every class of automated determination is classified, registered and authorised under FR-003 and FR-093. Every adverse determination gives reasons that trace to a rule and a fact. It also carries a recourse notice stating what may be challenged, by when, how, and what happens to payment in the meantime.
Measurement Method
The random-sample reconstruction test in TA §C.8.5, run each cycle.
Rationale
Every determination that harms a person's interests is an administrative decision, and carries a duty to give reasons and a right of recourse (TA §A.7 risk 6).
Parameters
N07, N08, N17, N20
NFR-C-006 Must
Privacy, security, accessibility and records evidence at every gate
A context is not captured until four pieces of evidence are complete: Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
A context is not captured until four pieces of evidence are complete: its privacy assessment; its security assessment (threat model, review, penetration test and tested incident runbook); its accessibility conformance evidence, including manual testing; and its records disposition classification (TA §E.10 items 7–9).
Measurement Method
The gate checklist.
Rationale
The architecture holds that a definition of done covering privacy but not security fails (TA §E.10).
Parameters
N12, N15, N18
NFR-C-007 Must
Alignment with the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act
The ministry's Indigenous relations function confirms which action-plan commitments apply to this system. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
The ministry's Indigenous relations function confirms which action-plan commitments apply to this system. Each commitment is traced to the registry features that carry it: the participant class, the legal-basis vocabulary, the custodianship attribute and the transfer outcome (FR-084, FR-085).
Measurement Method
A traceability review by the Indigenous relations function.
Rationale
The architecture has not verified which commitments apply, and they must be recorded (TA §B.8.4).
Parameters
N13
NFR-C-008 Must
Financial administration
The corporate financial system remains the book of record. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
The corporate financial system remains the book of record. Five items are Comptroller and CFO sign-off points, held as configuration under change control: the delegated authority schedule, run approval thresholds, the month-end position, write-off thresholds and the decision to invoke emergency issuance.
Measurement Method
A configuration audit and the sign-off records.
Rationale
Each is a financial control and belongs in governed configuration, not as a constant written into a deployment (TA §C.6.5).
Parameters
N17
Usability 5
NFR-U-001 Must
Workers' tasks do not get slower
Before each context's gate, the ten most common work item types take no longer, and need no more screens or system switches, than the legacy baseline. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Before each context's gate, the ten most common work item types take no longer, and need no more screens or system switches, than the legacy baseline. This is measured with real workers on realistic data. Workers' confidence in the system's answers and the time a new worker takes to become competent are measured and published.
Measurement Method
A baseline captured before the context's build begins TA-C12, then acceptance measurement for each office.
Rationale
A capture that makes a top task slower is a defect. Only a named executive can override this go-live criterion, in writing (TA §E.9).
Parameters
N15
NFR-U-002 Must
Accessibility
The system meets WCAG 2.2 Level AA at first release . Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
The system meets WCAG 2.2 Level AA at first release TA-C40. Conformance evidence follows the clause tables of the harmonised ICT standard. Each component has accessibility acceptance criteria in the repository. Each release has an assistive-technology test matrix with manual test evidence. A published conformance ledger for each component covers cross-element ARIA association and the minimum browser version it relies on.
Accessibility Features
Keyboard operation for all functions
Screen reader compatibility, tested manually
Cross-element ARIA association checked across component boundaries
Accessible alternative formats for notices (FR-065)
Accessibility defects accepted as a valid reason for a breaking change
Testing
Automated checks in CI act as a gate but catch only about 30% of issues, so funded manual testing is also required.
Rationale
Provincial policy commits to WCAG AA. An ICT standard is expected, and evidence built this way can be re-filed rather than re-tested when it arrives (TA §C.5.7).
Parameters
N15
NFR-U-003 Must
Language and plain language
Client-facing content meets a published readability standard and is available in every language the ministry is obliged to use. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Client-facing content meets a published readability standard and is available in every language the ministry is obliged to use. The Chief Digital Officer, with legal counsel, confirms those obligations and the standard by the end of the foundation module.
Rationale
Plain language is a fairness control (TA §C.10.4).
Parameters
N15, N08
NFR-U-004 Must
Supported browsers and assistive technology
The list of supported browsers and assistive technologies is recorded before the first shared interface component is published. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
The list of supported browsers and assistive technologies is recorded before the first shared interface component is published. Each component records the minimum version its accessibility fixes rely on.
Rationale
That list decides whether the basic components can use shadow roots at all (TA §C.5.7).
Parameters
N15
NFR-U-005 Should
Consistent interface components, in tiers
Screens are built from a tiered component library, with rules enforced in CI. Show detail
Priority: SHOULD_HAVE ---
Requirement
Screens are built from a tiered component library, with rules enforced in CI. Presentational components are owned centrally and make no network calls. Connected components are owned by the domain that owns their contract. Accessibility-critical logic sits in the lower tiers. The provincial design system is used behind a facade.
Rationale
A component that carries both presentation and a data contract turns into an enterprise data dictionary by the back door (TA §C.5; decision D4).
Parameters
N03, N15
Maintainability and Supportability 7
NFR-M-001 Must
Tracing requests across the whole platform
One instrumentation standard covers components on and off the platform; Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
One instrumentation standard covers components on and off the platform; OpenTelemetry is the candidate. One correlation identifier travels through every hop: browser, experience back end, contract, layer, legacy, outbox, backbone, context, store and exchange. Naming conventions for domain concepts are owned alongside the published language.
Telemetry Requirements
Structured logs; RED metrics (rate, errors, duration); distributed tracing that can be joined across both telemetry systems; dashboards for SLOs, queues and reconciliation.
Rationale
Without this, "where did this determination's evidence come from" and "who was affected" have to be pieced together by hand (TA §C.17).
Parameters
N18, N06
NFR-M-002 Must
Service level objectives at the contract boundary
Each context publishes SLOs for its contract: Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Each context publishes SLOs for its contract: availability, p95 and p99 latency, and error rate. They are measured at the contract boundary, with error budgets derived from the tier availability figures.
Rationale
An SLO measured inside a service only describes the service. An SLO measured at the contract describes what the consumer gets (TA §C.17.1).
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED], N18
NFR-M-003 Must
Exception queues and reconciliation are monitored like everything else
The human reconciliation, adjudication and write-back exception queues publish their depth, the age of the oldest item, arrival and clearance rates, and SLA breaches. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
The human reconciliation, adjudication and write-back exception queues publish their depth, the age of the oldest item, arrival and clearance rates, and SLA breaches. Reconciliation and drift metrics also have a threshold and a named recipient. These cover event capture completeness, financial control totals across systems, drift sampling and the decommission burn-down.
Rationale
A reconciliation queue with no age metric is an unbounded backlog (TA §C.17.1).
Parameters
N18
NFR-M-004 Must
A breach of any architecture principle can be detected
For each of N01–N21, the detection mechanism is named. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
For each of N01–N21, the detection mechanism is named. Where it can be expressed as a lint rule, fitness function or schema-registry compatibility check, it runs as one in CI. Manual checks that could be automated are listed with the reason they are not.
Measurement Method
A detection register reviewed at each gate, read alongside the volume of findings.
Rationale
A control that nobody can see being broken is not a control (PRIN N18).
Parameters
N18
NFR-M-005 Must
One authoritative home for each rule
To understand how any business rule works, a person needs to look in one system. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
To understand how any business rule works, a person needs to look in one system. Any other copy of the rule is generated from that one, and the generation is shown.
Measurement Method
The N04 test applied to a sample of rules at each gate, including the five entitlement-deciding spreadsheets once they are acquired.
Rationale
Rules live in six places today (RULES §5). Logic spread across layers cannot be understood or changed with confidence.
Parameters
N04
NFR-M-006 Must
Operations, on-call and support
Tier-1 components (Open Host Service, layer, backbone, determination service, payment chokepoint) have 24×7 on-call cover. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Tier-1 components (Open Host Service, layer, backbone, determination service, payment chokepoint) have 24×7 on-call cover. Each rotation has at least six people, and escalation clocks are published. The team that builds a component stays on call until a handover gate: tested runbooks and three months of clean operation. Support runs through the ministry service desk and an application support tier. Staff reach engineering only through tier two. Runbooks cover deployment, rollback, restore, fallback modes and incident response.
Rationale
In every documented failure in the comparison record, the operations model was written during the incident (TA §E.8).
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED]
NFR-M-007 Must
Release calendar set by the financial calendar
Deployment blackout windows for payment services follow the corporate financial calendar. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Deployment blackout windows for payment services follow the corporate financial calendar. The child protection reporting line has its own change window and rollback rehearsal.
Rationale
The financial calendar governs the release calendar, and the programme cannot choose otherwise (TA §C.6.6).
Parameters
N17
Portability and Interoperability 7
NFR-I-001 Must
The contract outlasts whatever implements it
Published contracts use the words of policy and of the ministry's work, whatever product sits behind them. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Published contracts use the words of policy and of the ministry's work, whatever product sits behind them. No legacy row identifier, code list or term reaches a published endpoint. The anti-corruption layer is a private, temporary implementation set up to be retired.
Measurement Method
The excision test: remove the product and count the contract changes, with a target of zero. Also a demonstrated swap of the implementation with no change for any consumer.
Rationale
Once a partner stores one legacy identifier, the contract is tied to the platform it was meant to outlive (TA §A.7 risk 5; decision D1).
Parameters
N10
NFR-I-002 Must
Only evidence and determinations cross between contexts, and no model is shared
Contexts exchange only evidence and determinations. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Contexts exchange only evidence and determinations. They never exchange rows, table projections, internal identifiers or result sets. No context reads another's tables or depends on a type it does not own. A value type joins the shared published language only by a recorded decision.
Measurement Method
Payload inspection and dependency analysis in CI.
Rationale
A shared model tends to come back as a shared schema, not as a shared database (PRIN N03).
Parameters
N02, N03
NFR-I-003 Must
Schema compatibility and contract testing
Event and API schemas follow a published compatibility policy for each surface, enforced by the schema registry. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Event and API schemas follow a published compatibility policy for each surface, enforced by the schema registry. Consumer-driven contract tests run in CI. Versions, deprecations and retirement dates are published.
Rationale
Breaking replay of an old event is a data-loss incident (TA §B.5.4, §D.1).
Parameters
N10, N18
NFR-I-004 Must
Delivery rules and safe retries
Events are delivered at least once through a transactional outbox. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Events are delivered at least once through a transactional outbox. Every consumer is idempotent, so a repeated message has no extra effect. Ordering guarantees are stated for each stream.
Rationale
At-least-once delivery on a payment path is safe only if idempotency is designed in (TA §C.6.8).
Parameters
N06, N05
NFR-I-005 Must
Ministry-owned formats and portable records
Decision records, evidence and documents are held in formats the ministry owns. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Decision records, evidence and documents are held in formats the ministry owns. The ministry can export them without a vendor's tools, including a transfer package with its offline verifier.
Export Formats
Open, documented formats for each record class, with published schemas.
Rationale
Replay must still work after every component that produced the decision has been retired (PRIN N08).
Parameters
N08, N13
NFR-I-006 Must
Open standards, and buying what is generic
The system uses open standards throughout, and prefers open source for generic needs. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
The system uses open standards throughout, and prefers open source for generic needs. It buys, adopts or reuses workflow, notification, identity, secrets, policy evaluation, scheduling, document storage, search and print-and-mail. Any decision to build one of these must name the statutory, policy or program requirement that no commodity option meets. Someone other than the component's owner assesses the claim TA-C41. Each selection records the open alternative that was rejected.
Before procurement, custom build is evaluated against commercial and reusable case management platforms for the platform as a whole, and that evaluation is assessed independently.
Rationale
The platform-level build-or-buy question is the largest open question in the architecture, and leaving it open breaks the architecture's own rules PRIN-C9.
Parameters
N11
NFR-I-007 Should
API styles
REST for commands, resources and bulk operations. Show detail
Priority: SHOULD_HAVE ---
Requirement
REST for commands, resources and bulk operations. GraphQL for combined reads during transactions, with persisted operations mandatory. Access control, audit, versioning and idempotency are applied the same way at the Open Host Service.
Rationale
This is the recommendation of decision D2. Shared caching is not possible for responses about individual people (TA §C.1.4).
Parameters
N10, N02
DRAFT
A design proposal for the successor to British Columbia's integrated case management systems, covering employment assistance, disability assistance, child care subsidy, employment services and child protection.
Figures on this site are drawn from the architecture document and from 326 service-delivery procedures. Nothing here is a government commitment.

title: Trade-offs — The Future of Case Management IT
description: The eight conflicts between requirements, how each was resolved or who must resolve it, and the dependencies and risks the requirements carry.

Trade-offs 8
Trade-offs and open decisions
Some requirements pull against each other. These conflicts come from the sources themselves: policy against practice, one design parameter against another, a legal duty against a design property. Each one says what was chosen, what it costs, and who decides.
[aria-label] Conflict status
8 conflicts set out
6 resolved by the source hierarchy or the architecture
2 waiting on a ministry ruling
C-1 PRIORITIZE (policy), with INNOVATE (Option 3) Resolved
Policy against practice on the right to challenge
Decision: Option 3. Every request is recorded, and the pre-decision communication tells clients truthfully where they stand. Who decides: The source hierarchy settles the requirement. The ministry (ADM Policy and Program Design) is asked to correct the procedures (DEP-10).
Conflicting Requirements:
Requirement A: FR-055. A reconsideration request is always accepted and recorded, and the independent unit decides whether reconsideration is available (FR-056).
Requirement B: Current procedures. Staff are told "Do not offer the right to reconsideration" when food vouchers are denied RECON-C1; overpayment workers are told to answer a request with "there is nothing to reconsider"; and the brochure is held back when an overpayment is notified (RC-01, RC-14).
Stakeholders Involved:
Reconsideration and Administrative Fairness Unit and the policy authority: policy gives an unconditional right to ask.
Front-line service delivery: procedures were written to stop early or pointless requests and keep queues manageable.
Nature of Conflict:
A request cannot both be refused at the counter and recorded. In practice, the worker decides whether reconsideration is available, which they have no authority to do.
Trade-off Analysis:
Option
Pros
Cons
Impact
Option 1: Follow policy. Record every request and decide availability centrally
✅ Lawful<br>✅ Consistent across channels
❌ More requests reach the independent unit
Policy authority satisfied; the unit's workload rises
Option 2: Follow practice. Allow refusal at the point of contact
✅ Fewer requests
❌ Contradicts policy, which takes precedence<br>❌ Refusals nobody can review
Rejected by the source hierarchy
Option 3: Record every request, and use the pre-decision communication to tell clients that no decision has been made yet (FR-006)
✅ Lawful<br>✅ Fewer pointless requests, because clients know where they stand
❌ Needs the proposal object
Meets each side's underlying interest
Resolution Strategy: PRIORITIZE (policy), with INNOVATE (Option 3)
Decision: Option 3. Every request is recorded, and the pre-decision communication tells clients truthfully where they stand.
Rationale: Policy takes precedence over practice (BC-1). The ministry's own intake practice already uses the pre-decision pattern correctly (NOTE-001).
Decision Authority: The source hierarchy settles the requirement. The ministry (ADM Policy and Program Design) is asked to correct the procedures (DEP-10).
Impact on Requirements:
Added: FR-006 (pre-decision communication), FR-056 (availability decided by the independent unit).
Recorded: RC-01 and RC-14 as practice defects for the ministry to correct.
Stakeholder Management:
Front-line service delivery (bears the cost): the pre-decision communication gives workers a correct, scripted route. The independent unit's request volume is monitored.
Future Consideration:
After M7, measure request volume by channel and adjust staffing, not the right.
C-2 COMPROMISE Resolved
A history that is never changed against the duty to destroy records
Decision: Option 3 (TA §B.7; decision D13). Who decides: Ministry Records Officer with the Privacy Officer and the Chief Architect (D13), before the first production event.
Conflicting Requirements:
Requirement A: FR-008, DR-001. A permanent history that can be replayed, with nothing overwritten.
Requirement B: NFR-C-003, DR-004. Records destroyed on schedule, and one person's records destroyed where a duty or order requires it.
Stakeholders Involved:
Chief Architect: a tribunal examines whether decisions can be reproduced.
Records Officer and Privacy Officer: destroying records on schedule is a legal duty.
Nature of Conflict:
A store that never forgets cannot destroy anything, and a store that destroys records cannot replay everything.
Trade-off Analysis:
Option
Pros
Cons
Impact
Option 1: Encrypt everything per person and destroy keys
✅ Any one person's records can be destroyed
❌ The most expensive method for every fact<br>❌ The conflict between backing up keys and destroying them applies everywhere
Over-built
Option 2: Never destroy anything in the event store
✅ Full replay forever
❌ Breaks the records duty
Rejected
Option 3: A disposal method per fact class, a published shred-survivor list, typed placeholders for destroyed facts, and an advance statement of what can no longer be reproduced
✅ Meets each duty where it applies<br>✅ Cost in proportion
❌ Replay is limited for people whose records were destroyed, and this must be said in advance
Both duties met, with a stated limit
Resolution Strategy: COMPROMISE
Decision: Option 3 (TA §B.7; decision D13).
Rationale: The common duty is scheduled disposal of a whole class of records, not erasure on request. Designing the whole store around the rare case buys the wrong capability.
Decision Authority: Ministry Records Officer with the Privacy Officer and the Chief Architect (D13), before the first production event.
Impact on Requirements:
Modified: FR-008 carries the declared limit on replay; DR-004 requires the survivor list before the first event.
Stakeholder Management:
Chief Architect (loses unlimited replay): the limit is declared before the first disposal, not discovered at the first challenge.
Future Consideration:
Revisit the method for each fact class once the ARCS/ORCS schedules are obtained (DEP-09).
C-3 INNOVATE Open
Reaching every client against a verification check tied to how they are paid
Decision: Option 3, subject to a ministry ruling (DEP-10). Until then, clients can choose office pickup as a payment channel, but it is never used as the check. Who decides: ADM Policy and Program Design.
Conflicting Requirements:
Requirement A: FR-086, BR-009. Outcomes do not depend on channel, and electronic payment is available.
Requirement B: OB-SU-61. Hardship cheques are sent to the local office so that eligibility is re-checked every month.
Stakeholders Involved:
Head of Service Delivery Operations and clients: reach and dignity; clients should not have to visit an office every month to get paid.
Policy authority and compliance: hardship eligibility re-checked every month.
Nature of Conflict:
One mechanism meets two requirements. Paying electronically removes the monthly check PRIN-C8.
Trade-off Analysis:
Option
Pros
Cons
Impact
Option 1: Keep sending cheques to the office
✅ Check preserved
❌ Clients must travel to an office to be paid
Clients bear the cost
Option 2: Pay electronically and drop the check
✅ Better reach
❌ Removes a policy control
Compliance bears the risk
Option 3: Separate the two. A monthly re-check work item that applies whatever the channel (FR-040), with the client choosing how to be paid
✅ Both requirements met
❌ Needs a policy ruling on what counts as a re-check
Both met if policy agrees
Resolution Strategy: INNOVATE
Decision: Option 3, subject to a ministry ruling (DEP-10). Until then, clients can choose office pickup as a payment channel, but it is never used as the check.
Rationale: N15 has exposed two requirements met by one mechanism, which nobody saw until it was written down (PRIN N15).
Decision Authority: ADM Policy and Program Design.
Impact on Requirements:
Modified: FR-040 makes the monthly re-check a work item whatever the channel.
Stakeholder Management:
Compliance (loses the incidental check): a stated re-check that can be audited replaces an unstated one.
Future Consideration:
The same pattern may exist elsewhere. Phase D should look for controls that depend on a channel.
C-4 INNOVATE Resolved
Changing policy quickly against releasing rules that will stand up at tribunal
Decision: Option 3 (commitment 2; TA §C.4.3). Who decides: The Chief Architect and the ADM Policy and Program Design, jointly, as the authority that can relax commitment 2.
Conflicting Requirements:
Requirement A: BR-010. Policy staff release rate changes on their effective date without a software release.
Requirement B: FR-090, FR-091, FR-003. Release needs a second person's approval, legal sign-off, a regression test set, approval of decision classes, and no unresolved date conflicts.
Stakeholders Involved:
ADM Policy and Program Design: changes take effect on the date the minister sets.
Chief Architect and legal counsel: every release must stand up at tribunal.
Nature of Conflict:
Every check slows release. Removing checks makes releases harder to defend.
Trade-off Analysis:
Option
Pros
Cons
Impact
Option 1: Rules written in code and released with software
✅ Engineering controls
❌ Every rate change waits for a software release
Policy frustrated
Option 2: Analysts release rules freely
✅ Speed
❌ Releases that cannot be defended
Legal exposure
Option 3: An automated release pipeline. Simulation, regression and classification checks run automatically; people only review and give legal sign-off, and do so before the effective date
✅ Speed and defensibility
❌ The pipeline must be funded as a product
Both met
Resolution Strategy: INNOVATE
Decision: Option 3 (commitment 2; TA §C.4.3).
Rationale: Release and effect are separate. A rule released early takes effect on its stated date.
Decision Authority: The Chief Architect and the ADM Policy and Program Design, jointly, as the authority that can relax commitment 2.
Impact on Requirements:
Added: FR-091 blocks rules with date conflicts; DEP-14 tests analyst capability.
Stakeholder Management:
Policy (loses the ability to release alone): policy staff run the pipeline themselves, and the capability test proves they can before D3 is final.
Future Consideration:
If DEP-14 fails, improve the authoring tools rather than remove the checks.
C-5 COMPROMISE Resolved
Automated decisions at scale against the need for a human decision-maker
Decision: Option 3. Who decides: The statutory decision-maker for each program authorises each class (FR-093). The program policy authority approves the classification on legal advice.
Conflicting Requirements:
Requirement A: NFR-P-003, BR-004. Decisions and payments for the whole caseload, on time.
Requirement B: FR-003, FR-052, NFR-C-005. A human must decide any adverse decision based on inferred data, and every overpayment.
Stakeholders Involved:
Service delivery operations: volume and timeliness.
Statutory decision-makers and legal counsel: lawful administrative decisions.
Nature of Conflict:
Human review of every decision cannot keep up with the volume. Elsewhere, decisions with no human review have produced unlawful debt at scale.
Trade-off Analysis:
Option
Pros
Cons
Impact
Option 1: A person reviews every decision
✅ Safe
❌ Unworkable volume; late decisions change what clients are owed (FR-061)
Clients harmed by delay
Option 2: Automate everything
✅ Fast
❌ Unlawful for discretionary decisions and adverse decisions based on inference
Rejected
Option 3: Classify each output. Automate only verified administrative decisions with no discretion, under the four conditions in TA §D.5.2. A person decides anything involving discretion or inference, and every overpayment. A class is suspended automatically if challenges succeed too often
✅ Automates where lawful<br>✅ Safe where not
❌ Classification has to be governed
Both met, class by class
Resolution Strategy: COMPROMISE
Decision: Option 3.
Rationale: What the comparator jurisdiction lacked was a rule about which outputs count as decisions (TA §D.5).
Decision Authority: The statutory decision-maker for each program authorises each class (FR-093). The program policy authority approves the classification on legal advice.
Impact on Requirements:
Added: FR-093 register and suspension triggers.
Stakeholder Management:
Service delivery (loses full automation): volume by class is published every cycle, so the line between automated and human decisions is argued from evidence.
Future Consideration:
Review each class every year, and whenever challenges pass their trigger.
C-6 PHASE Open
Paying on time against verifying first
Decision: Option 3, pending a ministry ruling on which checks may be done after payment (DEP-10). Who decides: Program policy authority.
Conflicting Requirements:
Requirement A: NFR-A-008. No client's payment waits on another organisation's gateway. Decisions go ahead on the evidence held and are flagged for later checking.
Requirement B: FR-015. Mandatory third-party checks at application and review, unless a registered deferral applies.
Stakeholders Involved:
Clients and service delivery: payment on the due date.
Compliance and the policy authority: eligibility checked before assistance is paid.
Nature of Conflict:
When the exchange is down, the system must either pay without a mandatory check or hold the payment.
Trade-off Analysis:
Option
Pros
Cons
Impact
Option 1: Hold every decision until checks complete
✅ Checks preserved
❌ Payment depends on an outside gateway
Clients bear the outages
Option 2: Always go ahead and check later
✅ Payment on time
❌ Breaks the mandatory-check policy where no deferral applies
Compliance risk
Option 3: Go ahead only where a registered deferral applies or policy allows checking after payment; otherwise use emergency issuance under authority (FR-047) and reconcile later
✅ Lawful and on time
❌ Needs policy to state the deferral cases
Both met within policy
Resolution Strategy: PHASE
Decision: Option 3, pending a ministry ruling on which checks may be done after payment (DEP-10).
Rationale: For this failure, the architecture names the program policy authority as the one who decides whether to go ahead on the evidence held (TA §E.8.3).
Decision Authority: Program policy authority.
Impact on Requirements:
Modified: NFR-A-008 applies only to cases policy allows.
Stakeholder Management:
Compliance: every check done after payment is a tracked work item with its own deadline.
Future Consideration:
Revisit once the exchange commits to an availability target (DEP-06).
C-7 COMPROMISE Resolved
Keeping old reports and interfaces working against the detail the new record holds
Decision: Option 3 (TA §C.2.6; DR-014, DR-015). Who decides: The Policy Directors accept the published losses for each part of the system and each group of clients; the Coexistence Lead owns the mechanism.
Conflicting Requirements:
Requirement A: DR-014. Write changes back to the old system for groups of clients the new system has taken over, so old reports, batch jobs and interfaces not yet moved keep working.
Requirement B: DR-001, DR-002. The new record holds dates, lifecycle and source detail the old system's structure cannot hold.
Stakeholders Involved:
Users of the old systems and operations staff: things keep working while both systems run.
Program policy authority: accountable for what a rollback loses.
Nature of Conflict:
Writing back always loses detail, so every day in state S2 is a day on an incomplete copy.
Trade-off Analysis:
Option
Pros
Cons
Impact
Option 1: No write-back; move every user of the old data in one cutover
✅ No loss
❌ The single-cutover risk the evidence from other jurisdictions rules out
Rejected
Option 2: Write back indefinitely
✅ Old systems keep working
❌ Running both systems becomes permanent
How the predecessor programme failed
Option 3: Write back for a limited time and with limited detail. The losses are published and accepted per fact class, and a retirement date is set when each group moves
✅ Old systems keep working, at a stated cost and with an end date
❌ Named losses must be accepted
Both met, with a stated limit
Resolution Strategy: COMPROMISE
Decision: Option 3 (TA §C.2.6; DR-014, DR-015).
Rationale: Claiming a move can be reversed without saying what is lost means the cost has not been worked out.
Decision Authority: The Policy Directors accept the published losses for each part of the system and each group of clients; the Coexistence Lead owns the mechanism.
Impact on Requirements:
Added: DR-015's published list of losses, including the difference between a correction and a supersession.
Stakeholder Management:
Program policy authority (accepts named losses): acceptance is explicit, for each group of clients, before state S2.
Future Consideration:
Retire each user of the old data as parts of the system reach state S3.
C-8 PHASE Resolved
Building the ministry-specific parts against buying a platform
Decision: Option 3 (DEP-19). This document does not assume a particular solution, so it can serve as the baseline for that evaluation (A-7). Who decides: ED Digital Services with the ADM Policy and Program Design (D3), assessed by someone other than the owners of the parts.
Conflicting Requirements:
Requirement A: NFR-I-006. Buy generic capability, have any decision to build assessed independently, and evaluate the whole platform against commercial and reusable case management platforms.
Requirement B: The architecture's list of parts to build (the evidence store, the decision machinery, case handling, the translation layer, the exchange's authorization and evidence services, overpayment, appeals, and identity matching) (TA §C.18.1).
Stakeholders Involved:
ED Digital Services and ADM Policy and Program Design: own D3 and the rules platform.
Chief Architect: owns the reasons for each part to be built.
Nature of Conflict:
The architecture has not applied its own build-or-buy test to the platform as a whole, and three of its eight build decisions fail that test (PRIN N11).
Trade-off Analysis:
Option
Pros
Cons
Impact
Option 1: Build the list as written
✅ Keeps the architecture as it is
❌ Fails the architecture's own rule
The largest open question stays open
Option 2: Buy a commercial case management platform
✅ Off-the-shelf capability
❌ Not assessed against the legal requirements here (replay, three-date evidence, deadlines)
Unknown fit
Option 3: Evaluate the whole platform against these requirements, assessed independently, before procurement
✅ Decision based on evidence
❌ Takes time before procurement
Decision waits for evidence
Resolution Strategy: PHASE
Decision: Option 3 (DEP-19). This document does not assume a particular solution, so it can serve as the baseline for that evaluation (A-7).
Rationale: By the architecture's own rules, leaving this unanswered is a compliance failure PRIN-C9.
Decision Authority: ED Digital Services with the ADM Policy and Program Design (D3), assessed by someone other than the owners of the parts.
Impact on Requirements:
Unchanged: requirements are stated as outcomes, and the architecture commitments that apply are named as such.
Stakeholder Management:
Chief Architect (build list open to challenge): each build decision keeps its requirement-based reason, which is tested rather than thrown out.
Future Consideration:
Record the result in an ADR, and amend this document where the result changes a requirement.

A boundary that lives only in a diagram will not survive delivery pressure. These four are written so a reviewer can point at something and say whether it complies.
A child protection investigation and a child care subsidy renewal share almost nothing. A shared model turns every change into a negotiation. The last programme cut scope rather than reopen one.

A database table
A decision records the moment its facts were read
A decision that reads anything not stored with it cannot be re-run. Re-running is what lets you show a tribunal what happened, rather than piece it together from memory.
A decision you can re-run
A design proposal for the successor to British Columbia's integrated case management systems, covering employment assistance, disability assistance, child care subsidy, employment services and child protection.
A design proposal for the successor to British Columbia's integrated case management systems, explained in plain English.
A document is not evidence.
A document is what a verification policy accepts as satisfying an evidence type. Losing that distinction turns the file store into a second system of record.
A fact carries a note of where it came from. A database row doesn’t. The part that receives a bare row can’t tell who said it, so it can’t know what it is safe to conclude. And if the source later fixes the value, there is nothing to attach the fix to.
A first assertion about a period nothing covered yet.
A limit missing when information is first collected is missing from every copy made before it was added
A link to a system that is still running is not proof. You have to be able to replay a decision long after the systems that made it are gone, the rules engine included. The client also has a right to the record itself, gathered together, with protected details removed as FOIPPA requires. Being able to replay a decision doesn’t give them that.
A modernisation has to know what it is replacing. The rules that decide entitlement sit in four separate places, and only one of them is a rules engine.
A parameter is something a system must comply with. A parameter must be check-able; it must be possible to check whether the system complies to it. To make sure that these rules are parameters, every entry below ends in a question you can put to a running system and get a wrong answer to.
A part that needs another's data keeps its own copy, built from that part's events and shaped the way it needs. When the source corrects something, the copy has to follow.
A partner moves in on 1 May, and the client reports it.
A person can get the same result whatever their disability and whichever way they contact the ministry. Screens and forms meet the Province’s accessibility standard from the first release. And every service has a supported way to use it that isn’t online.
A pointer resolves to whatever the database says today. Replay returns today’s answer to a four-year-old question.
A published interface for reads, and published events for notices. There is no third way, and adding one is not a shortcut.
A review establishes the household was a couple from January, not a single person.
A rule nobody can check is not a rule
A rules engine
A store built without a plan for destroying records can’t get one later
A system that stores only the current state, "Income: $900", leaves the important questions open. How do we know? What evidence is there? When did we know? Is this the corrected number, or the number we recorded at the time?
A team accountable for a thing will grow and protect it. A team measured on its own dissolution will not.
A tribunal asks equally what the client was told.
A tribunal asks two questions: what was true, and what did the ministry know. Each needs its own axis. The third axis exists because fifteen years of records arrive from a system still in use. Flatten their history into the migration date and a whole class of question stops having an answer.
A tribunal asks what the person was told as often as it asks what the system worked out. A decision that re-runs perfectly, next to a letter nobody can rebuild, still misses the question.
Access for everyone
Accommodation and the signature problem
Accounts, accruals, schedules, double-entry postings.
Added since the source
All twenty-one
An Excel workbook decides which queue a request joins, how urgent it is, how long it has, and where a scanned document goes. Fifty-six procedures point at it. One of its sheets maps 445 form numbers to their handling. So the priorities and service-level targets for the whole service sit outside the platform, kept up by hand.
An engine upgrade can change how the same rules evaluate.
An entitlement determined twice must not be paid twice, and that guarantee lives here rather than in five case contexts.
And together they carry what the architecture is trying to do.
Any group of clients moved to the new system can be moved back to the old one without a separate data project. An approved statement says what information would be lost on the way back. Being able to undo a move means both having a way to do it and knowing how much survives.
Appeals & Reconsideration
Apt boundaries
Archiving the software tells you what it was. It does not promise that anything in twenty years can still run it. The operating system, the processor and the container runtime all die younger than a child protection record, which the ministry keeps for ninety years.
As the first copy is made
Ask a typical case management system why a person got a particular amount in March 2022 and it will work the sum again. It uses today's rules, today's data and today's software, then reports the answer with confidence. The answer may well be right. Nobody can tell, and nobody can show a tribunal the difference.
Ask about
Asked in
At application in March, no disability designation is in place.
At application, the client declares they live alone.
Back to the
Backdated recalculation runs off valid time, which any competent migration preserves, so recalculation survives. Something narrower breaks without the third axis: what the ministry knew and when. That is the question separating a recoverable debt from the ministry's own error.
Before the first event is written
Before the first group of clients moves
Before the first real event, has someone chosen how each kind of fact will be destroyed, and published what survives?
Before the first rule is written
Before the system stores anything, decide how each kind of fact will be destroyed when its time comes. There are three ways: delete a whole kind of record on a set schedule, keep personal details in a separate place that can be deleted, or lock one person’s records with a key and then destroy the key. Publish what is left after a record is destroyed. Plan who holds the keys. And say what a replay does when it reaches a record it can no longer read.
Benefit calculation, rate recalculation, time limits, sanction end dates
Beyond 20 years
Boundaries between parts
Boundary test
Business requirements
Business requirements — The Future of Case Management IT
Business rules by location
Buy common tools, and have someone else check any choice to build
Can only partly be added later
Can this group go back to the old system today, without a data project? Can you name every kind of fact that wouldn’t survive the trip? The old system has no way to tell a correction from a later update. If that isn’t on the list, the list isn’t complete.
Can you replay a decision made three years ago using only what is stored, with no systems running? Can you put together the appeal record, and remove the protected details, whenever someone asks?
Cannot be added later
Capture, attachment lifecycle, extraction, e-signature, and the link between a document and the claim it supports.

Copies and corrections
Copies are owned by whoever holds them
Correct a fact at its source. Can you list every part that holds a copy? Does each one have to act on the correction? And does something raise an alarm if a correction goes unread?
Could a reviewer tell from the interface’s definition which product is behind it? Now take the product away. How many changes does the interface need?
Counted by naming every system referenced in each procedure. The most common pairing is the Siebel case system with the client portal, then the case system with Service Canada, then the case system with the mainframe.

Documents & Capture
Documents and capture
Does any part read another part’s tables, or rely on a data type another part owns? The second question matters more. A shared model rarely comes back as a shared database. It comes back as a shared layout that everyone copies.
Does not own
Does the design name the point each decision read up to (the watermark), write it into the decision record, and set a limit on how far behind a store can be? If a store is past that limit, does the decision stop instead of going ahead?
Does the system hold each limit once, with who owns it, what kind it is, what starts it, how long it runs, and its extensions and approvals? Does a missed deadline show up without a person having to spot it? Does its consequence apply automatically?
Domains — The Future of Case Management IT
Each benefit records whether and how a decision can be challenged
Each category has its own page. Every requirement opens to show its description, the checks that prove it is met, and the reasons it exists.
Each decision stores which version of the rules was used and which version of the facts. It stores full copies of them, not links to them. It also records what the client asked for, which requirements they met and which they didn’t, what the ministry assumed, what evidence was missing, and the date the client was told.
Each entry below demonstrates the first two claims. The third rests on an argument against a list of intents, and it is the weakest of the three, because another architect could reasonably draw some of these lines elsewhere.
Each object belongs to one part of the system. They are not a shared model that every part must use; each part keeps its own view of what it needs.
Each one carries a header naming its purpose, the policy it carries out, the law behind it, and how the system classifies the work. That turns the whole set into a map of the services.
Each one lists the policy obligations it meets and the design parameters that test it, and links to them.
Each parameter says how you would find out it has been broken. Where software could do that check automatically, it has to be built as an automated check.
Each part can be released on its own
Each part keeps its own picture of the data
Each part of the system keeps its own description of a person, a case or a payment. There is no single shared “Person” record that every part must use. No part shares a database layout with another, reads another part’s tables, or relies on a data type that another part defines.
Each service has recovery targets, proven in practice runs
Eligibility & Entitlement
Employment and disability assistance
Employment assistance
Employment services
Every copy can be traced, and every correction reaches it
Every dated claim about the world, and how it was checked.
Every entitlement decision stores the rules, the engine, the facts it saw, its own reasoning and what it decided. A manager four days later, or a tribunal years later, can re-run it instead of piecing it together from memory.
Every evidence assertion carries three time dimensions:
Every evidence type needs a records ruling before anyone can use it, which puts the records office on the critical path.
Every fact is dated and has a source
Every move can be undone, and what is lost is written down
Every outside system it must exchange information with, and on what terms.
Every outside system the new system must exchange information with: what flows each way, how it is protected, and what happens when it fails.
Every parameter is necessary: take one away and the design loses something nothing else supplies.
Every principle in the architecture is accounted for. Seven carried across, with their wording narrowed or widened. Three split, because each held two ideas that could stand apart. One took in a clause from another, and one became more general. So twelve principles turned into fourteen parameters, and seven more joined them.
Every read gets harder. Developers have to think in periods rather than values, and every report has to say which point in time it means.
Every record has one system in charge of it: its system of record. That holds for each group of clients, and it still holds while clients move from the old system to the new one. The two systems never both make changes and sort out the differences afterwards. And where the data affects what a person receives, no automatic process decides which version wins.
Every recurring task a caseworker does has a written procedure: what starts it, which screens to open, which form to send, what to type in which field. Together they run to 8.2 million characters. They describe the service as staff really deliver it.
Every requirement carries acceptance criteria written as "given, when, then", so a tester can say whether it passes.
Every rule carries a label saying what kind of decision it produces. Some produce an administrative decision, which needs reasons. Some produce a decision a person has to make before it takes effect. The rest are working sums that affect nobody on their own.
Every rule comes with a way to catch it being broken
Every service has a target for how much of the time it must be working, and limits on how long it can be down and how much recent data it can lose. These targets depend on how much harm an outage does to a client. A practice run has to show the targets can be met. Anything shared by several services must meet the strictest target of any of them.
